6.10.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti pratipadaṃ kuryād yeṣāṃ dīkṣitānāṃ pramīyate
6.10.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवस इति प्रतिपदं कुर्याद् येषां दीक्षितानां प्रमीयते
6.10.m: He should make 'O Agni, clarify lifespans' the introductory verse for those among consecrated persons one of whom dies.

6.10.s: apūtā iva vā ete yeṣāṃ dīkṣitānāṃ pramīyate yady eṣāgnipāvamānī pratipad bhavaty agnir evainān niṣṭapati pavamānaḥ punāti
6.10.d: अपूता इव वा एते येषां दीक्षितानां प्रमीयते यद्य् एषाग्निपावमानी प्रतिपद् भवत्य् अग्निर् एवैनान् निष्टपति पवमानः पुनाति
6.10.m: Unpurified indeed are they among consecrated persons one of whom dies. If this introductory verse addressed to Agni Pavamāna is used, Agni consumes [their impurity] and Pavamāna purifies them.

6.10.s: yad āyūṃṣīty āha ya eva jīvanti teṣv āyur dadhāti
6.10.d: यद् आयूंषीत्य् आह य एव जीवन्ति तेष्व् आयुर् दधाति
6.10.m: When he says, 'lifespans', he bestows lifespan upon those who live.

6.10.s: ā no mitrāvaruṇeti jyogāmayāvine pratipadaṃ kuryāt
6.10.d: आ नो मित्रावरुणेति ज्योगामयाविने प्रतिपदं कुर्यात्
6.10.m: He should make 'Hither to us, Mitra and Varuṇa' the introductory verse for one who is chronically ill.

6.10.s: apakrāntau vā etasya prāṇāpānau yasya jyog āmayati prāṇāpānau mitrāvaruṇau prāṇāpānāv evāsmin dadhāti
6.10.d: अपक्रान्तौ वा एतस्य प्राणापानौ यस्य ज्योग् आमयति प्राणापानौ मित्रावरुणौ प्राणापानाव् एवास्मिन् दधाति
6.10.m: Inhalation and exhalation have departed from him who is chronically ill. Mitra and Varuṇa are inhalation and exhalation; he bestows inhalation and exhalation upon him.

6.10.s: apaghnan pavate mṛdho 'pa somo arāvṇa ity anṛtam abhiśasyamānāya pratipadaṃ kuryāt
6.10.d: अपघ्नन् पवते मृधो ऽप सोमो अराव्ण इत्य् अनृतम् अभिशस्यमानाय प्रतिपदं कुर्यात्
6.10.m: He should make 'Striking away the foes, the stingy ones, Soma clarifies himself' the introductory verse for one falsely accused.

6.10.s: arāvāṇo vā ete ye 'nṛtam abhiśaṃsanti tān evāsmād apahanti
6.10.d: अरावाणो वा एते ये ऽनृतम् अभिशंसन्ति तान् एवास्माद् अपहन्ति
6.10.m: Stingy are they who make false accusations; he strikes them away from him.

6.10.s: gacchann indrasya niṣkṛtam iti pūtam evainaṃ yajñiyam indrasya niṣkṛtaṃ gamayati
6.10.d: गच्छन्न् इन्द्रस्य निष्कृतम् इति पूतम् एवैनं यज्ञियम् इन्द्रस्य निष्कृतं गमयति
6.10.m: With 'going to Indra's appointed place', he causes him, purified and worthy of sacrifice, to reach Indra's appointed place.

6.10.s: vṛṣā pavasva dhārayeti rājanyāya pratipadaṃ kuryād vṛṣā vai rājanyo vṛṣāṇam evainaṃ karoti
6.10.d: वृषा पवस्व धारयेति राजन्याय प्रतिपदं कुर्याद् वृषा वै राजन्यो वृषाणम् एवैनं करोति
6.10.m: He should make 'As a bull, clarify yourself with a stream' the introductory verse for a nobleman; the nobleman is a bull; he makes him a bull.

6.10.s: marutvate ca matsara iti maruto vai devānāṃ viśo viśam evāsmā anu niyunakty anapakrāmukāsmād viḍ bhavati
6.10.d: मरुत्वते च मत्सर इति मरुतो वै देवानां विशो विशम् एवास्मा अनु नियुनक्त्य् अनपक्रामुकास्माद् विड् भवति
6.10.m: With 'and exhilarating for the one accompanied by the Maruts', the Maruts are the common people of the gods; he attaches the common people to him; the common people do not depart from him.

6.10.s: viśvā dadhāna ojasety ojasaivāsmai vīryeṇa viśaṃ purastāt parigṛhṇāty anapakrāmukāsmād viḍ bhavati
6.10.d: विश्वा दधान ओजसेत्य् ओजसैवास्मै वीर्येण विशं पुरस्तात् परिगृह्णात्य् अनपक्रामुकास्माद् विड् भवति
6.10.m: With 'holding all vigour', he grasps the common people in front of him with vigour and virility; the common people do not depart from him.

6.10.s: pavasvendo vṛṣāsuta iti pratipadaṃ kuryād yaḥ kāmayeta jane ma ṛdhyeteti
6.10.d: पवस्वेन्दो वृषासुत इति प्रतिपदं कुर्याद् यः कामयेत जने म ऋध्येतेति
6.10.m: He should make 'Clarify yourself, O drop, pressed out as a bull' the introductory verse for one who desires: 'May it prosper for me among the people.'

6.10.s: kṛdhī no yaśaso jana iti janatāyām evāsmā ṛdhyate
6.10.d: कृधी नो यशसो जन इति जनतायाम् एवास्मा ऋध्यते
6.10.m: With 'Make us famous among the people', it prospers for him among the people.

6.10.s: yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svaḥ patī iti dvābhyāṃ pratipadaṃ kuryāt samāvadbhājāv evainau yajñasya karoty ubhau yajñayaśasenārpayati
6.10.d: युवं हि स्थः स्वः पती इति द्वाभ्यां प्रतिपदं कुर्यात् समावद्भाजाव् एवैनौ यज्ञस्य करोत्य् उभौ यज्ञयशसेनार्पयति
6.10.m: He should make 'For you two are lords of heaven' the introductory verse for two; he makes the two of them equal sharers of the sacrifice; he endows both with the fame of the sacrifice.

6.10.s: prāsya dhārā akṣarann iti vṛṣṭikāmāya pratipadaṃ kuryāt
6.10.d: प्रास्य धारा अक्षरन्न् इति वृष्टिकामाय प्रतिपदं कुर्यात्
6.10.m: He should make 'Forth flowed his streams' the introductory verse for one who desires rain.

6.10.s: prāsya dhārā akṣarann iti divo vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvayati vṛṣṇaḥ sutasyaujasa ity antarikṣāt
6.10.d: प्रास्य धारा अक्षरन्न् इति दिवो वृष्टिं च्यावयति वृष्णः सुतस्यौजस इत्य् अन्तरिक्षात्
6.10.m: With 'Forth flowed his streams', he brings down rain from the sky; with 'by the vigour of the pressed bull', from the intermediate space.

6.10.s: devāṃ anu prabhūṣata ity asmin loke pratiṣṭhāpayati
6.10.d: देवां अनु प्रभूषत इत्य् अस्मिन् लोके प्रतिष्ठापयति
6.10.m: With 'serving the gods', he establishes it in this world.

6.10.s: ojasā vā etad vīryeṇa pradīyate yad aprattaṃ bhavati yad vṛṣṇaḥ sutasyaujasa ity āhaujasaivāsmai vīryeṇa divo vṛṣṭiṃ prayacchati
6.10.d: ओजसा वा एतद् वीर्येण प्रदीयते यद् अप्रत्तं भवति यद् वृष्णः सुतस्यौजस इत्य् आहौजसैवास्मै वीर्येण दिवो वृष्टिं प्रयच्छति
6.10.m: That which is not given is given forth with vigour and virility. When he says, 'by the vigour of the pressed bull', he gives him rain from the sky with vigour and virility.

6.10.s: tayā pavasva dhārayā yayā gāva ihāgamañ janyāsa up no gṛham iti pratipadaṃ kuryād yaḥ kāmayetopa mā janyā gāvo nameyur vindeta me janyā gā rāṣṭram iti yad eṣā pratipad bhavaty upainaṃ janyā gāvo namanti vindate 'sya janyā gā rāṣṭram
6.10.d: तया पवस्व धारया यया गाव इहागमञ् जन्यास उप् नो गृहम् इति प्रतिपदं कुर्याद् यः कामयेतोप मा जन्या गावो नमेयुर् विन्देत मे जन्या गा राष्ट्रम् इति यद् एषा प्रतिपद् भवत्य् उपैनं जन्या गावो नमन्ति विन्दते ऽस्य जन्या गा राष्ट्रम्
6.10.m: He should make 'With that stream clarify yourself, by which foreign cattle may come here to our home' the introductory verse for one who desires: 'May foreign cattle incline toward me; may the kingdom win foreign cattle for me.' When this is the introductory verse, foreign cattle incline toward him; his kingdom wins foreign cattle.

7.1.s: ime vai lokā gāyatraṃ tryāvṛd geyaṃ trayo hīme lokā yat tryāvṛd gāyaty ebhir evainaṃ lokaiḥ saṃmimīte
7.1.d: इमे वै लोका गायत्रं त्र्यावृद् गेयं त्रयो हीमे लोका यत् त्र्यावृद् गायत्य् एभिर् एवैनं लोकैः संमिमीते
7.1.m: These worlds are the Gāyatra; it should be sung thrice-repeated, for these worlds are three. When he sings it thrice-repeated, he measures it out in accordance with these worlds.
Twice he should roar; the third time he should sound hiṅ.

7.1.s: yat trir avanardaty ati tad gāyatraṃ recayati
7.1.d: यत् त्रिर् अवनर्दत्य् अति तद् गायत्रं रेचयति
7.1.m: When he roars three times, he causes the Gāyatra to spill over.

7.1.s: yo vai gāyatreṇāpratihṛtenodgāyaty apratiṣṭhāno bhavati hiṅkāro vai gāyatrasya pratihāraḥ
7.1.d: यो वै गायत्रेणाप्रतिहृतेनोद्गायत्य् अप्रतिष्ठानो भवति हिङ्कारो वै गायत्रस्य प्रतिहारः
7.1.m: He who sings the udgītha with a Gāyatra lacking a pratihāra becomes without a firm support. The hiṅkāra is the pratihāra of the Gāyatra.

7.1.s: sa manasā dhyeyaḥ pratihṛtena gāyatreṇodgāyati pratitiṣṭhati
7.1.d: स मनसा ध्येयः प्रतिहृतेन गायत्रेणोद्गायति प्रतितिष्ठति
7.1.m: It should be meditated upon in the mind; he sings the udgītha with a Gāyatra provided with a pratihāra; he gains a firm support.

7.1.s: yo vā ebhyo lokebhyo gāyatraṃ gāyati naibhyo lokebhya āvṛścyata ima enaṃ lokā ūrjjābhisaṃvasate
7.1.d: यो वा एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो गायत्रं गायति नैभ्यो लोकेभ्य आवृश्च्यत इम एनं लोका ऊर्ज्जाभिसंवसते
7.1.m: He who sings the Gāyatra for these worlds is not torn away from these worlds; these worlds dwell together with him with nourishment.

7.1.s: mandram ivāgra ādadītātha tārataram atha tāratamaṃ tad ebhyo lokebhyo 'gāsīt
7.1.d: मन्द्रम् इवाग्र आददीताथ तारतरम् अथ तारतमं तद् एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽगासीत्
7.1.m: He should begin in a low tone as it were, then louder, then loudest; in that way he has sung for these worlds.

7.1.s: aniruktaṃ geyam etad vai gāyatrasya krūraṃ yan niruktaṃ yad aniruktaṃ gāyati krūram evāsya parivṛṇakti
7.1.d: अनिरुक्तं गेयम् एतद् वै गायत्रस्य क्रूरं यन् निरुक्तं यद् अनिरुक्तं गायति क्रूरम् एवास्य परिवृणक्ति
7.1.m: It should be sung undefined. Cruel indeed is that of the Gāyatra which is defined. When he sings it undefined, he avoids its cruel [aspect].

7.1.s: prāṇo gāyatraṃ na vyavānyāt prāṇasyāvicchedāya yadi vyavāniti pramāyuko bhavati yadi na vyavāniti sarvam āyur eti
7.1.d: प्राणो गायत्रं न व्यवान्यात् प्राणस्याविच्छेदाय यदि व्यवानिति प्रमायुको भवति यदि न व्यवानिति सर्वम् आयुर् एति
7.1.m: The Gāyatra is breath; he should not inhale, so as not to interrupt the breath. If he inhales, he is liable to die; if he does not inhale, he attains a full lifespan.

7.1.s: yadi vyavānyān madhya ṛco vyavānyāt prāṇo vai gāyatraṃ prāṇaḥ svaraḥ prāṇam eva tan madhyata ātman dadhāti sa sarvam āyur eti
7.1.d: यदि व्यवान्यान् मध्य ऋचो व्यवान्यात् प्राणो वै गायत्रं प्राणः स्वरः प्राणम् एव तन् मध्यत आत्मन् दधाति स सर्वम् आयुर् एति
7.1.m: If he should inhale, he should inhale in the middle of a verse. The Gāyatra is breath, breath is tone; he thus places breath in the middle of himself; he attains a full lifespan.

7.1.s: iḍāṃ paśukāmāya nidhanaṃ kuryāt svaḥ svargakāmāya yaśo brahmavarcasakāmāyāyur āmayāvine haṃsīty abhicarate
7.1.d: इडां पशुकामाय निधनं कुर्यात् स्वः स्वर्गकामाय यशो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामायायुर् आमयाविने हंसीत्य् अभिचरते
7.1.m: One should make ‘iḍā’ the cadence for one who is desirous of cattle; ‘svaḥ’ for one who is desirous of heaven; ‘yaśaḥ’ for one who is desirous of brahminical lustre; ‘āyuḥ’ for one who is sick; ‘haṁsi’ for one who is performing sorcery.
These are indeed the milkings of the Gāyatra [sāman].

7.1.s: brahmavarcasasī paśumān bhavati ya evaṃv veda
7.1.d: ब्रह्मवर्चससी पशुमान् भवति य एवंव् वेद
7.1.m: Possessed of brahminical lustre, possessed of cattle does he become who knows thus.

7.2.s: prajāpatir devebhya ātmānaṃ yajñaṃ kṛtvā prāyacchat te 'nyo 'nyasmā agrāya nātiṣṭhanta tān abravīd ājim asminn iteti ta ājim āyan yad ājim āyaṃs tad ājyānām ājyatvam
7.2.d: प्रजापतिर् देवेभ्य आत्मानं यज्ञं कृत्वा प्रायच्छत् ते ऽन्यो ऽन्यस्मा अग्राय नातिष्ठन्त तान् अब्रवीद् आजिम् अस्मिन्न् इतेति त आजिम् आयन् यद् आजिम् आयंस् तद् आज्यानाम् आज्यत्वम्
7.2.m: Prajāpati, having made himself into the sacrifice, gave it to the gods. They did not yield to one another for the first [share]. He said to them, 'Run a race for this.' They ran a race. Because they ran a race (ājim āyan), that is the reason why the ājyastotras are called ājyastotras (ājyānām ājyatvam).

7.2.s: sa indro 'ved agnir vā idam agra ujjyeṣyatīti so 'bravīd yataro nāv idam agra ujjayat tan nau saheti so 'gnir agra udajayad atha mitrāvaruṇāv athendro 'thaiṣaikā hotrānujjitāsīt sa indro 'gnim abravīd yat sahāvocāvahī yan nau tad iti saiṣaindrāgny adhyardham agne stotram adhyardham indrasya
7.2.d: स इन्द्रो ऽवेद् अग्निर् वा इदम् अग्र उज्ज्येष्यतीति सो ऽब्रवीद् यतरो नाव् इदम् अग्र उज्जयत् तन् नौ सहेति सो ऽग्निर् अग्र उदजयद् अथ मित्रावरुणाव् अथेन्द्रो ऽथैषैका होत्रानुज्जितासीत् स इन्द्रो ऽग्निम् अब्रवीद् यत् सहावोचावही यन् नौ तद् इति सैषैन्द्राग्न्य् अध्यर्धम् अग्ने स्तोत्रम् अध्यर्धम् इन्द्रस्य
7.2.m: Indra knew, 'Agni will win this first.' He said, 'Whichever of us two wins this first, that shall belong to both of us together.' Agni won first; then Mitra and Varuṇa; then Indra; then this single Hotṛ's [office] was won. Indra said to Agni, 'What we two agreed together, that is ours.' That is this [chant] sacred to Indra and Agni: half belongs to Agni, half to Indra.
There are four [stotras], addressed to six deities.

7.2.s: ṣaḍdhā vihito yajño yāvān yajñas tam evārabhate
7.2.d: षड्धा विहितो यज्ञो यावान् यज्ञस् तम् एवारभते
7.2.m: The sacrifice is arranged sixfold; as great as the sacrifice is, upon that he enters.

7.2.s: sarvāṇi svārāṇy ājyāni taj jāmi nānādevatyaiḥ stuvanty ajāmitāyai
7.2.d: सर्वाणि स्वाराण्य् आज्यानि तज् जामि नानादेवत्यैः स्तुवन्त्य् अजामितायै
7.2.m: All the ājyastotras end in a tone; that is a tautology. They chant to different deities for the sake of variation.

7.2.s: grāmyebhyo vā etat paśubhyaḥ stuvanti yad ājyaiḥ punarabhyāvartaṃ stuvanti tasmāt parāñcaḥ prājyante pratyañcaḥ prajāyante tasmād u pretya punar āyanti
7.2.d: ग्राम्येभ्यो वा एतत् पशुभ्यः स्तुवन्ति यद् आज्यैः पुनरभ्यावर्तं स्तुवन्ति तस्मात् पराञ्चः प्राज्यन्ते प्रत्यञ्चः प्रजायन्ते तस्माद् उ प्रेत्य पुनर् आयन्ति
7.2.m: It is for domestic cattle that they praise when they chant the ājyastotras with repeated returns. Therefore, [cattle] are driven away facing backwards, and are born facing forwards; and therefore, having gone forth, they come back again.

7.3.s: etāvatā vāva mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ pupuve
7.3.d: एतावता वाव माध्यन्दिनं सवनं पुपुवे
7.3.m: By just so much was the midday pressing purified:

7.3.s: tribhiś ca cchandobhiḥ pañcabhiś ca sāmabhiḥ
7.3.d: त्रिभिश् च च्छन्दोभिः पञ्चभिश् च सामभिः
7.3.m: by three metres and by five sāmans.

7.3.s: yan mādhyandinena pavamānena stuvanti mādhyandinam eva tat savanaṃ pāvayanti
7.3.d: यन् माध्यन्दिनेन पवमानेन स्तुवन्ति माध्यन्दिनम् एव तत् सवनं पावयन्ति
7.3.m: When they chant with the midday pavamāna, they purify the midday pressing itself.

7.3.s: etāvanti vāva sarvāṇi sāmāni yāvanti mādhyandine pavamāne
7.3.d: एतावन्ति वाव सर्वाणि सामानि यावन्ति माध्यन्दिने पवमाने
7.3.m: All sāmans are just as many as are in the midday pavamāna:

7.3.s: gāyatraṃ nidhanavad anidhanam aiḍam
7.3.d: गायत्रं निधनवद् अनिधनम् ऐडम्
7.3.m: the Gāyatra, having a cadence, lacking a cadence, having an iḍā [cadence].

7.3.s: yan mādhyandinena pavamānena stuvanti sarvair eva tat sāmabhiḥ stuvanti
7.3.d: यन् माध्यन्दिनेन पवमानेन स्तुवन्ति सर्वैर् एव तत् सामभिः स्तुवन्ति
7.3.m: When they chant with the midday pavamāna, they chant with all sāmans.

7.3.s: ātmā vai yajñasya pavamāno mukhaṃ gāyatrī prāṇo gāyatraṃ yad gāyatryāṃ gāyatreṇa stuvanti mukhata eva tat prāṇān dadhati
7.3.d: आत्मा वै यज्ञस्य पवमानो मुखं गायत्री प्राणो गायत्रं यद् गायत्र्यां गायत्रेण स्तुवन्ति मुखत एव तत् प्राणान् दधति
7.3.m: The Pavamāna is the body of the sacrifice, the gāyatrī is the mouth, the Gāyatra [sāman] is the breath. When they chant on the gāyatrī with the Gāyatra [sāman], they place the breaths in the mouth.

7.3.s: prāṇāpānā vā etāni cchandāṃsi prāṇo gāyatrī vyāno bṛhaty apānas triṣṭub yad etaiś chandobhiḥ stuvanti prāṇāpānānām avicchedāya
7.3.d: प्राणापाना वा एतानि च्छन्दांसि प्राणो गायत्री व्यानो बृहत्य् अपानस् त्रिष्टुब् यद् एतैश् छन्दोभिः स्तुवन्ति प्राणापानानाम् अविच्छेदाय
7.3.m: These metres are out-breathing and in-breathing: the gāyatrī is the out-breathing, the bṛhatī is the diffused breath, the triṣṭubh is the in-breathing. When they chant with these metres, [it is] for the non-interruption of out-breathing and in-breathing.

7.3.s: ime vai lokā etāni cchandāṃsy ayam eva gāyatry ayaṃ madhyamo bṛhaty asāv uttamas triṣṭub yad etaś chandobhiḥ saṃhitaiḥ stuvanty eṣāṃ lokānām avicchedāya
7.3.d: इमे वै लोका एतानि च्छन्दांस्य् अयम् एव गायत्र्य् अयं मध्यमो बृहत्य् असाव् उत्तमस् त्रिष्टुब् यद् एतश् छन्दोभिः संहितैः स्तुवन्त्य् एषां लोकानाम् अविच्छेदाय
7.3.m: These metres are these worlds: this [earth] is the gāyatrī, this intermediate [world] is the bṛhatī, that highest [world] is the triṣṭubh. When they chant with these metres combined, [it is] for the non-separation of these worlds.

7.3.s: yad anyac chando 'ntarā vyaveyād imāṃl lokān vicchindyāt
7.3.d: यद् अन्यच् छन्दो ऽन्तरा व्यवेयाद् इमांल् लोकान् विच्छिन्द्यात्
7.3.m: If another metre should intervene between [them], it would tear these worlds apart.

7.3.s: gāyatreṇa stutvā nidhanavatā stuvantīyaṃ vai gāyatry asyām eva tad āyatanaṃ kriyate
7.3.d: गायत्रेण स्तुत्वा निधनवता स्तुवन्तीयं वै गायत्र्य् अस्याम् एव तद् आयतनं क्रियते
7.3.m: Having chanted with the Gāyatra, they chant with that which has a cadence. This [earth] is the gāyatrī; upon it a firm foundation is thereby made.

7.3.s: yad anidhanenāgre stuyur anāyatano yajamānaḥ syāt
7.3.d: यद् अनिधनेनाग्रे स्तुयुर् अनायतनो यजमानः स्यात्
7.3.m: If they were to chant with that which lacks a cadence at the beginning, the sacrificer would be without a firm foundation.

7.3.s: nidhanavatā stuvanti vīryaṃ vai gāyatrī vīryaṃ nidhanaṃ vīryeṇaiva tad vīryaṃ samardhayati
7.3.d: निधनवता स्तुवन्ति वीर्यं वै गायत्री वीर्यं निधनं वीर्येणैव तद् वीर्यं समर्धयति
7.3.m: They chant with that which has a cadence. The gāyatrī is valour, the cadence is valour; with valour he thus provides valour.

7.3.s: aiḍena bṛhatīm ārabhante
7.3.d: ऐडेन बृहतीम् आरभन्ते
7.3.m: With that which has an iḍā [cadence] they begin the bṛhatī.

7.3.s: paśavo vā iḍā paśavo bṛhatī paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti
7.3.d: पशवो वा इडा पशवो बृहती पशुष्व् एव तत् पशून् दधाति
7.3.m: Iḍā is cattle, the bṛhatī is cattle; in cattle he thus places cattle.

7.3.s: bṛhatyāṃ bhūyiṣṭhāni sāmāni bhavanti
7.3.d: बृहत्यां भूयिष्ठानि सामानि भवन्ति
7.3.m: Upon the bṛhatī are the most numerous sāmans.

7.3.s: tatrāpi triṇidhanam
7.3.d: तत्रापि त्रिणिधनम्

7.3.s: abaliṣṭha iva vā ayaṃ madhyami lokas tasyaiva tad āyatanaṃ kriyate
7.3.d: अबलिष्ठ इव वा अयं मध्यमि लोकस् तस्यैव तद् आयतनं क्रियते
7.3.m: This middle world is, as it were, weakest; a firm foundation is thereby made for it.

7.3.s: triṇidhanaṃ bhavati trīṇi savanānāṃ chidrāṇi tāni tenāpidhīyante
7.3.d: त्रिणिधनं भवति त्रीणि सवनानां छिद्राणि तानि तेनापिधीयन्ते
7.3.m: It has three cadences. Three are the gaps of the pressings; they are covered over by it.

7.3.s: triṇidhanaṃ bhavati traya ime lokā eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
7.3.d: त्रिणिधनं भवति त्रय इमे लोका एष्व् एव लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
7.3.m: It has three cadences. Three are these worlds; in these worlds he finds a firm foundation.

7.3.s: triṇidhanaṃ bhavaty etena vai mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yat triṇidhanaṃ yat triṇidhanaṃ na syād apratiṣṭhitaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ syāt
7.3.d: त्रिणिधनं भवत्य् एतेन वै माध्यन्दिनं सवनं प्रतिष्ठितं यत् त्रिणिधनं यत् त्रिणिधनं न स्याद् अप्रतिष्ठितं माध्यन्दिनं सवनं स्यात्
7.3.m: It has three cadences. By this, indeed, the midday pressing is firmly established, that it has three cadences. If it were not to have three cadences, the midday pressing would be without a firm foundation.

7.3.s: dvyakṣarāṇi nidhanāni bhavanti dvipād yajamāno yajamānam eva yajñe paśuṣu pratiṣthāpayati
7.3.d: द्व्यक्षराणि निधनानि भवन्ति द्विपाद् यजमानो यजमानम् एव यज्ञे पशुषु प्रतिष्थापयति
7.3.m: The cadences are of two syllables. Two-footed is the sacrificer; he establishes the sacrificer in the sacrifice, in cattle.

7.3.s: anidhanam antato bhavati svargasya lokasyānatipādāya
7.3.d: अनिधनम् अन्ततो भवति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानतिपादाय
7.3.m: It lacks a cadence at the end, so as not to overstep the world of heaven.

7.3.s: yan nidhanavat syād yajamānaṃ svargāl lokān nirhanyāt
7.3.d: यन् निधनवत् स्याद् यजमानं स्वर्गाल् लोकान् निर्हन्यात्
7.3.m: If it were to have a cadence, it would cast the sacrificer out of the world of heaven.

7.3.s: svāraṃ bhavati
7.3.d: स्वारं भवति

7.3.s: svareṇa vai devebhyo 'ntato 'nnādyaṃ pradīyate svareṇaiva tad devebhyo 'ntato 'nnādyaṃ prayacchati
7.3.d: स्वरेण वै देवेभ्यो ऽन्ततो ऽन्नाद्यं प्रदीयते स्वरेणैव तद् देवेभ्यो ऽन्ततो ऽन्नाद्यं प्रयच्छति
7.3.m: By the tone, indeed, food is offered to the gods at the end; by the tone he offers food to the gods at the end.

7.3.s: gāyatraṃ purastād bhavati svāram antataḥ
7.3.d: गायत्रं पुरस्ताद् भवति स्वारम् अन्ततः
7.3.m: The Gāyatra is at the beginning, ending in a tone at the end.

7.3.s: prāṇo vai gāyatraṃ prāṇaḥ svaraḥ prāṇān evatad ubhayato dadhāti tasmād ubhayataḥ prāṇāḥ paśavaḥ
7.3.d: प्राणो वै गायत्रं प्राणः स्वरः प्राणान् एवतद् उभयतो दधाति तस्माद् उभयतः प्राणाः पशवः
7.3.m: The Gāyatra is the breath, the tone is the breath; he thus places the breaths on both sides. Therefore cattle have breath on both sides.

7.3.s: yad gāyatraṃ purastād bhavati svāram antataḥ prāṇair eva praity apāne pratitiṣṭhati
7.3.d: यद् गायत्रं पुरस्ताद् भवति स्वारम् अन्ततः प्राणैर् एव प्रैत्य् अपाने प्रतितिष्ठति
7.3.m: In that the Gāyatra is at the beginning, ending in a tone at the end, he goes forth with the out-breathings and establishes himself in the in-breathing.

7.4.s: etad vai yajñasya svargyaṃ yan mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ mādhyandinasya pavamānaḥ pavamānasya bṛhatī yad bṛhatyāḥ stotre dakṣiṇā dīyante svargasyaiva tal lokasyāyatane dīyante
7.4.d: एतद् वै यज्ञस्य स्वर्ग्यं यन् माध्यन्दिनं सवनं माध्यन्दिनस्य पवमानः पवमानस्य बृहती यद् बृहत्याः स्तोत्रे दक्षिणा दीयन्ते स्वर्गस्यैव तल् लोकस्यायतने दीयन्ते
7.4.m: That which leads to heaven in the sacrifice is the midday pressing; of the midday [pressing], the Pavamāna; of the Pavamāna, the bṛhatī. In that the sacrificial gifts are given at the chant of praise of the bṛhatī, they are given in the very abode of the world of heaven.

7.4.s: devā vai cchandāṃsy abruvan yuṣmābhiḥ svargyaṃl lokam ayāmeti te gāyatrīṃ prāyuñjata tayā na vyāpnuvaṃs triṣṭubhaṃ prāyuñjata tayā na vyāpnuvañ jagatīṃ prāyuñjata tayā na vyāpnuvann anuṣṭubhaṃ prāyuñjata tayālpakādi na vyāpnuvaṃs ta āsāṃ diśāṃ rasān prabṛhya catvāry akṣarāṇy upādadhuḥ sā bṛhaty abhavat tayemāṃl lokān vyāpnuvan
7.4.d: देवा वै च्छन्दांस्य् अब्रुवन् युष्माभिः स्वर्ग्यंल् लोकम् अयामेति ते गायत्रीं प्रायुञ्जत तया न व्याप्नुवंस् त्रिष्टुभं प्रायुञ्जत तया न व्याप्नुवञ् जगतीं प्रायुञ्जत तया न व्याप्नुवन्न् अनुष्टुभं प्रायुञ्जत तयाल्पकादि न व्याप्नुवंस् त आसां दिशां रसान् प्रबृह्य चत्वार्य् अक्षराण्य् उपादधुः सा बृहत्य् अभवत् तयेमांल् लोकान् व्याप्नुवन्
7.4.m: The gods said to the metres, 'Let us go to the world of heaven with you.' They harnessed the gāyatrī; with it they did not reach [it]. They harnessed the triṣṭubh; with it they did not reach [it]. They harnessed the jagatī; with it they did not reach [it]. They harnessed the anuṣṭubh; with it, because of its smallness, they did not reach [it]. Having extracted the essences of these directions, they added four syllables [to it]. It became the bṛhatī; with it they reached these worlds.

7.4.s: bṛhatī maryā yayemāṃl lokān vyāpāmeti tad bṛhatyā bṛhattvam
7.4.d: बृहती मर्या ययेमांल् लोकान् व्यापामेति तद् बृहत्या बृहत्त्वम्
7.4.m: 'It has become great (bṛhatī), O mortals, by which we reached these worlds'; that is the bṛhatī-nature of the bṛhatī.

7.4.s: paśūn vā asyāntān upādadhuḥ paśavo vai bṛhatī yad bṛhatyāḥ stotre dakṣiṇā dīyante sva eva tad āyatane dīyante
7.4.d: पशून् वा अस्यान्तान् उपादधुः पशवो वै बृहती यद् बृहत्याः स्तोत्रे दक्षिणा दीयन्ते स्व एव तद् आयतने दीयन्ते
7.4.m: They added cattle to its ends. The bṛhatī is cattle. In that the sacrificial gifts are given at the chant of praise of the bṛhatī, they are given in its own abode.

7.4.s: yan nv ity āhur anyāni cchandāṃsi varṣīyāṃsi kasmād bṛhaty ucyata eṣā hīmāṃl lokān vyāpnon nānyac chandaḥ kiṃ cana yāni sapta caturuttarāṇi cchandāṃsi tāni bṛhatīm abhisaṃpadyante tasmād bṛhaty ucyate
7.4.d: यन् न्व् इत्य् आहुर् अन्यानि च्छन्दांसि वर्षीयांसि कस्माद् बृहत्य् उच्यत एषा हीमांल् लोकान् व्याप्नोन् नान्यच् छन्दः किं चन यानि सप्त चतुरुत्तराणि च्छन्दांसि तानि बृहतीम् अभिसंपद्यन्ते तस्माद् बृहत्य् उच्यते
7.4.m: As to what they say: 'Other metres are larger; why is it called the great (bṛhatī)?' Because it pervaded these worlds, and no other metre whatever [did]. The seven metres that increase by four [syllables] merge into the bṛhatī; therefore it is called the bṛhatī.

7.4.s: yan nv ity āhur gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ kasmād bṛhatyā madhyandine stuvantīti
7.4.d: यन् न्व् इत्य् आहुर् गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं त्रैष्टुभं माध्यन्दिनं सवनं जागतं तृतीयसवनं कस्माद् बृहत्या मध्यन्दिने स्तुवन्तीति
7.4.m: As to what they say: 'The morning pressing belongs to the gāyatrī, the midday pressing belongs to the triṣṭubh, the third pressing belongs to the jagatī; why do they chant on the bṛhatī at midday?'

7.4.s: bahiṣpavamānena vai devā ādityaṃ svargaṃl lokam aharan sa nādhriyata taṃ bṛhatyā madhyandine 'stabhnuvaṃs tasmād bṛhatyā madhyandinaṃ stuvanty ādityaṃ hy eṣā madhyandine dādhāra
7.4.d: बहिष्पवमानेन वै देवा आदित्यं स्वर्गंल् लोकम् अहरन् स नाध्रियत तं बृहत्या मध्यन्दिने ऽस्तभ्नुवंस् तस्माद् बृहत्या मध्यन्दिनं स्तुवन्त्य् आदित्यं ह्य् एषा मध्यन्दिने दाधार
7.4.m: By the Bahiṣpavamāna, the gods carried the sun to the world of heaven; it did not stay upright. By the bṛhatī they supported it at midday. Therefore they chant with the bṛhatī at midday, for it held up the sun at midday.

7.4.s: yair u kaiś ca cchandobhir madhyandine stuvanti tāni triṣṭubham abhi saṃpadyante tasmāt triṣṭubho nayanti mādhyandināt savanāt
7.4.d: यैर् उ कैश् च च्छन्दोभिर् मध्यन्दिने स्तुवन्ति तानि त्रिष्टुभम् अभि संपद्यन्ते तस्मात् त्रिष्टुभो नयन्ति माध्यन्दिनात् सवनात्
7.4.m: And whatever metres they chant with at midday, they merge into the triṣṭubh. Therefore they do not depart from the triṣṭubh at the midday pressing.

7.5.s: prajāpatir akāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa śocann amahīyamāno 'tiṣṭhat sa etad āmahīyavam apaśyat tenemāḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭā amahīyanta yad amahīyanta tasmād āmahīyavam
7.5.d: प्रजापतिर् अकामयत बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति स शोचन्न् अमहीयमानो ऽतिष्ठत् स एतद् आमहीयवम् अपश्यत् तेनेमाः प्रजा असृजत ताः सृष्टा अमहीयन्त यद् अमहीयन्त तस्माद् आमहीयवम्
7.5.m: Prajāpati desired: 'May I be many, may I propagate.' Grieving, unesteemed, he remained. He saw this Āmahīyava [sāman]; by it he created these creatures. Once created, they were esteemed (amahīyanta); because they were esteemed, that is why it is called the Āmahīyava.

7.5.s: tā asmāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tāsāṃ divi sad bhūmy ādada iti prāṇān ādatta tā enaṃ prāṇeṣv ātteṣu punar upāvartanta tābhya ugraṃ śarma mahi śrava iti punaḥ prāṇān prāyacchat tā asmād ud evāyodhaṃs tāsāṃ stauṣa iti manyūn avāśṛṇāt tato vai tasmai tāḥ śraiṣṭhyāyātiṣṭhanta
7.5.d: ता अस्मात् सृष्टा अपाक्रामंस् तासां दिवि सद् भूम्य् आदद इति प्राणान् आदत्त ता एनं प्राणेष्व् आत्तेषु पुनर् उपावर्तन्त ताभ्य उग्रं शर्म महि श्रव इति पुनः प्राणान् प्रायच्छत् ता अस्माद् उद् एवायोधंस् तासां स्तौष इति मन्यून् अवाशृणात् ततो वै तस्मै ताः श्रैष्ठ्यायातिष्ठन्त
7.5.m: Created, they departed from him. With [the words], 'Dwelling in heaven, I have taken on earth,' he took their vital breaths. Their vital breaths having been taken, they turned back to him. With [the words], 'Fierce protection, great renown,' he gave them back their vital breaths. They rose up against him; with [the word], 'I shall praise,' he broke their wrath. Thereupon, indeed, they submitted to him for pre-eminence.

7.5.s: tiṣṭhante 'smai samānāḥ śraiṣṭhyāya ya evaṃv veda
7.5.d: तिष्ठन्ते ऽस्मै समानाः श्रैष्ठ्याय य एवंव् वेद
7.5.m: His equals submit to him for pre-eminence, who knows thus.

7.5.s: prajānāṃ ca vā eṣā sṛṣṭiḥ pāpavasīyaś ca vidhṛtir yad āmahīyavam
7.5.d: प्रजानां च वा एषा सृष्टिः पापवसीयश् च विधृतिर् यद् आमहीयवम्
7.5.m: The creation of creatures and the separation of the worse and the better, indeed, is that which is the Āmahīyava [sāman].

7.5.s: vidhṛtiḥ pāpavasīyaso bhavati ya evaṃv veda
7.5.d: विधृतिः पापवसीयसो भवति य एवंव् वेद
7.5.m: He becomes a separator of the worse and the better, who knows thus.

7.5.s: devā vai yaśaskāmāḥ sattram āsatāgnir indro vāyur makhas te 'bruvsn yan no yaśa ṛcchāt tan naḥ sahāsad iti teṣā makhaṃ yaśa ārcchat tad ādāyāpākrāmat tad asya prāsahāditsanta taṃ paryayatanta svadhanuḥ pratiṣṭhābhyātiṣṭhat tasya dhanurārtnir ūrdhvā patitvā śiro 'cchinat sa pravargyo 'bhavad yajño vai makho yat pravargyaṃ pravṛñjanti yajñasyaiva tac chiraḥ pratidadhati
7.5.d: देवा वै यशस्कामाः सत्त्रम् आसताग्निर् इन्द्रो वायुर् मखस् ते ऽब्रुव्स्न् यन् नो यश ऋच्छात् तन् नः सहासद् इति तेषा मखं यश आर्च्छत् तद् आदायापाक्रामत् तद् अस्य प्रासहादित्सन्त तं पर्ययतन्त स्वधनुः प्रतिष्ठाभ्यातिष्ठत् तस्य धनुरार्त्निर् ऊर्ध्वा पतित्वा शिरो ऽच्छिनत् स प्रवर्ग्यो ऽभवद् यज्ञो वै मखो यत् प्रवर्ग्यं प्रवृञ्जन्ति यज्ञस्यैव तच् छिरः प्रतिदधति
7.5.m: The gods, desirous of glory, held a sacrificial session: Agni, Indra, Vāyu, [and] Makha. They said, 'Whichever glory reaches us, that shall belong to us in common.' Glory reached Makha among them. Taking it, he departed. They wished to take it from him by force. They surrounded him. He stood resting upon his bow. The tip of his bow, springing upward, cut off his head. He became the Pravargya. Makha, indeed, is the sacrifice. When they perform the Pravargya rite, it is the head of the sacrifice that they restore.

7.5.s: tad devā yaśo vyabhajanta tasyāgnī rauravaṃ prābṛhata
7.5.d: तद् देवा यशो व्यभजन्त तस्याग्नी रौरवं प्राबृहत
7.5.m: The gods divided that glory. From it Agni drew out the Raurava [sāman].

7.5.s: tad vai sa paśuvīryaṃ prābṛhata paśavo vai rauravam
7.5.d: तद् वै स पशुवीर्यं प्राबृहत पशवो वै रौरवम्
7.5.m: He, indeed, drew out the valour of cattle; cattle, indeed, are the Raurava.

7.5.s: paśumān bhavati ya evaṃv veda
7.5.d: पशुमान् भवति य एवंव् वेद
7.5.m: He becomes possessed of cattle, who knows thus.

7.5.s: agnir vai rūras tasyaitad rauravam
7.5.d: अग्निर् वै रूरस् तस्यैतद् रौरवम्
7.5.m: Agni, indeed, is Rūra; this Raurava is his.

7.5.s: asurā vai devān paryayatanta tata etāv agnī rūrau viṣvañcau stobhāv apaśyat tābhyām enān pratyauṣat te pratyuṣyamāṇā aravanta yad aravanta tasmād rauravam
7.5.d: असुरा वै देवान् पर्ययतन्त तत एताव् अग्नी रूरौ विष्वञ्चौ स्तोभाव् अपश्यत् ताभ्याम् एनान् प्रत्यौषत् ते प्रत्युष्यमाणा अरवन्त यद् अरवन्त तस्माद् रौरवम्
7.5.m: The Asuras, indeed, surrounded the gods. Then Agni saw these two Rūra stobhas, extending in all directions. With them he burnt them away. Being burnt away, they roared. Because they roared, therefore it is called Raurava.

7.5.s: athendro yaudhājayaṃ prābṛhata tad vai sa vajraṃ prābṛhata vajro vai yaudhājayam
7.5.d: अथेन्द्रो यौधाजयं प्राबृहत तद् वै स वज्रं प्राबृहत वज्रो वै यौधाजयम्
7.5.m: Then Indra drew out the Yaudhājaya [sāman]. He, indeed, drew out the thunderbolt; the thunderbolt, indeed, is the Yaudhājaya.

7.5.s: vajraṃ bhrātṛvyāya praharati ya evaṃv veda
7.5.d: वज्रं भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति य एवंव् वेद
7.5.m: He hurls a thunderbolt at his rival, who knows thus.

7.5.s: indro vai yudhājit tasyaitad yaudhājayam
7.5.d: इन्द्रो वै युधाजित् तस्यैतद् यौधाजयम्
7.5.m: Indra, indeed, is Yudhājit; this Yaudhājaya is his.

7.5.s: yudhā maryā ajaiṣmeti tasmād yaudhājayam
7.5.d: युधा मर्या अजैष्मेति तस्माद् यौधाजयम्
7.5.m: Because [they said], 'O mortals, we have conquered by fighting,' therefore it is called Yaudhājaya.

7.5.s: atha vāyur auśanaṃ prābṛhata
7.5.d: अथ वायुर् औशनं प्राबृहत
7.5.m: Then Vāyu drew out the Auśana [sāman].

7.5.s: tad vai sa prāṇvīryaṃ prābṛhata prāṇā vā auśanam
7.5.d: तद् वै स प्राण्वीर्यं प्राबृहत प्राणा वा औशनम्
7.5.m: He, indeed, drew out the valour of vital breath; vital breaths, indeed, are the Auśana.

7.5.s: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃv veda
7.5.d: सर्वम् आयुर् एति य एवंव् वेद
7.5.m: He reaches the full span of life, who knows thus.

7.5.s: vāyur vā uśanaṃs tasyaitad auśanam
7.5.d: वायुर् वा उशनंस् तस्यैतद् औशनम्

7.5.s: uśanā vai kāvyo 'surāṇāṃ purohita āsīt taṃ devāḥ kāmadughābhir apāmantrayanta tasmā etāny auśanāni prāyacchan kāmadughā vā auśanāni
7.5.d: उशना वै काव्यो ऽसुराणां पुरोहित आसीत् तं देवाः कामदुघाभिर् अपामन्त्रयन्त तस्मा एतान्य् औशनानि प्रायच्छन् कामदुघा वा औशनानि
7.5.m: Uśanas Kāvya, indeed, was the domestic priest of the Asuras. The gods lured him away with wish-granting cows. They gave him these Auśana [sāmans]. The Auśana [sāmans], indeed, are wish-granting cows.

7.5.s: kāmadughā enam upatiṣṭhante ya evaṃv veda
7.5.d: कामदुघा एनम् उपतिष्ठन्ते य एवंव् वेद
7.5.m: Wish-granting cows attend upon him, who knows thus.

7.6.s: prajāpatir akāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa tūṣṇīṃ manasādhyāyat tasya yan manasy āsīt tad bṛhat samabhavat
7.6.d: प्रजापतिर् अकामयत बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति स तूष्णीं मनसाध्यायत् तस्य यन् मनस्य् आसीत् तद् बृहत् समभवत्
7.6.m: Prajāpati desired: 'May I be many, may I procreate.' He meditated silently in his mind. That which was in his mind became the Bṛhat.

7.6.s: sa ādadhīta garbho vai me 'yam antarhitas taṃv vācā prajanayā iti
7.6.d: स आदधीत गर्भो वै मे ऽयम् अन्तर्हितस् तंव् वाचा प्रजनया इति
7.6.m: He considered: 'This embryo is concealed within me; let me bring it forth by speech.'

7.6.s: sa vācaṃ vyasṛjata sā vāg rathantaram anvapadyata
7.6.d: स वाचं व्यसृजत सा वाग् रथन्तरम् अन्वपद्यत
7.6.m: He emitted speech; that speech followed after the Rathantara.

7.6.s: ratham aryāḥ kṣeplātārīd iti tad rathantarasya rathantaratvam
7.6.d: रथम् अर्याः क्षेप्लातारीद् इति तद् रथन्तरस्य रथन्तरत्वम्
7.6.m: That [he said], 'A chariot, O noble ones, has crossed with speed,' that is the Rathantara-nature of the Rathantara.

7.6.s: tato bṛhad anu prājāyata bṛhan maryā idaṃ sa jyog antarabhūd iti tad bṛhato bṛhattvam
7.6.d: ततो बृहद् अनु प्राजायत बृहन् मर्या इदं स ज्योग् अन्तरभूद् इति तद् बृहतो बृहत्त्वम्
7.6.m: Then the Bṛhat was born along after it: 'Great, O mortals, is this one; he was long within [me],' that is the Bṛhat-nature of the Bṛhat.

7.6.s: yathā vai putro jyeṣṭha evaṃ bṛhat prajāpateḥ
7.6.d: यथा वै पुत्रो ज्येष्ठ एवं बृहत् प्रजापतेः
7.6.m: Just as an eldest son is, so is the Bṛhat to Prajāpati.
This, indeed, is the Brāhmaṇa of the eldest.

7.6.s: pra jyaiṣṭhyam āpnoti ya evaṃv veda
7.6.d: प्र ज्यैष्ठ्यम् आप्नोति य एवंव् वेद
7.6.m: He attains seniority, who knows thus.

7.6.s: yan nv ity āhur bṛhat pūrvaṃ prajāpatau samabhavat kasmād rathantaraṃ pūrvaṃ yogam ānaśa iti
7.6.d: यन् न्व् इत्य् आहुर् बृहत् पूर्वं प्रजापतौ समभवत् कस्माद् रथन्तरं पूर्वं योगम् आनश इति
7.6.m: Now as to what they say: 'The Bṛhat came into being first in Prajāpati; why did the Rathantara attain prior employment?'

7.6.s: bṛhad eva pūrvaṃ samabhavad rathantaraṃ tu pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭyāsṛjata tasmāt pūrvaṃ yogam ānaśe
7.6.d: बृहद् एव पूर्वं समभवद् रथन्तरं तु पूर्वं सृष्ट्यासृजत तस्मात् पूर्वं योगम् आनशे
7.6.m: The Bṛhat, indeed, came into being first, but he emitted the Rathantara first through creation; therefore it attained prior employment.

7.6.s: tayoḥ samānaṃ nidhanam āsīt tasmin nātiṣṭhetāṃ ta ājim aitāṃ tayor has iti bṛhat prāṇam udajayad as iti rathantaram apānam abhisamaveṣṭata
7.6.d: तयोः समानं निधनम् आसीत् तस्मिन् नातिष्ठेतां त आजिम् ऐतां तयोर् हस् इति बृहत् प्राणम् उदजयद् अस् इति रथन्तरम् अपानम् अभिसमवेष्टत
7.6.m: They two had the same cadence. They could not agree upon it. They ran a race. Of the two, the Bṛhat won the out-breath with [the sound] 'has'; the Rathantara encompassed the in-breath with [the sound] 'as'.

7.6.s: prāṇāpānau vai bṛhadrathantare jyog āmayāvina ubhe kuryād apakrāntau vā etasya prāṇāpānau yasya jyog āmayati prāṇāpānāv evāsmin dadhāti
7.6.d: प्राणापानौ वै बृहद्रथन्तरे ज्योग् आमयाविन उभे कुर्याद् अपक्रान्तौ वा एतस्य प्राणापानौ यस्य ज्योग् आमयति प्राणापानाव् एवास्मिन् दधाति
7.6.m: The Bṛhat and the Rathantara, indeed, are out-breath and in-breath. For one who is chronically ill he should perform both; out-breath and in-breath have departed from him who is chronically ill; he thus places out-breath and in-breath in him.

7.6.s: yan nv ity āhur ubhe bṛhadrathantare bahirṇidhane kasmād bṛhad bahirṇidhanāni bhajate 'ntarṇidhanāni rathantaram iti
7.6.d: यन् न्व् इत्य् आहुर् उभे बृहद्रथन्तरे बहिर्णिधने कस्माद् बृहद् बहिर्णिधनानि भजते ऽन्तर्णिधनानि रथन्तरम् इति
7.6.m: Now as to what they say: 'Both the Bṛhat and the Rathantara have an external cadence; why does the Bṛhat partake of external cadences, and the Rathantara of internal cadences?'

7.6.s: prāṇo bṛhat tasmād bahirṇidhanāni bhajate bahir hi prāṇo 'pāno rathantaraṃ tasmād antarṇidhanāni bhajate 'ntar hy apānaḥ
7.6.d: प्राणो बृहत् तस्माद् बहिर्णिधनानि भजते बहिर् हि प्राणो ऽपानो रथन्तरं तस्माद् अन्तर्णिधनानि भजते ऽन्तर् ह्य् अपानः
7.6.m: Out-breath is the Bṛhat, therefore it partakes of external cadences, for out-breath is outside; in-breath is the Rathantara, therefore it partakes of internal cadences, for in-breath is inside.
The Bṛhat and Rathantara, indeed, are two great trees colliding with their cadence.

7.6.s: yad vai mahāvṛkṣau samṛcchete bahu tatra vibhagnaṃ prabhagnaṃ śete
7.6.d: यद् वै महावृक्षौ समृच्छेते बहु तत्र विभग्नं प्रभग्नं शेते
7.6.m: When two great trees collide, much lies broken to pieces and shattered there.

7.6.s: airaṃ vai bṛhad aiḍaṃ rathantaraṃ mano vai bṛhad vāg rathantaraṃ sām a vai bṛhad ṛg rathantaraṃ prāṇo vai bṛhad apāno rathantaram asau vai loko bṛhad ayaṃ rathantaram etāni manasānvīkṣyodgāyet kḷptābhyām evābhyām udgāyati
7.6.d: ऐरं वै बृहद् ऐडं रथन्तरं मनो वै बृहद् वाग् रथन्तरं साम् अ वै बृहद् ऋग् रथन्तरं प्राणो वै बृहद् अपानो रथन्तरम् असौ वै लोको बृहद् अयं रथन्तरम् एतानि मनसान्वीक्ष्योद्गायेत् कॢप्ताभ्याम् एवाभ्याम् उद्गायति
7.6.m: The Bṛhat, indeed, has [the sound] irā; the Rathantara has [the sound] iḍā. The Bṛhat, indeed, is mind; the Rathantara is speech. The Bṛhat, indeed, is the sāman; the Rathantara is the ṛc. The Bṛhat, indeed, is out-breath; the Rathantara is in-breath. That world, indeed, is the Bṛhat; this [world] is the Rathantara. Keeping these in mind, one should chant the udgītha; with both of them properly ordered, he chants the udgītha.

7.7.s: paśavo vai bṛhadrathantare aṣṭākṣareṇa prathamāyā ṛcaḥ prastauty aṣṭāśaphāṃs tat paśūn avarundhe
7.7.d: पशवो वै बृहद्रथन्तरे अष्टाक्षरेण प्रथमाया ऋचः प्रस्तौत्य् अष्टाशफांस् तत् पशून् अवरुन्धे
7.7.m: Cattle, indeed, are the Bṛhat and Rathantara. With eight syllables of the first verse he chants the prastāva; he thereby secures eight-hoofed cattle.

7.7.s: dvyakṣareṇottarayor ṛcoḥ prastauti dvipād yajamāno yajamānam eva yajñe paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati
7.7.d: द्व्यक्षरेणोत्तरयोर् ऋचोः प्रस्तौति द्विपाद् यजमानो यजमानम् एव यज्ञे पशुषु प्रतिष्ठापयति
7.7.m: With two syllables he chants the prastāva of the two subsequent verses. Two-footed is the sacrificer; he thus firmly establishes the sacrificer in the sacrifice among cattle.

7.7.s: pañcākṣareṇa rathantarasya pratiharati pāṅktāṃs tat paśūn avarundhe
7.7.d: पञ्चाक्षरेण रथन्तरस्य प्रतिहरति पाङ्क्तांस् तत् पशून् अवरुन्धे
7.7.m: With five syllables he chants the pratihāra of the Rathantara; he thereby secures five-fold cattle.

7.7.s: caturakṣareṇa bṛhataḥ pratiharati catuṣpadas tat paśūn avarundhe
7.7.d: चतुरक्षरेण बृहतः प्रतिहरति चतुष्पदस् तत् पशून् अवरुन्धे
7.7.m: With four syllables he chants the pratihāra of the Bṛhat; he thereby secures four-footed cattle.

7.7.s: na vai bṛhan na rathantaram ekaṃ chando 'yacchat tataḥ kakubhāv uttare upādadhus tasmād bṛhatī prathamā kakubhāv uttare tasmād bṛhadrathantare ekarcena kurvanti na hi te ekaṃ chando 'yacchat
7.7.d: न वै बृहन् न रथन्तरम् एकं छन्दो ऽयच्छत् ततः ककुभाव् उत्तरे उपादधुस् तस्माद् बृहती प्रथमा ककुभाव् उत्तरे तस्माद् बृहद्रथन्तरे एकर्चेन कुर्वन्ति न हि ते एकं छन्दो ऽयच्छत्
7.7.m: Neither the Bṛhat nor the Rathantara yielded to a single metre. Then they added two kakubhs after [it]; therefore the first is a bṛhatī, and the two subsequent are kakubhs. Therefore they perform the Bṛhat and Rathantara on a single verse, for they did not yield to a single metre.

7.7.s: nava bṛhato rohān rohati nava prāṇāḥ prāṇān evāvarundhe
7.7.d: नव बृहतो रोहान् रोहति नव प्राणाः प्राणान् एवावरुन्धे
7.7.m: He ascends the nine ascents of the Bṛhat. Nine are the vital breaths; he secures the vital breaths.

7.7.s: trīn prathamāyāṃ rohati bhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyat tān evāvarundhe trīn madhyamāyāṃ rohaty ātmānaṃ prajāṃ paśūṃs tān evāvarundhe trīn uttamāyāṃ rohati traya ime lokā eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
7.7.d: त्रीन् प्रथमायां रोहति भूतं भवद् भविष्यत् तान् एवावरुन्धे त्रीन् मध्यमायां रोहत्य् आत्मानं प्रजां पशूंस् तान् एवावरुन्धे त्रीन् उत्तमायां रोहति त्रय इमे लोका एष्व् एव लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
7.7.m: He ascends three on the first: the past, the present, the future—these he secures. He ascends three on the middle one: himself, offspring, cattle—these he secures. He ascends three on the last: three are these worlds; in these worlds he becomes firmly established.

7.7.s: sarvān kāmān avarundhe ya evaṃv vidvān bṛhato rohān rohati
7.7.d: सर्वान् कामान् अवरुन्धे य एवंव् विद्वान् बृहतो रोहान् रोहति
7.7.m: He secures all desires, who, knowing thus, ascends the ascents of the Bṛhat.

7.7.s: vajreṇa vā etat prastotodgātāram abhipravartayati yad rathantaraṃ prastauti samudram antardhāyodgāyed vāg ity ādeyaṃv vāg vai samudraḥ samudram evāntardadhāty ahiṃsāyai
7.7.d: वज्रेण वा एतत् प्रस्तोतोद्गातारम् अभिप्रवर्तयति यद् रथन्तरं प्रस्तौति समुद्रम् अन्तर्धायोद्गायेद् वाग् इत्य् आदेयंव् वाग् वै समुद्रः समुद्रम् एवान्तर्दधात्य् अहिंसायै
7.7.m: With a thunderbolt, indeed, the prastotṛ sets the udgātṛ in motion when he introduces the Rathantara. Putting the ocean in between, he should chant the udgītha. The syllable vāc is to be taken; speech, indeed, is the ocean. He puts the ocean in between for safety.

7.7.s: balavad geyaṃ vajram evaṃ pravṛttaṃ pratyudgṛhṇāti
7.7.d: बलवद् गेयं वज्रम् एवं प्रवृत्तं प्रत्युद्गृह्णाति
7.7.m: It should be chanted forcefully; thus he checks the thunderbolt that has been set in motion.

7.7.s: balvalā kurvatā geyam abhilobhayateva vajram evābhilobhayati
7.7.d: बल्वला कुर्वता गेयम् अभिलोभयतेव वज्रम् एवाभिलोभयति
7.7.m: It should be chanted making the sound balvalā, as if confusing [it]; he thus confuses the thunderbolt.
It should be chanted quickly, for the attainment of the heavenly world.

7.7.s: devaratho vai rathantaram akṣareṇākṣareṇa pratiṣṭhāpayatodgeyam areṇāreṇa hi rathaḥ pratitiṣṭhati
7.7.d: देवरथो वै रथन्तरम् अक्षरेणाक्षरेण प्रतिष्ठापयतोद्गेयम् अरेणारेण हि रथः प्रतितिष्ठति
7.7.m: A chariot of the gods, indeed, is the Rathantara. It should be chanted firmly establishing it syllable by syllable, for spoke by spoke a chariot is firmly established.

7.7.s: yo vai devaratham ananvālabhyātiṣṭhaty avāsmāt padyata iyaṃ vai devaratha imām ālabhyodgāyen nāsmād avapadyate
7.7.d: यो वै देवरथम् अनन्वालभ्यातिष्ठत्य् अवास्मात् पद्यत इयं वै देवरथ इमाम् आलभ्योद्गायेन् नास्माद् अवपद्यते
7.7.m: He who stands without holding on to the chariot of the gods falls down from it. This [earth], indeed, is the chariot of the gods. Touching this, he should chant the udgītha; he does not fall down from it.

7.7.s: īśvaraṃ vai rathantaram udgātuś cakṣuḥ pramathitoḥ prastuyamāne saṃmīlet svardṛśaṃ prativīkṣeta nainaṃ cakṣur jahāti
7.7.d: ईश्वरं वै रथन्तरम् उद्गातुश् चक्षुः प्रमथितोः प्रस्तुयमाने संमीलेत् स्वर्दृशं प्रतिवीक्षेत नैनं चक्षुर् जहाति
7.7.m: The Rathantara is liable to destroy the udgātṛ's eyesight. While the prastāva is being sung, he should close his eyes; at [the words] 'beholding the light of heaven', he should look up: his eyesight does not leave him.

7.7.s: prajananaṃ vai rathantaraṃ yat tasthuṣa ity āhāsthāyukodgātur vāg bhavaty api prajananaṃ hanty asthuṣa iti vaktavyaṃ susthuṣa iti vā sthāyukodgātur vāg bhavati na prajananam api hanti
7.7.d: प्रजननं वै रथन्तरं यत् तस्थुष इत्य् आहास्थायुकोद्गातुर् वाग् भवत्य् अपि प्रजननं हन्त्य् अस्थुष इति वक्तव्यं सुस्थुष इति वा स्थायुकोद्गातुर् वाग् भवति न प्रजननम् अपि हन्ति
7.7.m: The Rathantara is indeed procreation. When one says 'tasthuṣaḥ' (of what stands), the udgātṛ's voice becomes unstable, and he also harms procreation. One should say 'asthuṣaḥ' or 'susthuṣaḥ'; [then] the udgātṛ's voice becomes stable, and he does not harm procreation.

7.7.s: pṛṣṭhāni vā asṛjyanta tair devāḥ svargaṃl lokam āyaṃs teṣāṃ rathantaraṃ mahimnā nāśaknod utpatat
7.7.d: पृष्ठानि वा असृज्यन्त तैर् देवाः स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयंस् तेषां रथन्तरं महिम्ना नाशक्नोद् उत्पतत्
7.7.m: The pṛṣṭhas were indeed created. By means of them the gods went to the heavenly world. Among them, the Rathantara could not fly up because of its greatness.

7.7.s: tasya vaśiṣṭho mahimno vinidhāya tena stutvā svargaṃl lokam ait tān saṃbhṛtyodgāyet
7.7.d: तस्य वशिष्ठो महिम्नो विनिधाय तेन स्तुत्वा स्वर्गंल् लोकम् ऐत् तान् संभृत्योद्गायेत्
7.7.m: Vaśiṣṭha, having deposited its greatness, chanted praise with it and went to the heavenly world. Having gathered those [powers of greatness], he should chant the udgītha:

7.7.s: yas te goṣu mahimā yas te apsu rathe vā te stanayitnau ya u te yas te agnau mahimā tena saṃbhava rathantara draviṇavan na edhi
7.7.d: यस् ते गोषु महिमा यस् ते अप्सु रथे वा ते स्तनयित्नौ य उ ते यस् ते अग्नौ महिमा तेन संभव रथन्तर द्रविणवन् न एधि
7.7.m: 'What greatness of yours is in cattle, what in the waters, or in the chariot, or what in the thunder, / What greatness of yours is in fire—with that become united, O Rathantara! Be wealthy for us!'

7.8.s: apo vā ṛtvyam ārcchat tāsāṃv vāyuḥ pṛṣṭhe vyavartata tato vasu vāmaṃ samabhavat tasmin mitrāvaruṇau paryapaśyatāṃ tāv abrūtāṃv vāmaṃ maryā idaṃ deveṣv ājānīti tasmād vāmadevyam
7.8.d: अपो वा ऋत्व्यम् आर्च्छत् तासांव् वायुः पृष्ठे व्यवर्तत ततो वसु वामं समभवत् तस्मिन् मित्रावरुणौ पर्यपश्यतां ताव् अब्रूतांव् वामं मर्या इदं देवेष्व् आजानीति तस्माद् वामदेव्यम्
7.8.m: The waters indeed reached their fertile season. On their back Vāyu moved; from that, a fair treasure came into being. Mitra and Varuṇa looked upon it; they said: 'Men, recognize this fair [treasure] among the gods!' Therefore it is called Vāmadevya.

7.8.s: tat parigṛhṇantāv abrūtām idam avidāvedaṃ nau mābhyartiḍhvam iti tat prajāpatir abravīn mad vā etad dhy ajani mama vā etad iti tad agnir abravīn māṃ vā etad annam ajani mama vā etad iti tad indro 'bravīc chreṣṭhasthā vā etad ahaṃ vaḥ śreṣṭho 'smi mama vā etad iti tad viśve devā abruvann asmaddevatyaṃ vā etad yad adbhyo 'dhi samabhūd asmākaṃ vā etad iti tat prajāpatir abravīt sarveṣāṃ na idam astu sarva idam upajīvāmeti tat pṛṣṭheṣu nyadadhuḥ sarvadevatyaṃ vai vāmadevyam
7.8.d: तत् परिगृह्णन्ताव् अब्रूताम् इदम् अविदावेदं नौ माभ्यर्तिढ्वम् इति तत् प्रजापतिर् अब्रवीन् मद् वा एतद् ध्य् अजनि मम वा एतद् इति तद् अग्निर् अब्रवीन् मां वा एतद् अन्नम् अजनि मम वा एतद् इति तद् इन्द्रो ऽब्रवीच् छ्रेष्ठस्था वा एतद् अहं वः श्रेष्ठो ऽस्मि मम वा एतद् इति तद् विश्वे देवा अब्रुवन्न् अस्मद्देवत्यं वा एतद् यद् अद्भ्यो ऽधि समभूद् अस्माकं वा एतद् इति तत् प्रजापतिर् अब्रवीत् सर्वेषां न इदम् अस्तु सर्व इदम् उपजीवामेति तत् पृष्ठेषु न्यदधुः सर्वदेवत्यं वै वामदेव्यम्
7.8.m: Taking hold of it, they said: 'We two have found this; this belongs to us; do not contend for it!' Prajāpati said: 'From me indeed it was born; it is mine!' Agni said: 'For me indeed this food was born; it is mine!' Indra said: 'This belongs to the standing of the pre-eminent; I am the pre-eminent among you; it is mine!' The All-gods said: 'That which arose from the waters belongs to us as deities; it is ours!' Prajāpati said: 'Let this belong to all of us; let all of us subsist on this!' They placed it among the pṛṣṭhas. The Vāmadevya indeed belongs to all deities.

7.8.s: yat kavatīṣu tena prājāpatyaṃ ko hi prajāpatir yad aniruktāsu tena prājāpatyam anirukto hi prajāpatiḥ
7.8.d: यत् कवतीषु तेन प्राजापत्यं को हि प्रजापतिर् यद् अनिरुक्तासु तेन प्राजापत्यम् अनिरुक्तो हि प्रजापतिः
7.8.m: In that it is on [verses] containing the word 'ka', thereby it belongs to Prajāpati, for who (ka) is Prajāpati; in that it is on unexpressed [verses], thereby it belongs to Prajāpati, for Prajāpati is unexpressed.

7.8.s: yad gāyatrīṣu tenāgneyaṃ gāyatracchandā hy agniḥ
7.8.d: यद् गायत्रीषु तेनाग्नेयं गायत्रच्छन्दा ह्य् अग्निः
7.8.m: In that it is on gāyatrī verses, thereby it belongs to Agni, for Agni has the gāyatrī metre.

7.8.s: yat pṛṣṭheṣu nyadadadhus tenaindraṃ sarvāṇi hi pṛṣṭhānīndrasya niṣkevalyāni
7.8.d: यत् पृष्ठेषु न्यददधुस् तेनैन्द्रं सर्वाणि हि पृष्ठानीन्द्रस्य निष्केवल्यानि
7.8.m: In that they placed it among the pṛṣṭhas, thereby it belongs to Indra, for all pṛṣṭhas are Indra's exclusive [domain].
In that the Maitrāvaruṇa recites along with it, thereby it belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa.

7.8.s: yad bahudevatyam uttamaṃ padaṃ tena vaiśvadevaṃ sarveṣv eva rūpeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
7.8.d: यद् बहुदेवत्यम् उत्तमं पदं तेन वैश्वदेवं सर्वेष्व् एव रूपेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
7.8.m: In that the last verse-foot has many deities, thereby it belongs to the All-gods. He indeed becomes established in all forms.

7.8.s: prajāpatir vā etāṃ gāyatrīṃ yonim apaśyat sa ādīdhītāsmād yoneḥ pṛṣṭhāni sṛjā iti
7.8.d: प्रजापतिर् वा एतां गायत्रीं योनिम् अपश्यत् स आदीधीतास्माद् योनेः पृष्ठानि सृजा इति
7.8.m: Prajāpati saw this gāyatrī as a womb; he reflected: 'From this womb let me create the pṛṣṭhas.'

7.8.s: sa rathantaram asṛjata tad rathasya ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
7.8.d: स रथन्तरम् असृजत तद् रथस्य घोषो ऽन्वसृज्यत
7.8.m: He created the Rathantara; after it the noise of the chariot was created.

7.8.s: sa bṛhad asṛjata tat stanayitnor ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata sa vairūpam asṛjata tad vā tasya ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
7.8.d: स बृहद् असृजत तत् स्तनयित्नोर् घोषो ऽन्वसृज्यत स वैरूपम् असृजत तद् वा तस्य घोषो ऽन्वसृज्यत
7.8.m:
He created the Bṛhat; after it the noise of thunder was created. He created the Vairūpa; after it the noise of the wind was created.

He created the Vairāja; after it the noise of fire was created.

7.8.s: sa vairūpam asṛjata tad agner ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
7.8.d: स वैरूपम् असृजत तद् अग्नेर् घोषो ऽन्वसृज्यत

7.8.s: sa śakvarīr asṛjata tad apāṃ ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
7.8.d: स शक्वरीर् असृजत तद् अपां घोषो ऽन्वसृज्यत
7.8.m: He created the Śakvarīs; after them the noise of the waters was created.

7.8.s: sa revatīr asṛjata tad gavāṃ ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
7.8.d: स रेवतीर् असृजत तद् गवां घोषो ऽन्वसृज्यत
7.8.m: He created the Revatīs; after them the noise of cattle was created.

7.8.s: etair vā etāni saha ghoṣair asṛjyanta
7.8.d: एतैर् वा एतानि सह घोषैर् असृज्यन्त
7.8.m: Along with these noises indeed these [sāmans] were created.

7.8.s: sarve 'smin ghoṣāḥ sarvāḥ puṇyā vāco vadanti ya evaṃv veda
7.8.d: सर्वे ऽस्मिन् घोषाः सर्वाः पुण्या वाचो वदन्ति य एवंव् वेद
7.8.m: In him all sounds and all auspicious speeches resound, who knows thus.

7.9.s: pitā vai vāmadevyaṃ putrāḥ pṛṣṭhāni
7.9.d: पिता वै वामदेव्यं पुत्राः पृष्ठानि
7.9.m: The Vāmadevya is the father; the pṛṣṭhas are the sons.

7.9.s: etasmād vā etāni yoner asṛjyanta
7.9.d: एतस्माद् वा एतानि योनेर् असृज्यन्त
7.9.m: From this womb indeed they were created.

7.9.s: tasmāt pṛṣṭhānāṃ stotraṃ vāmadevyenānuṣṭuvanti śāntyai
7.9.d: तस्मात् पृष्ठानां स्तोत्रं वामदेव्येनानुष्टुवन्ति शान्त्यै
7.9.m: Therefore, after the chant of praise of the pṛṣṭhas, they chant with the Vāmadevya for pacification.

7.9.s: yad dhi putro 'śāntaṃ carati pitā tac chamayati
7.9.d: यद् धि पुत्रो ऽशान्तं चरति पिता तच् छमयति
7.9.m: For whatever unpacified [thing] a son commits, the father pacifies that.

7.9.s: ayaṃ vai loko madhyamo vāmadevyam etasmād vā imau lokau viṣvañcāv asṛjyetāṃ bṛhac ca ratantaraṃ ca
7.9.d: अयं वै लोको मध्यमो वामदेव्यम् एतस्माद् वा इमौ लोकौ विष्वञ्चाव् असृज्येतां बृहच् च रतन्तरं च
7.9.m: This middle world is the Vāmadevya. From it these two worlds were created turning in different directions: the Bṛhat and the Rathantara.

7.9.s: yad rathantareṇa stuvanti ye rathantarāḥ paśavo 'ntarīkṣaṃ ta upaśrayanti yad bṛhatā stuvanti ye bārhatāḥ paśavo 'ntarīkṣaṃ ta upaśrayanti te vāmadevyasya stotreṇāvaruddhāḥ
7.9.d: यद् रथन्तरेण स्तुवन्ति ये रथन्तराः पशवो ऽन्तरीक्षं त उपश्रयन्ति यद् बृहता स्तुवन्ति ये बार्हताः पशवो ऽन्तरीक्षं त उपश्रयन्ति ते वामदेव्यस्य स्तोत्रेणावरुद्धाः
7.9.m: When they praise with the Rathantara, those cattle that belong to the Rathantara resort to the intermediate space; when they praise with the Bṛhat, those cattle that belong to the Bṛhat resort to the intermediate space. They are secured by the chant of praise of the Vāmadevya.

7.9.s: dhruva āsīno vāmadevyenodgāyet paśūnām upavṛtyai
7.9.d: ध्रुव आसीनो वामदेव्येनोद्गायेत् पशूनाम् उपवृत्यै
7.9.m: Sitting firmly, he should chant the udgītha with the Vāmadevya, for the turning toward of cattle.

7.9.s: upainaṃ paśava āvartante ya evaṃv veda
7.9.d: उपैनं पशव आवर्तन्ते य एवंव् वेद
7.9.m: Cattle turn toward him, who knows thus.

7.9.s: antarikṣaṃ vai vāmadevyam adhūnvatevodgeyam adhūtam ivāntarikṣaṃ paśavo vai vāmadevyam ahiṃsatevodgeyaṃ paśūnām ahiṃsāyai
7.9.d: अन्तरिक्षं वै वामदेव्यम् अधून्वतेवोद्गेयम् अधूतम् इवान्तरिक्षं पशवो वै वामदेव्यम् अहिंसतेवोद्गेयं पशूनाम् अहिंसायै
7.9.m: The intermediate space is the Vāmadevya; it should be sung as if without shaking, as the intermediate space is unshaken. Cattle are the Vāmadevya; it should be sung as if without harming, for the non-harming of cattle.

7.9.s: katham iva vāmadevyaṃ geyam ity āhuḥ
7.9.d: कथम् इव वामदेव्यं गेयम् इत्य् आहुः
7.9.m: They say: 'How should the Vāmadevya be sung?'

7.9.s: yathāṅkulī putrān saṃdaśyāsaṃbhindantī harati yathā vāto 'psu śanair vāti
7.9.d: यथाङ्कुली पुत्रान् संदश्यासंभिन्दन्ती हरति यथा वातो ऽप्सु शनैर् वाति
7.9.m: Just as a bitch carries her pups, biting together without crushing them, [or] as the wind blows gently over the waters.

7.9.s: svadhūr vāmadevyaṃ geyam
7.9.d: स्वधूर् वामदेव्यं गेयम्
7.9.m: The Vāmadevya should be sung having its own yoke.

7.9.s: yo vai svadhūr vāmadevyaṃ gāyati svadhūr bhavati
7.9.d: यो वै स्वधूर् वामदेव्यं गायति स्वधूर् भवति
7.9.m: He who sings the Vāmadevya having its own yoke becomes one who possesses his own yoke.

7.9.s: yāty asyānyo niyānena nānyasya niyānena yāti
7.9.d: यात्य् अस्यान्यो नियानेन नान्यस्य नियानेन याति
7.9.m: Another goes by his path; he does not go by another's path.

7.9.s: na bṛhato na rathantarasyānurūpaṃ geyaṃ svenaivāyatanena geyam āyatanavān bhavati
7.9.d: न बृहतो न रथन्तरस्यानुरूपं गेयं स्वेनैवायतनेन गेयम् आयतनवान् भवति
7.9.m: It should not be sung as a counterpart to the Bṛhat or to the Rathantara; it should be sung in its own domain; he comes to possess a proper domain.

7.9.s: devā vai paśūn vyabhajanta te rudram antarāyaṃs tān vāmadevyasya stotra upekṣate
7.9.d: देवा वै पशून् व्यभजन्त ते रुद्रम् अन्तरायंस् तान् वामदेव्यस्य स्तोत्र उपेक्षते
7.9.m: The gods divided the cattle; they excluded Rudra. He looks upon them at the chant of praise of the Vāmadevya.

7.9.s: aniruktaṃ geyam
7.9.d: अनिरुक्तं गेयम्

7.9.s: yan nirāha rudrāya paśūn apidadhāti rudras tāṃ samāṃ paśūn dhātuko bhavati
7.9.d: यन् निराह रुद्राय पशून् अपिदधाति रुद्रस् तां समां पशून् धातुको भवति
7.9.m: If he utters it explicitly, he hands over the cattle to Rudra; Rudra becomes prone to destroy cattle for that year.

7.9.s: revatīṣu vāmadevyena paśukāmaḥ stuvīta
7.9.d: रेवतीषु वामदेव्येन पशुकामः स्तुवीत
7.9.m: One desirous of cattle should chant praise with the Vāmadevya on Revatī verses.

7.9.s: āpo vai revatyaḥ paśavo vāmadevyam adbhya evāsmai paśūn prajanayati
7.9.d: आपो वै रेवत्यः पशवो वामदेव्यम् अद्भ्य एवास्मै पशून् प्रजनयति
7.9.m: The Revatīs are waters; the Vāmadevya is cattle; from the waters indeed he produces cattle for him.

7.9.s: anavartiḥ paśuto bhavati prajā svasya mīliteva bhavati
7.9.d: अनवर्तिः पशुतो भवति प्रजा स्वस्य मीलितेव भवति
7.9.m: There is no turning away from cattle; his offspring becomes, as it were, close-knit.

7.9.s: kavatībhyo hy eti prajāpateḥ
7.9.d: कवतीभ्यो ह्य् एति प्रजापतेः
7.9.m: For it goes from the verses containing 'ka', [which belong] to Prajāpati.

7.10.s: imau vai lokau sahāstāṃ tau viyantāv abrūtāṃv vivāhaṃv vivahāvahai saha nāv astv iti
7.10.d: इमौ वै लोकौ सहास्तां तौ वियन्ताव् अब्रूतांव् विवाहंव् विवहावहै सह नाव् अस्त्व् इति
7.10.m: These two worlds were together. Parting, they said: 'Let us contract a marriage; let there be [a bond] between us!'

7.10.s: tayor ayam amuṣmai śyaitaṃ prāyacchan naudhasam asāv asmai
7.10.d: तयोर् अयम् अमुष्मै श्यैतं प्रायच्छन् नौधसम् असाव् अस्मै
7.10.m: Of the two, this [world] gave the Śyaita to that one; that one [gave] the Naudhasa to this one.

7.10.s: tata enayor nidhane viparyakrāmatāṃ devavivāho vai śyaitanaudhase
7.10.d: तत एनयोर् निधने विपर्यक्रामतां देवविवाहो वै श्यैतनौधसे
7.10.m: Then their cadences crossed over. The Śyaita and the Naudhasa are indeed a divine marriage.

7.10.s: pravasīyāṃsaṃ vivāham āpnoti ya evaṃv veda
7.10.d: प्रवसीयांसं विवाहम् आप्नोति य एवंव् वेद
7.10.m: He obtains a more prosperous marriage, who knows thus.

7.10.s: ito vā ime lokā ūrdhvāḥ kalpamānā yanty amuto 'rvāñcaḥ kalpamānā āyanti
7.10.d: इतो वा इमे लोका ऊर्ध्वाः कल्पमाना यन्त्य् अमुतो ऽर्वाञ्चः कल्पमाना आयन्ति
7.10.m: From here these worlds go upward, ordering themselves; from there they come hitherward, ordering themselves.

7.10.s: yad rathantareṇa stuvantīmaṃl lokaṃ tena yunakty antarikṣaṃv vāmadevyena naudhasenāmuṃ yad bṛhatā stuvanty amuṃl lokaṃ tena yanakty antarikṣaṃv vāmadevyena śyaitenemam
7.10.d: यद् रथन्तरेण स्तुवन्तीमंल् लोकं तेन युनक्त्य् अन्तरिक्षंव् वामदेव्येन नौधसेनामुं यद् बृहता स्तुवन्त्य् अमुंल् लोकं तेन यनक्त्य् अन्तरिक्षंव् वामदेव्येन श्यैतेनेमम्
7.10.m: When they praise with the Rathantara, he yokes this world with it, the intermediate space with the Vāmadevya, that [world] with the Naudhasa. When they praise with the Bṛhat, he yokes that world with it, the intermediate space with the Vāmadevya, this [world] with the Śyaita.

7.10.s: kḷptān imāl lokān upāste ya evaṃv veda
7.10.d: कॢप्तान् इमाल् लोकान् उपास्ते य एवंव् वेद
7.10.m: He attends upon these worlds well-ordered, who knows thus.

7.10.s: bṛhadrathantare vai śaitanaudhase yad rathantarāya naudhasaṃ prati prayuñjanti bṛhad evāsmai tat prati prayuñjanti bṛhad dhy etat paro'kṣaṃ yan naudhasaṃ yad bṛhate śyaitaṃ prati prayuñjanti rathantaram evāsmai tat prati prayuñjanti rathantaraṃ hy etat paro'kṣaṃ yac chyaitam
7.10.d: बृहद्रथन्तरे वै शैतनौधसे यद् रथन्तराय नौधसं प्रति प्रयुञ्जन्ति बृहद् एवास्मै तत् प्रति प्रयुञ्जन्ति बृहद् ध्य् एतत् परोऽक्षं यन् नौधसं यद् बृहते श्यैतं प्रति प्रयुञ्जन्ति रथन्तरम् एवास्मै तत् प्रति प्रयुञ्जन्ति रथन्तरं ह्य् एतत् परोऽक्षं यच् छ्यैतम्
7.10.m: The Śyaita and Naudhasa are indeed the Bṛhat and the Rathantara. When they apply the Naudhasa as a counterpart to the Rathantara, they apply the Bṛhat as a counterpart to it, for what is Naudhasa is cryptically the Bṛhat; when they apply the Śyaita as a counterpart to the Bṛhat, they apply the Rathantara as a counterpart to it, for what is Śyaita is cryptically the Rathantara.

7.10.s: ubhabhyāṃ bṛhadrathantarābhyāṃ stute ya evaṃv veda
7.10.d: उभभ्यां बृहद्रथन्तराभ्यां स्तुते य एवंव् वेद
7.10.m: Praise is chanted for him with both the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, who knows thus.

7.10.s: devā vai brahma vyabhajanta tāṃ nodhāḥ kākṣīvata āgacchat te 'bruvann ṛṣir na āgaṃs tasmai brahma dadāmeti tasmā etat sāma prāyacchaṃs tasmān naudhasaṃ brahma vai naudhasam
7.10.d: देवा वै ब्रह्म व्यभजन्त तां नोधाः काक्षीवत आगच्छत् ते ऽब्रुवन्न् ऋषिर् न आगंस् तस्मै ब्रह्म ददामेति तस्मा एतत् साम प्रायच्छंस् तस्मान् नौधसं ब्रह्म वै नौधसम्
7.10.m: The gods divided the sacred word. Nodhās, son of Kakṣīvat, approached them. They said: 'A seer has come to us; let us give him the sacred word.' They gave him this sāman; therefore it is called Naudhasa; the Naudhasa is indeed the sacred word.
One desirous of brahminical lustre should chant praise with this; he becomes endowed with brahminical lustre.

7.10.s: prajāpatiḥ paśūn asṛjata te 'smāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tān etena sāmnābhivyāharat te 'smā atiṣṭhanta te śetyā abhavan yac chetyā abhavaṃs tasmāc chyaitaṃ paśavo vai śyaitam
7.10.d: प्रजापतिः पशून् असृजत ते ऽस्मात् सृष्टा अपाक्रामंस् तान् एतेन साम्नाभिव्याहरत् ते ऽस्मा अतिष्ठन्त ते शेत्या अभवन् यच् छेत्या अभवंस् तस्माच् छ्यैतं पशवो वै श्यैतम्
7.10.m: Prajāpati created cattle. Having been created, they departed from him. He addressed them with this sāman. They stood still for him; they became docile. Because they became docile, therefore it is [called] the Śyaita. The Śyaita is indeed cattle.
One who desires cattle should chant with this; he becomes rich in cattle.

7.10.s: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭā aśocaṃs tāḥ śyaitena huṃmā ity abhyajighrat tato vai tāḥ samaidhanta samedhante tāṃ samāṃ prajā yatraivaṃ vidvāñ chyaitenodgāyati
7.10.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ताः सृष्टा अशोचंस् ताः श्यैतेन हुंमा इत्य् अभ्यजिघ्रत् ततो वै ताः समैधन्त समेधन्ते तां समां प्रजा यत्रैवं विद्वाञ् छ्यैतेनोद्गायति
7.10.m: Prajāpati created creatures. Having been created, they grieved. He sniffed at them with the Śyaita, saying 'huṃ-mā'. Then indeed they thrived. The creatures thrive for that year in which one who knows thus sings the udgītha with the Śyaita.

7.10.s: eṣa vai yajamānasya prajāpatir yad udgātā yac chyaitena hiṅ karoti prajāpatir eva bhūtvā prajā abhijihgrati
7.10.d: एष वै यजमानस्य प्रजापतिर् यद् उद्गाता यच् छ्यैतेन हिङ् करोति प्रजापतिर् एव भूत्वा प्रजा अभिजिह्ग्रति
7.10.m: The udgātṛ is indeed the Prajāpati of the sacrificer. In that he makes the sound 'hiṅ' with the Śyaita, he sniffs at the creatures, having himself become Prajāpati.

7.10.s: vasunidhanaṃ bhavati paśavo vai vasu paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
7.10.d: वसुनिधनं भवति पशवो वै वसु पशुष्व् एव प्रतितिष्ठति
7.10.m: It has 'vasu' as its cadence. Cattle are indeed wealth. He firmly establishes himself in cattle.

8.1.s: āṣkāraṇidhanaṃ kāṇvaṃv vaṣaṭkāraṇidhanam abhicaraṇīyasya brahmasāma kuryād abhinidhanaṃ mādhyandine pavamāne
8.1.d: आष्कारणिधनं काण्वंव् वषट्कारणिधनम् अभिचरणीयस्य ब्रह्मसाम कुर्याद् अभिनिधनं माध्यन्दिने पवमाने
8.1.m: One should make the Kāṇva [sāman] with the āṣ-sound as its cadence, or with the vaṣaṭ-call as its cadence, the Brahman's chant for one practicing sorcery, [or make it] with 'abhi' as its cadence in the mid-day Pavamāna.

8.1.s: deveṣur vā eṣā yad vaṣatkāro 'bhīti vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharad abhītyevāsmai vajraṃ prahṛtya deveṣv ā vaṣaṭkāreṇa vidhyati
8.1.d: देवेषुर् वा एषा यद् वषत्कारो ऽभीति वा इन्द्रो वृत्राय वज्रं प्राहरद् अभीत्येवास्मै वज्रं प्रहृत्य देवेष्व् आ वषट्कारेण विध्यति
8.1.m: The vaṣaṭ-call is indeed an arrow of the gods. Saying 'abhi' (forth!), Indra hurled his thunderbolt at Vṛtra. Having hurled the thunderbolt at him, saying 'abhi', he pierces him with the arrow of the gods by means of the vaṣaṭ-call.

8.1.s: traikakubhaṃ paśukāmāya brahmasāma kuryāt tvam aṅga praśaṃsiṣa ity etāsu
8.1.d: त्रैककुभं पशुकामाय ब्रह्मसाम कुर्यात् त्वम् अङ्ग प्रशंसिष इत्य् एतासु
8.1.m: One should make the Traikakubha the Brahman's chant for one who desires cattle, on these [verses beginning]: 'Do you indeed, O most mighty god, praise a mortal?'

8.1.s: indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat teṣāṃ traya udaśiṣyanta rāyovājo bṛhadgiriḥ pṛthuraśmis te 'bruvan ko naḥ putrān bhariṣyantīty aham intīndro 'bravīt tāṃs trikakub adhinidhāyācarat sa etat sāmāpaśyad yat trikakub apaśyat tasmāt traikakubham
8.1.d: इन्द्रो यतीन् सालावृकेभ्यः प्रायच्छत् तेषां त्रय उदशिष्यन्त रायोवाजो बृहद्गिरिः पृथुरश्मिस् ते ऽब्रुवन् को नः पुत्रान् भरिष्यन्तीत्य् अहम् इन्तीन्द्रो ऽब्रवीत् तांस् त्रिककुब् अधिनिधायाचरत् स एतत् सामापश्यद् यत् त्रिककुब् अपश्यत् तस्मात् त्रैककुभम्
8.1.m: Indra handed over the ascetics to the hyenas. Three of them were left over: Rāyovāja, Bṛhadgiri, and Pṛthuraśmi. They said: 'Who will support us, our sons?' 'I shall,' said Indra. Placing them on three peaks, he went about. He saw this sāman. Because he saw it on three peaks, therefore it is [called] the Traikakubha.

8.1.s: sa ātmānam eva punar upādhāvat tvam aṅga praśaṃsiṣo devaḥ śaviṣṭha martyaṃ na tvad anyo maghavann asti ca marḍitendra bravīmi te vaca iti sa etena ca pragāthenaitena sāmnā sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata tān ebhyaḥ prāyacchat te pratyatiṣṭhan
8.1.d: स आत्मानम् एव पुनर् उपाधावत् त्वम् अङ्ग प्रशंसिषो देवः शविष्ठ मर्त्यं न त्वद् अन्यो मघवन्न् अस्ति च मर्डितेन्द्र ब्रवीमि ते वच इति स एतेन च प्रगाथेनैतेन साम्ना सहस्रं पशून् असृजत तान् एभ्यः प्रायच्छत् ते प्रत्यतिष्ठन्
8.1.m: He took refuge in himself again: 'Do you indeed, O most mighty god, praise a mortal? There is no other comforter than you, O Maghavan; O Indra, I speak your word.' With this pragātha and with this sāman he created a thousand cattle. He gave them to these [three]. They became firmly established.

8.1.s: yaḥ paśukāmaḥ syād yah pratiṣṭhākāma etasmin pragātha etena sāmnā stuvīta pra sahasraṃ paśūn āpnoti pratitiṣṭhati
8.1.d: यः पशुकामः स्याद् यह् प्रतिष्ठाकाम एतस्मिन् प्रगाथ एतेन साम्ना स्तुवीत प्र सहस्रं पशून् आप्नोति प्रतितिष्ठति
8.1.m: He who desires cattle, he who desires firm standing, should chant with this sāman on this pragātha; he obtains a thousand cattle, he becomes firmly established.

8.1.s: trivīryaṃ vā etat sāma trīndriyam aindrya ṛca aindraṃ sāmaindreti nidhanam indriya eva vīrye pratitiṣṭhati
8.1.d: त्रिवीर्यं वा एतत् साम त्रीन्द्रियम् ऐन्द्र्य ऋच ऐन्द्रं सामैन्द्रेति निधनम् इन्द्रिय एव वीर्ये प्रतितिष्ठति
8.1.m: This sāman has threefold strength, threefold power: the verse belongs to Indra, the sāman belongs to Indra, and the cadence is 'o Indra'. He becomes firmly established in power, in strength.
One should make the Traiśoka the Brahman's chant for one who has been long diseased.

8.1.s: ime vai lokāḥ sahāsaṃs te 'śocantaṃs teṣām indra etena sāmnā śucam apāhan yat trayāṇāṃ śocatām apāhaṃs tasmāt traiśokam
8.1.d: इमे वै लोकाः सहासंस् ते ऽशोचन्तंस् तेषाम् इन्द्र एतेन साम्ना शुचम् अपाहन् यत् त्रयाणां शोचताम् अपाहंस् तस्मात् त्रैशोकम्
8.1.m: These worlds were together; they grieved. Indra struck away their grief with this sāman. Because he struck away the grief of the three grieving ones, therefore it is [called] the Traiśoka.

8.1.s: yāsmād apāhan sā puṃścalīṃ prāviśad yām antarikṣāt sā klībaṃ yām amuṣmāt sainasvinam
8.1.d: यास्माद् अपाहन् सा पुंश्चलीं प्राविशद् याम् अन्तरिक्षात् सा क्लीबं याम् अमुष्मात् सैनस्विनम्
8.1.m: The [grief] that he struck away from this [earth] entered an unchaste woman; that from the intermediate space [entered] a eunuch; that from yonder [sky entered] a sinner.

8.1.s: tasmāt teṣāṃ nāśaitavyā ya eṣām āśāmeti tasmā eva śuco 'pabhajate
8.1.d: तस्मात् तेषां नाशैतव्या य एषाम् आशामेति तस्मा एव शुचो ऽपभजते
8.1.m: Therefore one should not eat of their [food]. Whoever eats of their [food] partakes of that very grief.

8.1.s: śucā vā eṣa viddho yasya jyog āmayati yat traiśokaṃ brahmasāma bhavati śucam evāsmād apahanti
8.1.d: शुचा वा एष विद्धो यस्य ज्योग् आमयति यत् त्रैशोकं ब्रह्मसाम भवति शुचम् एवास्माद् अपहन्ति
8.1.m: He who is long diseased is pierced by grief. In that the Traiśoka is the Brahman's chant, he strikes away grief from him.

8.1.s: diveti nidhanam upayanti vyuṣṭir vai divā vy evāsmai vāsayati
8.1.d: दिवेति निधनम् उपयन्ति व्युष्टिर् वै दिवा व्य् एवास्मै वासयति
8.1.m: They sing with 'divā' ('by day') as the cadence. 'Divā' is dawn; it dawns for him.

8.2.m: One should make the Kāṇva [sāman] with the āṣ-sound as its cadence the Brahman's chant for one who desires firm standing.

8.2.s: kaṇvo vā etat sāmarte nidhanam apaśyat sa na pratyatiṣṭhat sa vṛṣadaṃśasyāṣiti kṣuvata upāśṛṇot sa tad eva nidhanam apaśyat tato vai sa pratyatiṣṭhad yad etat sāma bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
8.2.d: कण्वो वा एतत् सामर्ते निधनम् अपश्यत् स न प्रत्यतिष्ठत् स वृषदंशस्याषिति क्षुवत उपाशृणोत् स तद् एव निधनम् अपश्यत् ततो वै स प्रत्यतिष्ठद् यद् एतत् साम भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै
8.2.m: Kaṇva saw this sāman without a cadence; he did not become firmly established. He heard a tom-cat sneezing 'āṣ'. He saw that very cadence. Then indeed he became firmly established. That this sāman is [employed] is for firm standing.
One should make Vasiṣṭha's Janitra the Brahman's chant for one who desires offspring.

8.2.s: vasiṣṭho vā etat putrahataḥ sāmāpaśyat sa prajayā paśubhiḥ prājāyata yad etat sāma bhavati prajātyai
8.2.d: वसिष्ठो वा एतत् पुत्रहतः सामापश्यत् स प्रजया पशुभिः प्राजायत यद् एतत् साम भवति प्रजात्यै
8.2.m: Vasiṣṭha, his sons having been slain, saw this sāman. He propagated with offspring and cattle. That this sāman is [employed] is for propagation.
One should make the Ātharvaṇa the Brahman's chant for one who desires a world.

8.2.s: atharvāṇo vā etal lokākāmāḥ sāmāpaśyaṃs tenāmartyaṃl lokam apaśyan yad etat sāma bhavati svargasya lokasya prajātyai
8.2.d: अथर्वाणो वा एतल् लोकाकामाः सामापश्यंस् तेनामर्त्यंल् लोकम् अपश्यन् यद् एतत् साम भवति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य प्रजात्यै
8.2.m: The Atharvans, desiring a world, saw this sāman; through it they saw the immortal world. That this sāman is [employed] is for the propagation of the heavenly world.
One should make the Abhīvarta the Brahman's chant for one who has a rival.

8.2.s: abhīvartena vai devā asurān abhyavartanta yad abhīvarto brahmasāma bhavati bhrātṛvyasyābhivṛtyai
8.2.d: अभीवर्तेन वै देवा असुरान् अभ्यवर्तन्त यद् अभीवर्तो ब्रह्मसाम भवति भ्रातृव्यस्याभिवृत्यै
8.2.m: By means of the Abhīvarta the gods approached and overcame the Asuras. That the Abhīvarta is the Brahman's chant is for overcoming the rival.
One should make the Śrāyantīya the Brahman's chant for one who has fallen away from the sacrifice.

8.2.s: prajāpatir uṣasam adhyait svāṃ duhitaraṃ tasya retaḥ parāpatat tad asyāṃ nyaṣicyata tad aśrīṇād idaṃ me mā duṣad iti tat sad akarot paśūn eva
8.2.d: प्रजापतिर् उषसम् अध्यैत् स्वां दुहितरं तस्य रेतः परापतत् तद् अस्यां न्यषिच्यत तद् अश्रीणाद् इदं मे मा दुषद् इति तत् सद् अकरोत् पशून् एव
8.2.m: Prajāpati approached the Dawn, his own daughter. His semen fell away; it was poured out upon her. He mixed it, [thinking]: 'Let this of mine not be spoiled.' He made it real, namely, cattle.

8.2.s: yac chrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma bhavati śrīṇāti caivenaṃ sac ca karoti
8.2.d: यच् छ्रायन्तीयं ब्रह्मसाम भवति श्रीणाति चैवेनं सच् च करोति
8.2.m: In that the Śrāyantīya is the Brahman's chant, he mixes it and makes him real.

8.3.s: devāś ca vā asurāś caiṣu lokeṣv aspardhanta te devāḥ prajāpatim upādhāvaṃs tebhya etat sāma prāyacchad etenainān kālayiṣyaddham iti tenainān ebhyo lokebhyo 'kālayanta yad akālayanta tasmāt kāleyam
8.3.d: देवाश् च वा असुराश् चैषु लोकेष्व् अस्पर्धन्त ते देवाः प्रजापतिम् उपाधावंस् तेभ्य एतत् साम प्रायच्छद् एतेनैनान् कालयिष्यद्धम् इति तेनैनान् एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽकालयन्त यद् अकालयन्त तस्मात् कालेयम्
8.3.m: The gods and the Asuras were contending for these worlds. The gods ran up to Prajāpati. He gave them this sāman, [saying]: 'With this you shall drive them away.' With it they drove them away from these worlds. Because they drove them away (akālayanta), therefore it is [called] the Kāleya.

8.3.s: ebhyo vai lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ kālayate ya evaṃv veda
8.3.d: एभ्यो वै लोकेभ्यो भ्रातृव्यं कालयते य एवंव् वेद
8.3.m: He drives away his rival from these worlds who knows thus.

8.3.s: stomo vai deveṣu taro nāmāsīd yajño 'sureṣu vidadvasus te devās tarobhir vo vidadvasum iti stomena yajñam asurāṇām āvṛñjata
8.3.d: स्तोमो वै देवेषु तरो नामासीद् यज्ञो ऽसुरेषु विदद्वसुस् ते देवास् तरोभिर् वो विदद्वसुम् इति स्तोमेन यज्ञम् असुराणाम् आवृञ्जत
8.3.m: Among the gods there was a stoma named 'Taras'; among the Asuras the sacrifice was 'Vidadvasu'. The gods, with the verse 'With their speeds, Vidadvasu for you', seized the sacrifice of the Asuras by means of the stoma.

8.3.s: stomena yajñaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
8.3.d: स्तोमेन यज्ञं भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते य एवंव् वेद
8.3.m: He seizes the sacrifice of his rival by means of the stoma who knows thus.

8.3.s: sāhdyā vai nāma devā āsaṃs te 'vacchidya tṛtīyasavanaṃ mādhyandinena savanena saha svargaṃl lokam āyaṃs tad devāḥ lokeyena samatanvan yat kāleyaṃ bhavati tṛtīyasavanasya saṃtatyai
8.3.d: साह्द्या वै नाम देवा आसंस् ते ऽवच्छिद्य तृतीयसवनं माध्यन्दिनेन सवनेन सह स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयंस् तद् देवाः लोकेयेन समतन्वन् यत् कालेयं भवति तृतीयसवनस्य संतत्यै
8.3.m: There were gods named Sādhyas. Having cut off the third pressing together with the mid-day pressing, they went to the heavenly world. The gods then continued it by means of the [Kā]leya. That the Kāleya is [employed] is for the continuity of the third pressing.

8.3.s: vidadvasu vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ yat tarobhir vo vidadvasum iti prastauti tṛtīyasavanam eva tad abhyativadati
8.3.d: विदद्वसु वै तृतीयसवनं यत् तरोभिर् वो विदद्वसुम् इति प्रस्तौति तृतीयसवनम् एव तद् अभ्यतिवदति
8.3.m: Vidadvasu is indeed the third pressing. In that he chants the prastāva with 'With their speeds, Vidadvasu for you', he thereby addresses the third pressing.

8.3.s: sarvāṇi vai rūpāṇi kāleyaṃ yat padaprastāvaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ yad bṛhato rohān rohati tena bārhataṃ yat stobhavān pratihāras tena bārhataṃ yad dravadiḍaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ sarveṣv eva rūpeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
8.3.d: सर्वाणि वै रूपाणि कालेयं यत् पदप्रस्तावं तेन राथन्तरं यद् बृहतो रोहान् रोहति तेन बार्हतं यत् स्तोभवान् प्रतिहारस् तेन बार्हतं यद् द्रवदिडं तेन राथन्तरं सर्वेष्व् एव रूपेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
8.3.m: The Kāleya has all characteristics. In that it has the prastāva of a quarter-verse, it has the nature of the Rathantara; in that it ascends the ascents of the Bṛhat, it has the nature of the Bṛhat; in that the pratihāra has a stobha, it has the nature of the Bṛhat; in that it has a running iḍā, it has the nature of the Rathantara. He becomes firmly established in all forms.

8.4.s: sādhyā vai nāma devā āsaṃs te sarveṇa yajñena saha svargaṃl lokam āyaṃs te devāśīchandāṃsy abruvan somam āharateti te jagatīṃ prāhiṇvan sā trīṇy akṣarāṇi hitvaikākṣarā bhūtvāgacchat triṣṭubhaṃ prāhiṇvan saikam akṣaraṃ hitvā tryakṣarā bhūtvāgacchad gāyatrīṃ prāhiṇvaṃś caturakṣarāṇi vai tarhi cchandāṃsy āsan sā tāni cākṣarāṇi haranty āgacchad aṣṭākṣarā bhūtvā trīṇi ca savanāni hastābhyāṃ dve savane dantair daṃṣṭvā tṛtīyasavanaṃ tasmād dve aṃśumatī savane dhītaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ dantair hi tad daṃṣṭvā dhayanty aharat tasya ye hriyamāṇasyāṃśavaḥ parāpataṃs te pūtīkā abhavan yāni puṣpāṇy avāśīyanta tāny arjjunāni yat prāprothat te praprothās tasmāt tṛtīyasavana āśiram avanayanti yam eva taṃ gāvaḥ somam adanti tasya taṃ rasam avanayanti sasomatvāya
8.4.d: साध्या वै नाम देवा आसंस् ते सर्वेण यज्ञेन सह स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयंस् ते देवाशीछन्दांस्य् अब्रुवन् सोमम् आहरतेति ते जगतीं प्राहिण्वन् सा त्रीण्य् अक्षराणि हित्वैकाक्षरा भूत्वागच्छत् त्रिष्टुभं प्राहिण्वन् सैकम् अक्षरं हित्वा त्र्यक्षरा भूत्वागच्छद् गायत्रीं प्राहिण्वंश् चतुरक्षराणि वै तर्हि च्छन्दांस्य् आसन् सा तानि चाक्षराणि हरन्त्य् आगच्छद् अष्टाक्षरा भूत्वा त्रीणि च सवनानि हस्ताभ्यां द्वे सवने दन्तैर् दंष्ट्वा तृतीयसवनं तस्माद् द्वे अंशुमती सवने धीतं तृतीयसवनं दन्तैर् हि तद् दंष्ट्वा धयन्त्य् अहरत् तस्य ये ह्रियमाणस्यांशवः परापतंस् ते पूतीका अभवन् यानि पुष्पाण्य् अवाशीयन्त तान्य् अर्ज्जुनानि यत् प्राप्रोथत् ते प्रप्रोथास् तस्मात् तृतीयसवन आशिरम् अवनयन्ति यम् एव तं गावः सोमम् अदन्ति तस्य तं रसम् अवनयन्ति ससोमत्वाय
8.4.m: The gods named Sādhyas indeed existed. They went to the world of heaven together with the entire sacrifice. Those gods said to the metres: 'Fetch the Soma.' They sent the jagatī. Leaving three syllables behind, having become one syllable, she returned. They sent the triṣṭubh. Leaving one syllable behind, having become three syllables, she returned. They sent the gāyatrī. In those days, indeed, the metres were four-syllabled. She returned carrying those syllables, having become eight-syllabled, and the three pressings: two pressings with her two hands, [and] clamping the third pressing with her teeth. Therefore, two pressings are with shoots, [and] the third pressing is sucked, for she carried it away clamping it with her teeth and sucking it. The shoots of it that fell off as it was being carried, they became pūtīka plants; the flowers that dropped off, they became arjuna trees; what snorted forth, that became the praprothas. Therefore, at the third pressing, they pour on the milk-mixture. The very essence of that Soma which the cows eat, they pour in for the sake of its having [its full] Soma-nature.

8.4.s: te triṣṭub jagatyai gāyatrīm abrūtām upa tvāyāveti sābravīt kiṃ me tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayasa ity abrūtāṃ sābvravīn mama sarvaṃ prātaḥsavanam aham uttare savane praṇayānīti tasmād gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ gāyatry uttare savane praṇayati
8.4.d: ते त्रिष्टुब् जगत्यै गायत्रीम् अब्रूताम् उप त्वायावेति साब्रवीत् किं मे ततः स्याद् इति यत् कामयस इत्य् अब्रूतां साब्व्रवीन् मम सर्वं प्रातःसवनम् अहम् उत्तरे सवने प्रणयानीति तस्माद् गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं गायत्र्य् उत्तरे सवने प्रणयति
8.4.m: The triṣṭubh and the jagatī said to the gāyatrī: 'Let us two come along to you.' She said: 'What would be mine from that?' They said: 'Whatever you desire.' She said: 'All the morning pressing shall be mine, [and] I shall lead on the two subsequent pressings.' Therefore, the morning pressing belongs to the gāyatrī; the gāyatrī leads on the two subsequent pressings.

8.4.s: tān triṣṭup tribhir akṣarair upait saikādaśākṣarā bhūtvā prājāyata tāṃ jagaty ekenākṣareṇopait sā dvādaśākṣarā bhūtvā prājāyata
8.4.d: तान् त्रिष्टुप् त्रिभिर् अक्षरैर् उपैत् सैकादशाक्षरा भूत्वा प्राजायत तां जगत्य् एकेनाक्षरेणोपैत् सा द्वादशाक्षरा भूत्वा प्राजायत
8.4.m: The triṣṭubh approached her with three syllables; having become eleven-syllabled, she brought forth offspring. The jagatī approached her with one syllable; having become twelve-syllabled, she brought forth offspring.

8.4.s: tasmād āhur gāyatrī vāva sarvāṇi cchandāṃsi gāyatrī hy etān poṣān puṣyanty aid iti
8.4.d: तस्माद् आहुर् गायत्री वाव सर्वाणि च्छन्दांसि गायत्री ह्य् एतान् पोषान् पुष्यन्त्य् ऐद् इति
8.4.m: Therefore, they say: 'The gāyatrī indeed is all the metres, for the gāyatrī went on nourishing these nourishments.'

8.4.s: indras tṛtīyasavanād bībhatsamāna udakrāmat tad devāḥ svādiṣṭhayeti asvadayan madiṣṭhayeti madvad akurvan pavasva soma dhārayety apāvayann indrāya pātave suta iti tato vai tad indra upāvartata yat svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayeti prastauti tṛtīyasavanasya sendratvāya
8.4.d: इन्द्रस् तृतीयसवनाद् बीभत्समान उदक्रामत् तद् देवाः स्वादिष्ठयेति अस्वदयन् मदिष्ठयेति मद्वद् अकुर्वन् पवस्व सोम धारयेत्य् अपावयन्न् इन्द्राय पातवे सुत इति ततो वै तद् इन्द्र उपावर्तत यत् स्वादिष्ठया मदिष्ठयेति प्रस्तौति तृतीयसवनस्य सेन्द्रत्वाय
8.4.m: Indra stepped forth from the third pressing, feeling disgust. The gods made it sweet with [the verse]: 'With the sweetest' [SV 1.468]; they made it exhilarating with [the words]: 'with the most exhilarating'; they purified it with: 'purify yourself, O Soma, in a stream'; [they brought him back] with: 'pressed for Indra to drink.' Thereupon indeed Indra turned back to it. When he introduces [the chant] with 'With the sweetest, with the most exhilarating,' it is to provide the third pressing with Indra.

8.4.s: svādiṣṭhā vai deveṣu paśava āsan madiṣṭhā asureṣu te devāḥ svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayeti paśūn asurāṇām avṛñjata
8.4.d: स्वादिष्ठा वै देवेषु पशव आसन् मदिष्ठा असुरेषु ते देवाः स्वादिष्ठया मदिष्ठयेति पशून् असुराणाम् अवृञ्जत
8.4.m: The sweetest cattle indeed were among the gods, the most exhilarating among the asuras. The gods, with 'the sweetest, the most exhilarating,' wrested away the cattle of the asuras.

8.4.s: paśūn bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
8.4.d: पशून् भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते य एवंव् वेद
8.4.m: He wrests away the cattle of his rival who knows thus.

8.4.s: sādhyā vai nāmadevā āsaṃs te 'vacchidya tṛtīyasavanaṃ mādhyandinena savanena saha svargaṃl lokam āyaṃs tad devāḥ saṃhitena samadadhur yat samadadhus tasmāt saṃhitam
8.4.d: साध्या वै नामदेवा आसंस् ते ऽवच्छिद्य तृतीयसवनं माध्यन्दिनेन सवनेन सह स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयंस् तद् देवाः संहितेन समदधुर् यत् समदधुस् तस्मात् संहितम्
8.4.m: The gods named Sādhyas indeed existed. Having severed the third pressing, they went to the world of heaven along with the midday pressing. The gods joined it together with the Saṃhita. Because they joined it together, therefore it is the Saṃhita.

8.4.s: kāleyaṃ purastād bhavati saṃhitam upariṣṭād etābhyāṃ hi tṛtīyasavanaṃ saṃtāyate
8.4.d: कालेयं पुरस्ताद् भवति संहितम् उपरिष्टाद् एताभ्यां हि तृतीयसवनं संतायते
8.4.m: The Kāleya is in front; the Saṃhita is above. For by these two the third pressing is held together.

8.4.s: sarvāṇi vai rūpāṇi saṃhitaṃ yat padaprastāvaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ yad bṛhato rohān rohati tena bārhataṃ yad padanidhanaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ sarveṣv eva rūpeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
8.4.d: सर्वाणि वै रूपाणि संहितं यत् पदप्रस्तावं तेन राथन्तरं यद् बृहतो रोहान् रोहति तेन बार्हतं यद् पदनिधनं तेन राथन्तरं सर्वेष्व् एव रूपेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
8.4.m: All forms indeed are the Saṃhita. In that its introduction consists of a verse-quarter, thereby it has the character of the Rathantara; in that it ascends the ascents of the Bṛhat, thereby it has the character of the Bṛhat; in that its cadence consists of a verse-quarter, thereby it has the character of the Rathantara. He firmly establishes himself in all forms.

8.5.m: These two [metres], the uṣṇih and the kakubh, are [used here].
