8.5.s: uṣṇikkakubbhyāṃ vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat kakubhi parākramatoṣṇihā prāharat tasmāt kakubho madhyamaṃ padaṃ bhūyiṣṭhākṣaraṃ parākramaṇaṃ hi tad abhi samauhat tasmād uṣṇiha uttamaṃ padaṃ bhūyiṣṭhākṣaraṃ puro gurur iva hi vajraḥ
8.5.d: उष्णिक्ककुब्भ्यां वा इन्द्रो वृत्राय वज्रं प्राहरत् ककुभि पराक्रमतोष्णिहा प्राहरत् तस्मात् ककुभो मध्यमं पदं भूयिष्ठाक्षरं पराक्रमणं हि तद् अभि समौहत् तस्माद् उष्णिह उत्तमं पदं भूयिष्ठाक्षरं पुरो गुरुर् इव हि वज्रः
8.5.m: With the uṣṇih and the kakubh, Indra hurled the vajra at Vṛtra. Stepping forward on the kakubh, he struck with the uṣṇih. Therefore, the middle verse-quarter of the kakubh has the most syllables, for it gathered itself for the stepping forward. Therefore, the last verse-quarter of the uṣṇih has the most syllables, for the vajra is as if heavy in front.

8.5.s: vajraṃ bhrātṛvyāya praharati ya evaṃv veda
8.5.d: वज्रं भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति य एवंव् वेद
8.5.m: He hurls the vajra at his rival who knows thus.

8.5.s: nāsike vā ete yajñasya yad uṣṇikkakubhau tasmāt samānaṃ chandaḥ satī nānā yajñaṃv vahatas tasmāt samānāyā nāsikāyāḥ satyā nānā prāṇāv uccarataḥ
8.5.d: नासिके वा एते यज्ञस्य यद् उष्णिक्ककुभौ तस्मात् समानं छन्दः सती नाना यज्ञंव् वहतस् तस्मात् समानाया नासिकायाः सत्या नाना प्राणाव् उच्चरतः
8.5.m: These two, the uṣṇih and the kakubh, are indeed the two nostrils of the sacrifice. Therefore, being of the same metre, they carry the sacrifice variously. Therefore, the two nostrils being the same, the two breaths go forth variously.

8.5.s: prāṇā vā uṣṇikkakubhau tasmāt tābhyāṃ na vaṣaṭ kurvanti yad vaṣaṭ kuryuḥ prāṇān agnau pradadhyuḥ
8.5.d: प्राणा वा उष्णिक्ककुभौ तस्मात् ताभ्यां न वषट् कुर्वन्ति यद् वषट् कुर्युः प्राणान् अग्नौ प्रदध्युः
8.5.m: The uṣṇih and the kakubh are indeed the breaths. Therefore, they do not pronounce the vaṣaṭ-call with them. If they were to pronounce the vaṣaṭ-call, they would place the breaths into the fire.

8.5.s: tāsu saphaṃ vipham iva vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ tṛtīyasavanasya saphatvāyāthauṣkalam etena vai prajāpatiḥ puṣkalān paśūn asṛjata teṣu rūpam adadhād yad etat sāma bhavati paśuṣv eva rūpaṃ dadhāti
8.5.d: तासु सफं विफम् इव वै तृतीयसवनं तृतीयसवनस्य सफत्वायाथौष्कलम् एतेन वै प्रजापतिः पुष्कलान् पशून् असृजत तेषु रूपम् अदधाद् यद् एतत् साम भवति पशुष्व् एव रूपं दधाति
8.5.m: On these [verses is chanted] the Sapha [sāman]. The third pressing is, as it were, hooffless; [this is done] for the third pressing's having hooves. Then the Auṣkala [sāman]. By this Prajāpati created copious cattle; he placed form into them. In that this sāman is [used], he places form in cattle.

8.5.s: purojitī vo andhasa iti padyā cākṣaryā ca virājau bhavataḥ padyayā vai devāḥ svargaṃl lokam āyann akṣaryayā ṛṣayo nu prājānān yad ete padyā cākṣaryā ca virājau bhavataḥ svargasya lokasya prajñātyai
8.5.d: पुरोजिती वो अन्धस इति पद्या चाक्षर्या च विराजौ भवतः पद्यया वै देवाः स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयन्न् अक्षर्यया ऋषयो नु प्राजानान् यद् एते पद्या चाक्षर्या च विराजौ भवतः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य प्रज्ञात्यै
8.5.m: [On the verses beginning] 'With your ancient liquor' [SV 1.470], there are two virāj [verses], one measured by feet and one measured by syllables. By the one measured by feet, the gods went to the world of heaven; by the one measured by syllables, the ṛṣis perceived it. In that these two virāj [verses], one measured by feet and one measured by syllables, are [used], it is for the discernment of the world of heaven.

8.5.s: śyāvāśvam ārvanānasaṃ sattram āsīnaṃ dhanvodavahan sa etat sāmāpaśyat tena vṛṣṭim asṛjata tato vai sa pratyatiṣṭhat tato gātum avindata gātuvid vā etat sāma
8.5.d: श्यावाश्वम् आर्वनानसं सत्त्रम् आसीनं धन्वोदवहन् स एतत् सामापश्यत् तेन वृष्टिम् असृजत ततो वै स प्रत्यतिष्ठत् ततो गातुम् अविन्दत गातुविद् वा एतत् साम
8.5.m: When Śyāvāśva Ārvanānasa was engaged in a sacrificial session, the water carried him off into the desert. He saw this sāman. By it, he created rain. Thereupon indeed he firmly established himself; thereupon he found a path. A path-finding [sāman] indeed is this sāman.
He finds a path, he establishes himself firmly, who has praised with this.

8.5.s: indras tṛtīyasavanād bībhatsamāna udakrāmat taṃ devāḥ śyāvāślvenaihāyi ehiyety anvāhvayan sa upāvartata yad etat sāma bhavati tṛtīyasavanasya sendratvāya
8.5.d: इन्द्रस् तृतीयसवनाद् बीभत्समान उदक्रामत् तं देवाः श्यावाश्ल्वेनैहायि एहियेत्य् अन्वाह्वयन् स उपावर्तत यद् एतत् साम भवति तृतीयसवनस्य सेन्द्रत्वाय
8.5.m: Indra stepped forth from the third pressing, feeling disgust. The gods called after him with the Śyāvāśva [sāman]: 'O come hither, come hither!' He turned back. In that this sāman is [used], it is to provide the third pressing with Indra.

8.5.s: athaitad āndhīgavam andhīgur vā etat paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai madhye nidhanam aiḍaṃ bhavaty etena vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yan madhye nidhanam aiḍaṃ na syād apratiṣṭhitaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ syāt
8.5.d: अथैतद् आन्धीगवम् अन्धीगुर् वा एतत् पशुकामः सामापश्यत् तेन सहस्रं पशून् असृजत यद् एतत् साम भवति पशूनां पुष्ट्यै मध्ये निधनम् ऐडं भवत्य् एतेन वै तृतीयसवनं प्रतिष्ठितं यन् मध्ये निधनम् ऐडं न स्याद् अप्रतिष्ठितं तृतीयसवनं स्यात्
8.5.m: Now this Āndhīgava [sāman]. Andhīgu, desiring cattle, saw this sāman. By it he created a thousand cattle. In that this sāman is [used], it is for the flourishing of cattle. In the middle, the cadence contains the word 'iḍā'. By this indeed the third pressing is firmly established. If the cadence containing 'iḍā' were not in the middle, the third pressing would be without firm support.

8.5.s: daśākṣaraṃ madhyato nidhanam upayanti daśākṣarā virāḍ virājy eva pratitiṣṭhati
8.5.d: दशाक्षरं मध्यतो निधनम् उपयन्ति दशाक्षरा विराड् विराज्य् एव प्रतितिष्ठति
8.5.m: They undertake the ten-syllabled cadence in the middle. The virāj has ten syllables. He firmly establishes himself in the virāj.

8.5.s: abhi priyāṇi pavata iti kāvaṃ prājāpatyaṃ sāma
8.5.d: अभि प्रियाणि पवत इति कावं प्राजापत्यं साम
8.5.m: [On the verse beginning] 'He purifies himself towards what is dear' [SV 1.471] is the Kāva [sāman], belonging to Prajāpati.

8.5.s: prajā vai priyāṇi paśavaḥ priyāṇi prajāyām eva paśuṣu pratitiṣtśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
8.5.d: प्रजा वै प्रियाणि पशवः प्रियाणि प्रजायाम् एव पशुषु प्रतितिष्त्शुषु प्रतितिष्ठति
8.5.m: Offspring are what is dear; cattle are what is dear. He firmly establishes himself in offspring, in cattle.

8.5.s: raśmī vā etau yajñasya yad auśanakāve devakośo vā eṣa yajñam abhisamubjito yad ete antato bhavato yajñasyāriṣṭyai
8.5.d: रश्मी वा एतौ यज्ञस्य यद् औशनकावे देवकोशो वा एष यज्ञम् अभिसमुब्जितो यद् एते अन्ततो भवतो यज्ञस्यारिष्ट्यै
8.5.m: The Auśana and the Kāva are indeed the two reins of the sacrifice. This divine container holds the sacrifice enclosed. In that these two are at the end, it is for the uninjured state of the sacrifice.

8.6.s: devā vai brahma vyabhajanta tasya yo raso 'tyaricyata tad yajñāyajñīyam abhavat
8.6.d: देवा वै ब्रह्म व्यभजन्त तस्य यो रसो ऽत्यरिच्यत तद् यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अभवत्
8.6.m: The gods divided the sacred word. Whatever sap of it was left over, that became the Yajñāyajñīya [sāman].

8.6.s: brahmaṇo vā eṣa raso yad yajñāyajñīyaṃ yad yajñāyajñīyena stuvanti brahmaṇa eva rase yajñaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
8.6.d: ब्रह्मणो वा एष रसो यद् यज्ञायज्ञीयं यद् यज्ञायज्ञीयेन स्तुवन्ति ब्रह्मण एव रसे यज्ञं प्रतिष्ठापयति
8.6.m: The sap of the sacred word indeed is this Yajñāyajñīya. In that they praise with the Yajñāyajñīya, he firmly establishes the sacrifice in the sap of the sacred word.

8.6.s: yonir vai yajñāyajñīyam etasmād vai yoneḥ prajāpatir yajñam asṛjata tasmād yajñāyajñīyam
8.6.d: योनिर् वै यज्ञायज्ञीयम् एतस्माद् वै योनेः प्रजापतिर् यज्ञम् असृजत तस्माद् यज्ञायज्ञीयम्
8.6.m: The womb indeed is the Yajñāyajñīya. From this womb Prajāpati created the sacrifice. Therefore, it is the Yajñāyajñīya.

8.6.s: tasmād vā etena purā brāhmaṇā bahiṣpavamānam astoṣata yoner yajñaṃ pratanavāmahā iti yajñaṃ tataḥ stuvanti yonau yajñaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
8.6.d: तस्माद् वा एतेन पुरा ब्राह्मणा बहिष्पवमानम् अस्तोषत योनेर् यज्ञं प्रतनवामहा इति यज्ञं ततः स्तुवन्ति योनौ यज्ञं प्रतिष्ठापयति
8.6.m: Therefore, with this [sāman], brāhmaṇas formerly praised the Bahiṣpavamāna, [thinking]: 'Let us extend the sacrifice from the womb.' When they praise the sacrifice from it, he firmly establishes the sacrifice in the womb.

8.6.s: asureṣu vai sarvo yajña āsīt te devā yajñāyajñīyam apaśyaṃs teṣāṃ yajñā yajñā vo agnaya ity agnihotram avṛñjata girā girā ca dakṣasa iti darśapūrṇamāsau pra pra vayam amṛtaṃ jātavedasam iti cāturmāsyāni priyaṃ mitraṃ na śaṃsiṣam iti saumyam adhvaram
8.6.d: असुरेषु वै सर्वो यज्ञ आसीत् ते देवा यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अपश्यंस् तेषां यज्ञा यज्ञा वो अग्नय इत्य् अग्निहोत्रम् अवृञ्जत गिरा गिरा च दक्षस इति दर्शपूर्णमासौ प्र प्र वयम् अमृतं जातवेदसम् इति चातुर्मास्यानि प्रियं मित्रं न शंसिषम् इति सौम्यम् अध्वरम्
8.6.m: All sacrifice was indeed with the Asuras. The gods saw the Yajñāyajñīya. From them, with "At every sacrifice, for you, O Agni...", they tore away the agnihotra; with "and with song for the capable...", the New and Full Moon sacrifices; with "Forth, forth we [praise] the immortal Jātavedas...", the Cāturmāsya rites; with "A dear friend, as it were, I would not fail to praise...", the Soma sacrifice.

8.6.s: yajñā vo agnaye girā ca dakṣase pra vayam amṛtaṃ jātavedasaṃ priyaṃ mitraṃ na śaṃsiṣam iti vai tarhi cchandāṃsy āsaṃs te devā abhyārambham abhinivartyaṃ cchandobhir yajñam asurāṇām avṛñjata
8.6.d: यज्ञा वो अग्नये गिरा च दक्षसे प्र वयम् अमृतं जातवेदसं प्रियं मित्रं न शंसिषम् इति वै तर्हि च्छन्दांस्य् आसंस् ते देवा अभ्यारम्भम् अभिनिवर्त्यं च्छन्दोभिर् यज्ञम् असुराणाम् अवृञ्जत
8.6.m: In the beginning the metres were indeed: "Sacrifices for you, O Agni, and with song for the capable; forth we [praise] the immortal Jātavedas; a dear friend, as it were, I would not fail to praise." Taking hold of them [and] bringing them round, the gods tore away the sacrifice of the Asuras by means of the metres.

8.6.s: chandobhir yajñaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
8.6.d: छन्दोभिर् यज्ञं भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते य एवंव् वेद
8.6.m: He who knows thus tears away the sacrifice of his rival by means of the metres.

8.6.s: etad dha sma vā āha kūśāmbaḥ svāyavo brahmā lātavyaḥ kaṃ svid adya śiśumārī yajñapathe 'pyastā gariṣyati
8.6.d: एतद् ध स्म वा आह कूशाम्बः स्वायवो ब्रह्मा लातव्यः कं स्विद् अद्य शिशुमारी यज्ञपथे ऽप्यस्ता गरिष्यति
8.6.m: On this point, Kūśāmba Svāyava, the Brahman of the Lātavyas, used to say: "Whom indeed will the female dolphin cast into the path of the sacrifice swallow today?"

8.6.s: eṣā vai śiśumārī yajñapathe 'pyastā yajñāyajñīyaṃ yad girā girety āhātmānaṃ tad udgātā girati
8.6.d: एषा वै शिशुमारी यज्ञपथे ऽप्यस्ता यज्ञायज्ञीयं यद् गिरा गिरेत्य् आहात्मानं तद् उद्गाता गिरति
8.6.m: This female dolphin cast into the path of the sacrifice is indeed the Yajñāyajñīya. When he says "girā-girā" [with song after song], the udgātṛ swallows himself [girati].

8.6.s: airaṃ kṛtvodgeyam irāyāṃ yajñaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayaty apramāyuka udgātā bhavati
8.6.d: ऐरं कृत्वोद्गेयम् इरायां यज्ञं प्रतिष्ठापयत्य् अप्रमायुक उद्गाता भवति
8.6.m: Having made it into "irā" [nourishment], it should be chanted. He firmly establishes the sacrifice in nourishment; the udgātṛ does not become liable to die before his time.

8.6.s: vaiśvānare vā etad udgātātmānaṃ pradadhāti yat pra pra vayam ity āha praprīṃ vayam iti vaktavyaṃv vaiśvānaram eva parikrāmati
8.6.d: वैश्वानरे वा एतद् उद्गातात्मानं प्रदधाति यत् प्र प्र वयम् इत्य् आह प्रप्रीं वयम् इति वक्तव्यंव् वैश्वानरम् एव परिक्रामति
8.6.m: The udgātṛ indeed places himself into Vaiśvānara when he says "pra-pra vayam" [forth, forth we]. He should say "praprīṃ vayam"; he thereby steps around Vaiśvānara.

8.6.s: yo vai nihnuvānaṃ cchanda upaiti pāpīyān ujjagivān bhavaty etad vai nihnuvānaṃ cchando yan na śaṃsiṣam iti nu śaṃsiṣam iti vaktavyaṃ suśaṃsiṣam iti vā na nihnuvānaṃ chanda upaiti vasīyān ujjagivān bhavati
8.6.d: यो वै निह्नुवानं च्छन्द उपैति पापीयान् उज्जगिवान् भवत्य् एतद् वै निह्नुवानं च्छन्दो यन् न शंसिषम् इति नु शंसिषम् इति वक्तव्यं सुशंसिषम् इति वा न निह्नुवानं छन्द उपैति वसीयान् उज्जगिवान् भवति
8.6.m: Whoever approaches a metre that makes denial becomes worse off after chanting. This indeed is a metre that makes denial, namely "na śaṁsiṣam" [I would not praise]. He should say "nu śaṁsiṣam" [now I would praise], or "suśaṁsiṣam" [I would praise well]. He does not approach a metre that makes denial; he becomes better off after chanting.

8.6.s: yasya vai yajñā vāgantā bhavanti vācaś chidreṇa sravanty ete vai yajñā vāgantā ye yajñāyajñīyāntā etad vācaś chidraṃ yad anṛtaṃ yad agniṣṭomayājy anṛtam āha tad anv asya yajñaḥ sravaty akṣareṇāntataḥ pratiṣṭhāpyam akṣareṇaiva yajñasya cchidram api dadhāti
8.6.d: यस्य वै यज्ञा वागन्ता भवन्ति वाचश् छिद्रेण स्रवन्त्य् एते वै यज्ञा वागन्ता ये यज्ञायज्ञीयान्ता एतद् वाचश् छिद्रं यद् अनृतं यद् अग्निष्टोमयाज्य् अनृतम् आह तद् अन्व् अस्य यज्ञः स्रवत्य् अक्षरेणान्ततः प्रतिष्ठाप्यम् अक्षरेणैव यज्ञस्य च्छिद्रम् अपि दधाति
8.6.m: The sacrifices of him which end in speech flow out through the hole in speech. Those sacrifices indeed end in speech which end with the Yajñāyajñīya. Untruth is this hole in speech: when one who has offered the Agniṣṭoma speaks untruth, his sacrifice flows out after it. It should be firmly established at the end with a syllable; by means of the syllable he stops up the hole of the sacrifice.

8.6.s: virājo vā etad rūpaṃ yad akṣaraṃ virājy evāntataḥ pratitiṣṭhati
8.6.d: विराजो वा एतद् रूपं यद् अक्षरं विराज्य् एवान्ततः प्रतितिष्ठति
8.6.m: This syllable is indeed the form of the virāj; at the end he is firmly established in the virāj.

8.7.s: ito vai prātar ūrdhvāṇi cchandāṃsi yujyante 'muto 'vāñci yajñāyajñīyasya stotre yujyante yajñā vo agnaye girā ca dakṣasa iti dvādaśākṣaraṃ pra vayam amṛtaṃ jātavedasam ity ekādaśākṣaraṃ priyaṃ mitraṃn na śaṃsiṣam ity aṣṭākṣaram
8.7.d: इतो वै प्रातर् ऊर्ध्वाणि च्छन्दांसि युज्यन्ते ऽमुतो ऽवाञ्चि यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य स्तोत्रे युज्यन्ते यज्ञा वो अग्नये गिरा च दक्षस इति द्वादशाक्षरं प्र वयम् अमृतं जातवेदसम् इत्य् एकादशाक्षरं प्रियं मित्रंन् न शंसिषम् इत्य् अष्टाक्षरम्
8.7.m: From here, in the morning, the metres are yoked upwards; from yonder, they are yoked downwards in the chant of praise of the Yajñāyajñīya: "yajñā vo agnaye girā ca dakṣase" is of twelve syllables; "pra vayam amṛtaṃ jātavedasam" is of eleven syllables; "priyaṃ mitraṃ na śaṁsiṣam" is of eight syllables.

8.7.s: anuṣṭubham uttamāṃ saṃpādayatīyaṃ vā anuṣṭub asyām eva pratitiṣṭhati
8.7.d: अनुष्टुभम् उत्तमां संपादयतीयं वा अनुष्टुब् अस्याम् एव प्रतितिष्ठति
8.7.m: He brings about the anuṣṭubh as the last. This [earth] is the anuṣṭubh; he is firmly established on this very [earth].

8.7.s: vāg vā anuṣṭub vācy eva pratitiṣṭhati jyaiṣṭhyaṃ vā anuṣṭub jaiṣṭhya eva pratitiṣṭhati
8.7.d: वाग् वा अनुष्टुब् वाच्य् एव प्रतितिष्ठति ज्यैष्ठ्यं वा अनुष्टुब् जैष्ठ्य एव प्रतितिष्ठति
8.7.m: The anuṣṭubh is speech; he is firmly established in speech. The anuṣṭubh is seniority; he is firmly established in seniority.

8.7.s: katham iva yajñāyajñīyaṃ geyam ity āhur yathānaḍvān prasrāvayamāṇa ittham iva cettham iva ceti
8.7.d: कथम् इव यज्ञायज्ञीयं गेयम् इत्य् आहुर् यथानड्वान् प्रस्रावयमाण इत्थम् इव चेत्थम् इव चेति
8.7.m: They ask: "How should the Yajñāyajñīya be chanted?" As an ox while urinating, like this and like that.

8.7.s: vaiśvānaraṃ vā etad udgātānu prasīdann etīty āhur yad yajñāyajñīyasyarcaṃ saṃpratyāheti parikrāmatevodgeyaṃv vaiśvānaram eva parikrāmati
8.7.d: वैश्वानरं वा एतद् उद्गातानु प्रसीदन्न् एतीत्य् आहुर् यद् यज्ञायज्ञीयस्यर्चं संप्रत्याहेति परिक्रामतेवोद्गेयंव् वैश्वानरम् एव परिक्रामति
8.7.m: They say: "The udgātṛ indeed goes sliding along after Vaiśvānara when he recites the verse of the Yajñāyajñīya continuously." It should be chanted as if stepping around; he thereby steps around Vaiśvānara.

8.7.s: vaiśvānare vā etad adhvaryuḥ sadasyān abhisṛjati yad yajñāyajñīyasya stotram upāvartayati prāvṛtenodgeyaṃv vaiśvānareṇānabhidāhāya
8.7.d: वैश्वानरे वा एतद् अध्वर्युः सदस्यान् अभिसृजति यद् यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य स्तोत्रम् उपावर्तयति प्रावृतेनोद्गेयंव् वैश्वानरेणानभिदाहाय
8.7.m: The adhvaryu indeed brings the members of the assembly into contact with Vaiśvānara when he introduces the chant of praise of the Yajñāyajñīya. It should be chanted covered, in order not to be scorched by Vaiśvānara.

8.7.s: na ha tu vai pitaraḥ prāvṛtaṃ jānanti yajñāyajñīyasya vai stotre pitaro yathāyathaṃ jijñāsanta ākarṇābhyāṃ prāvṛtyaṃ tad eva prāvṛtaṃ tad aprāvṛtaṃ jānanti pitaro na vaiśvānaro hinasti
8.7.d: न ह तु वै पितरः प्रावृतं जानन्ति यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य वै स्तोत्रे पितरो यथायथं जिज्ञासन्त आकर्णाभ्यां प्रावृत्यं तद् एव प्रावृतं तद् अप्रावृतं जानन्ति पितरो न वैश्वानरो हिनस्ति
8.7.m: The fathers, however, do not know one who is [completely] covered. At the chant of praise of the Yajñāyajñīya, the fathers wish to recognise each his own. It should be covered up to the ears; that is both covered and uncovered. The fathers recognise [him], and Vaiśvānara does not harm [him].

8.7.s: apaḥ paścāt patnya upasṛjanti vaiśvānaram eva tac chamayanty āpo hi śāntiḥ
8.7.d: अपः पश्चात् पत्न्य उपसृजन्ति वैश्वानरम् एव तच् छमयन्त्य् आपो हि शान्तिः
8.7.m: Behind, the wives pour water; they thereby appease Vaiśvānara, for water is appeasement.

8.7.s: atho reta eva tat siñcanty āpo hi retaḥ
8.7.d: अथो रेत एव तत् सिञ्चन्त्य् आपो हि रेतः
8.7.m: Moreover, they thereby pour semen, for water is semen.

8.7.s: dakṣiṇān ūrūn abhiṣiñcanti dakṣiṇato hi retaḥ sicyate
8.7.d: दक्षिणान् ऊरून् अभिषिञ्चन्ति दक्षिणतो हि रेतः सिच्यते
8.7.m: They pour it over the right thighs, for semen is poured from the right side.

8.7.s: mahad iva pratyūhyaṃ mana evāsya taj janayanti
8.7.d: महद् इव प्रत्यूह्यं मन एवास्य तज् जनयन्ति
8.7.m: One should draw it back, as it were, greatly; they thereby generate his mind.
They cause the wives to look together with the udgātṛ, for the placing of semen.

8.7.s: hiṅkāraṃ prati saṃkhyāpayanti hiṅkṛtād dhi reto 'dhīyata
8.7.d: हिङ्कारं प्रति संख्यापयन्ति हिङ्कृताद् धि रेतो ऽधीयत
8.7.m: They cause them to look together at the sound hiṅ; for from the uttered hiṅ semen is deposited.
They cause them to look together until the third [verse]; for semen is threefold.

8.8.s: devā vā agniṣṭomam abhijityokthāni nāśaknuvann abhijetuṃ te 'gnim abruvaṃs tvayā mukhenedaṃ cayāmeti so 'bravīt kiṃ me tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayasa ity abruvan so 'bravīn maddevatyāsūkthāni praṇayān iti
8.8.d: देवा वा अग्निष्टोमम् अभिजित्योक्थानि नाशक्नुवन्न् अभिजेतुं ते ऽग्निम् अब्रुवंस् त्वया मुखेनेदं चयामेति सो ऽब्रवीत् किं मे ततः स्याद् इति यत् कामयस इत्य् अब्रुवन् सो ऽब्रवीन् मद्देवत्यासूक्थानि प्रणयान् इति
8.8.m: The gods, having conquered the Agniṣṭoma, were unable to conquer the ukthas. They said to Agni: "With you as our leader, let us conquer this." He said: "What shall be for me therefrom?" They said: "Whatever you desire." He said: "Let them bring forward the ukthas on verses dedicated to me."

8.8.s: tasmād āgneyīṣūkthāni praṇayanti
8.8.d: तस्माद् आग्नेयीषूक्थानि प्रणयन्ति
8.8.m: Therefore, they bring forward the ukthas on verses dedicated to Agni.

8.8.s: tasmād u gāyatrīṣu gāyatracchandā hy agniḥ
8.8.d: तस्माद् उ गायत्रीषु गायत्रच्छन्दा ह्य् अग्निः
8.8.m: And therefore on gāyatrī verses, for Agni has the gāyatrī metre.

8.8.s: te 'gniṃ mukhaṃ kṛtvā sākam aśvenābhyakrāman yat sākam aśvenābhyakrāmaṃs tasmāt sākamaśvam
8.8.d: ते ऽग्निं मुखं कृत्वा साकम् अश्वेनाभ्यक्रामन् यत् साकम् अश्वेनाभ्यक्रामंस् तस्मात् साकमश्वम्
8.8.m: Having made Agni their leader, they marched forth with the Sākamaśva. Because they marched forth with a horse together [sākam aśvena], therefore it is called the Sākamaśva.

8.8.s: tasmāt sākamaśvenokthāni praṇayanty etena hi tāny agre 'bhyajayan
8.8.d: तस्मात् साकमश्वेनोक्थानि प्रणयन्त्य् एतेन हि तान्य् अग्रे ऽभ्यजयन्
8.8.m: Therefore, they bring forward the ukthas with the Sākamaśva, for with this they conquered them in the beginning.

8.8.s: sa indro 'bravīt kaś cāhaṃ cedam anvavaiṣyāva ity ahaṃ ceti varuṇas taṃv varuṇo 'nvatiṣṭhad indra āharat tasmād aindrāvaruṇam anuśasyate
8.8.d: स इन्द्रो ऽब्रवीत् कश् चाहं चेदम् अन्ववैष्याव इत्य् अहं चेति वरुणस् तंव् वरुणो ऽन्वतिष्ठद् इन्द्र आहरत् तस्माद् ऐन्द्रावरुणम् अनुशस्यते
8.8.m: That Indra said: "Who and I shall go down after this?" "I also," said Varuṇa. Varuṇa stood behind him; Indra brought it away. Therefore, [a recitation] addressed to Indra and Varuṇa is recited after.

8.8.s: sa evābravīt kaś cāhaṃ cedam anvavaiṣyāva ity ahaṃ ceti bṛhaspatis taṃ bṛhaspatir anvatiṣṭad indra āharat tasmād aindrābārhaspatyam anuśasyate sa evābravīt kaś cāhaṃ cedam anvavaiṣyāva ity ahaṃ ceti viṣṇus taṃ viṣṇur anvatiṣṭad indra āharat tasmād aindrāvaiṣṇavam anuśasyate
8.8.d: स एवाब्रवीत् कश् चाहं चेदम् अन्ववैष्याव इत्य् अहं चेति बृहस्पतिस् तं बृहस्पतिर् अन्वतिष्टद् इन्द्र आहरत् तस्माद् ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यम् अनुशस्यते स एवाब्रवीत् कश् चाहं चेदम् अन्ववैष्याव इत्य् अहं चेति विष्णुस् तं विष्णुर् अन्वतिष्टद् इन्द्र आहरत् तस्माद् ऐन्द्रावैष्णवम् अनुशस्यते
8.8.m: He alone said: "Who and I shall go down after this?" "I also," said Bṛhaspati. Bṛhaspati stood behind him; Indra brought it away. Therefore, [a recitation] addressed to Indra and Bṛhaspati is recited after. He alone said: "Who and I shall go down after this?" "I also," said Viṣṇu. Viṣṇu stood behind him; Indra brought it away. Therefore, [a recitation] addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu is recited after.

8.8.s: paśūn vā ebhyas tān āharat paśavo vā ukthāni paśukāma ukthena stuvīta paśumān bhavati
8.8.d: पशून् वा एभ्यस् तान् आहरत् पशवो वा उक्थानि पशुकाम उक्थेन स्तुवीत पशुमान् भवति
8.8.m: He brought those cattle away for them. Cattle, indeed, are the ukthas. One who desires cattle should chant with an uktha; he becomes possessed of cattle.

8.8.s: bṛhatā vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat tasya tejaḥ parāpatat tat saubharam abhavat
8.8.d: बृहता वा इन्द्रो वृत्राय वज्रं प्राहरत् तस्य तेजः परापतत् तत् सौभरम् अभवत्
8.8.m: Indra hurled the vajra at Vṛtra with the Bṛhat. Its splendour flew away; it became the Saubhara.

8.8.s: jāmi vā etad yajñe kriyata ity āhur yad rathantaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ rathantaraṃ saṃdhir nāntarā bṛhatā stuvantīti yat saubhareṇa stuvanti bṛhataiva tad antarā stuvanti bṛhato hy etat tejo yat saubharam
8.8.d: जामि वा एतद् यज्ञे क्रियत इत्य् आहुर् यद् रथन्तरं पृष्ठं रथन्तरं संधिर् नान्तरा बृहता स्तुवन्तीति यत् सौभरेण स्तुवन्ति बृहतैव तद् अन्तरा स्तुवन्ति बृहतो ह्य् एतत् तेजो यत् सौभरम्
8.8.m: They say: "A tautology indeed is committed in the sacrifice when the pṛṣṭha is the Rathantara, the saṃdhi is the Rathantara, and between them they do not chant with the Bṛhat." In that they chant with the Saubhara, they chant between them with the Bṛhat itself, for this Saubhara is the splendour of the Bṛhat.

8.8.s: yadi bṛhat sāmātirātraḥ syāt saubharam ukthānāṃ brahma sāma kāryaṃ bṛhad eva tat tejasā samardhayati
8.8.d: यदि बृहत् सामातिरात्रः स्यात् सौभरम् उक्थानां ब्रह्म साम कार्यं बृहद् एव तत् तेजसा समर्धयति
8.8.m: If the atirātra has the Bṛhat as its sāman, the Saubhara should be made the brahma-sāman of the ukthas; he thereby supplies the Bṛhat with splendour.

8.8.s: yadi rathantarasāmnā saubharaṃ kuryād ajāmitāyai
8.8.d: यदि रथन्तरसाम्ना सौभरं कुर्याद् अजामितायै
8.8.m: If with the Rathantara as sāman, he should use the Saubhara for the sake of variation.

8.8.s: devānāṃ vai svargaṃl lokaṃ yatāṃ diśo 'vlīyanta tāḥ saubhareṇo ity udastaṃbhuvaṃs tato vai tā adṛṃhanta tataḥ pratyatiṣṭhaṃs tataḥ svargaṃl lokaṃ prājānan yaḥ svargakāmaḥ syād yaḥ pratiṣṭhākāmaḥ saubhareṇa stuvīta pra svargaṃl lokaṃ jānāti pratitṣṭhati
8.8.d: देवानां वै स्वर्गंल् लोकं यतां दिशो ऽव्लीयन्त ताः सौभरेणो इत्य् उदस्तंभुवंस् ततो वै ता अदृंहन्त ततः प्रत्यतिष्ठंस् ततः स्वर्गंल् लोकं प्राजानन् यः स्वर्गकामः स्याद् यः प्रतिष्ठाकामः सौभरेण स्तुवीत प्र स्वर्गंल् लोकं जानाति प्रतित्ष्ठति
8.8.m: When the gods were going to the heavenly world, the quarters collapsed. With the Saubhara [saying] "u", they propped them up. Then indeed they became firm; then they were firmly established; then they discerned the heavenly world. He who desires heaven, he who desires a firm foundation, should chant with the Saubhara; he discerns the heavenly world and is firmly established.

8.8.s: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭā āśanāyaṃs tābhyaḥ saubhareṇorg ity annaṃ prāyacchat tato vai tāḥ samaidhanta
8.8.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ताः सृष्टा आशनायंस् ताभ्यः सौभरेणोर्ग् इत्य् अन्नं प्रायच्छत् ततो वै ताः समैधन्त
8.8.m: Prajāpati created creatures. Once created, they were hungry. To them, with the Saubhara, saying "ūrg" [nourishment], he gave food. Then indeed they prospered.

8.8.s: samedhante tāṃ samāṃ prajā yatraivaṃv vidvān saubhareṇodgāyati
8.8.d: समेधन्ते तां समां प्रजा यत्रैवंव् विद्वान् सौभरेणोद्गायति
8.8.m: Creatures prosper for that year in which one who knows thus chants as udgātṛ with the Saubhara.

8.8.s: tā abruvan subhṛtaṃ no 'bhārṣīr iti tasmāt saubharam
8.8.d: ता अब्रुवन् सुभृतं नो ऽभार्षीर् इति तस्मात् सौभरम्
8.8.m: They said, 'You have maintained us well (subhṛtam).' Therefore it is called Saubhara.

8.8.s: vṛṣṭiṃ vā abhyastāṃ prāyacchad annam eva
8.8.d: वृष्टिं वा अभ्यस्तां प्रायच्छद् अन्नम् एव
8.8.m: Verily, it was rain that he gave them, [namely] food.

8.8.s: yo vṛṣṭikāmaḥ syād yo 'nnādyakāmo yaḥ svargakāmaḥ saubhareṇa stuvīta
8.8.d: यो वृष्टिकामः स्याद् यो ऽन्नाद्यकामो यः स्वर्गकामः सौभरेण स्तुवीत
8.8.m: He who is desirous of rain, he who is desirous of food, he who is desirous of heaven should praise with the Saubhara.

8.8.s: hīṣiti vṛṣṭikāmāya nidhanaṃ kuryād ūrg ity annādyakāmāyo iti svargakāmāya
8.8.d: हीषिति वृष्टिकामाय निधनं कुर्याद् ऊर्ग् इत्य् अन्नाद्यकामायो इति स्वर्गकामाय
8.8.m: He should make 'hīṣ' as the cadence for one desirous of rain, 'ūrj' for one desirous of food, [and] 'u' for one desirous of heaven.

8.8.s: sarve vai kāmāḥ saubharaṃ sarveṣv eva kāmeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
8.8.d: सर्वे वै कामाः सौभरं सर्वेष्व् एव कामेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
8.8.m: All desires are the Saubhara; he becomes firmly established in all desires.

8.8.s: athaitan nārmedham
8.8.d: अथैतन् नार्मेधम्

8.8.s: nṛmedhasam āṅgirasaṃ sattram āsīnaṃ śvabhir abhyāhvayan so 'gnim upādhāvat pāhi no agna ekayeti taṃv vaiśvānaraḥ paryudatiṣṭhat tato vai sa pratyatiṣṭhat tato gātum avindata
8.8.d: नृमेधसम् आङ्गिरसं सत्त्रम् आसीनं श्वभिर् अभ्याह्वयन् सो ऽग्निम् उपाधावत् पाहि नो अग्न एकयेति तंव् वैश्वानरः पर्युदतिष्ठत् ततो वै स प्रत्यतिष्ठत् ततो गातुम् अविन्दत
8.8.m: While Nṛmedha Āṅgirasa was engaged in a sacrificial session, they challenged him with dogs. He ran up to Agni with [the verse]: 'Protect us, O Agni, with the single [verse].' Vaiśvānara rose up all around him; thereby he stood firm, thereby he found a way.

8.8.s: gātuvid vā etat sāma vindate gātuṃ pratitiṣṭhaty etena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
8.8.d: गातुविद् वा एतत् साम विन्दते गातुं प्रतितिष्ठत्य् एतेन तुष्टुवानः
8.8.m: This sāman is indeed a way-finder; praising with it, he finds a way [and] stands firm.

8.8.s: naiva hy etad ahno rūpaṃ na rātrer yad ukthānām
8.8.d: नैव ह्य् एतद् अह्नो रूपं न रात्रेर् यद् उक्थानाम्
8.8.m: For that which belongs to the ukthas is not the form of the day, nor of the night.

8.8.s: kakup prathamāthoṣṇig atha purauṣṇig anuṣṭup tenānuṣṭubho nayanty acchāvākasāmnaḥ
8.8.d: ककुप् प्रथमाथोष्णिग् अथ पुरौष्णिग् अनुष्टुप् तेनानुष्टुभो नयन्त्य् अच्छावाकसाम्नः
8.8.m: The first is a kakubh, then an uṣṇih, then a purauṣṇih, an anuṣṭubh. Thereby they lead [the uktha] from the anuṣṭubh of the Acchāvāka's sāman.

8.9.s: hārivarṇaṃ bhavati
8.9.d: हारिवर्णं भवति

8.9.s: asurā vā eṣu lokeṣv āsaṃs tān devā hariśriyam ity asmāl lokāt prāṇudanta virājasīty antarikṣād divo diva ity amuṣmāt
8.9.d: असुरा वा एषु लोकेष्व् आसंस् तान् देवा हरिश्रियम् इत्य् अस्माल् लोकात् प्राणुदन्त विराजसीत्य् अन्तरिक्षाद् दिवो दिव इत्य् अमुष्मात्
8.9.m: The Asuras were in these worlds. The gods drove them out from this world with [the words] 'having the beauty of Hari', from the intermediate space with 'thou shinest', [and] from yonder [world] with 'day by day'.

8.9.s: tad ya evaṃ vedaibhyo lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ praṇudyemāṃl lokān abhyārohati
8.9.d: तद् य एवं वेदैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो भ्रातृव्यं प्रणुद्येमांल् लोकान् अभ्यारोहति
8.9.m: He who knows thus, having driven his rival away from these worlds, ascends these worlds.

8.9.s: harivarṇo vā etat paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭaiḥ
8.9.d: हरिवर्णो वा एतत् पशुकामः सामापश्यत् तेन सहस्रं पशून् असृजत यद् एतत् साम भवति पशूनां पुष्टैः
8.9.m: Harivarṇa, being desirous of cattle, saw this sāman. With it he produced a thousand cattle. Since this sāman is [used], it is for the thriving of cattle.

8.9.s: aṅgirasaḥ svargaṃl lokaṃ yato rakṣāṃsy anvasacanta tāny etena harivarṇo 'pāhanta yad etat sāma bhavati rakṣasām apahatyai
8.9.d: अङ्गिरसः स्वर्गंल् लोकं यतो रक्षांस्य् अन्वसचन्त तान्य् एतेन हरिवर्णो ऽपाहन्त यद् एतत् साम भवति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै
8.9.m: The demons pursued the Aṅgirases as they were going to the heavenly world. Harivarṇa struck them down with this [sāman]. Since this sāman is [used], it is for the smiting of the demons.

8.9.s: pṛṣṭhāni vā asṛjyanta teṣāṃ yat tejo raso 'tyaricyata tad devāḥ samabharaṃs tad udvaṃśīyam abhavat
8.9.d: पृष्ठानि वा असृज्यन्त तेषां यत् तेजो रसो ऽत्यरिच्यत तद् देवाः समभरंस् तद् उद्वंशीयम् अभवत्
8.9.m: The pṛṣṭhas were created. Whatever brilliance, [whatever] sap was left over from them, the gods collected together; that became the Udvaṁśīya.

8.9.s: sarveṣāṃ vā etat pṛṣṭhānāṃ tejo yad udvaṃśīyaṃ tasmād vā etat purā sajātāya nākran pāpavasīyaso vidhṛtyai
8.9.d: सर्वेषां वा एतत् पृष्ठानां तेजो यद् उद्वंशीयं तस्माद् वा एतत् पुरा सजाताय नाक्रन् पापवसीयसो विधृत्यै
8.9.m: The Udvaṁśīya is the brilliance of all the pṛṣṭhas. Therefore, in former times, they did not perform this for a fellow-tribesman, in order to maintain the distinction between worse and better.

8.9.s: eṣa hy eva pṛṣṭhais tuṣṭuvāno ya udvaṃśīyena stuvate
8.9.d: एष ह्य् एव पृष्ठैस् तुष्टुवानो य उद्वंशीयेन स्तुवते
8.9.m: For he indeed has praised with the pṛṣṭhas who praises with the Udvaṁśīya.

8.9.s: sarvāṇi vai rūpāṇy udvaṃśīyam
8.9.d: सर्वाणि वै रूपाण्य् उद्वंशीयम्
8.9.m: All forms indeed are the Udvaṁśīya.

8.9.s: gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇa eti rathantarasya rūpam eti hi rathantaram
8.9.d: गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिण एति रथन्तरस्य रूपम् एति हि रथन्तरम्
8.9.m: 'The singers sing to thee, he goes' is the form of the Rathantara, for the Rathantara goes.

8.9.s: ādir bṛhata ūrdhvam iva hi bṛhat
8.9.d: आदिर् बृहत ऊर्ध्वम् इव हि बृहत्
8.9.m: The ādi belongs to the Bṛhat, for the Bṛhat is, as it were, upward.

8.9.s: pariṣṭobho vairūpasya pariṣṭubhaṃ hi vairūpam
8.9.d: परिष्टोभो वैरूपस्य परिष्टुभं हि वैरूपम्
8.9.m: The pariṣṭobha belongs to the Vairūpa, for the Vairūpa has pariṣṭobhas.

8.9.s: anutodo vairājasyānutunnaṃ hi vairājam
8.9.d: अनुतोदो वैराजस्यानुतुन्नं हि वैराजम्
8.9.m: The anutoda belongs to the Vairāja, for the Vairāja is anutunna.

8.9.s: ardheḍā śakvarīṇām atisvāro revatīnām
8.9.d: अर्धेडा शक्वरीणाम् अतिस्वारो रेवतीनाम्
8.9.m: The ardheḍā belongs to the Śakvarīs; the atisvāra belongs to the Revatīs.

8.9.s: ardheḍayā vai devā asurān avahatyātisvāreṇa svargaṃl lokam ārohan
8.9.d: अर्धेडया वै देवा असुरान् अवहत्यातिस्वारेण स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आरोहन्
8.9.m: By means of the ardheḍā the gods smote the Asuras, [and] by means of the atisvāra they ascended to the heavenly world.

8.9.s: tad ya evaṃv vedārdheḍayaiva bhrātṛvyam avahatyātisvāreṇa svargaṃl lokam ārohati
8.9.d: तद् य एवंव् वेदार्धेडयैव भ्रातृव्यम् अवहत्यातिस्वारेण स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आरोहति
8.9.m: He who knows thus, having smitten his rival by means of the ardheḍā, ascends to the heavenly world by means of the atisvāra.

8.9.s: ardheḍayā vai pūrvaṃ yajñaṃ saṃsthāpayanty atisvāreṇottram ārabhante
8.9.d: अर्धेडया वै पूर्वं यज्ञं संस्थापयन्त्य् अतिस्वारेणोत्त्रम् आरभन्ते
8.9.m: With the ardheḍā they bring the former sacrifice to completion; with the atisvāra they undertake the latter.

8.9.s: upainam uttaro yajño namati ya evaṃv veda
8.9.d: उपैनम् उत्तरो यज्ञो नमति य एवंव् वेद
8.9.m: The latter sacrifice inclines unto him who knows thus.

8.9.s: pāṅktaṃ vā etat sāma pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavo yajña eva paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
8.9.d: पाङ्क्तं वा एतत् साम पाङ्क्तो यज्ञः पाङ्क्ताः पशवो यज्ञ एव पशुषु प्रतितिष्ठति
8.9.m: This sāman is fivefold; the sacrifice is fivefold; cattle are fivefold. He is established in the sacrifice, in cattle.

8.9.s: āṣṭādaṃṣṭre ṛddhikāmāya kuryāt
8.9.d: आष्टादंष्ट्रे ऋद्धिकामाय कुर्यात्

8.9.s: aṣṭādaṃṣṭro vairūpo 'putro 'prajā ajīryat sa imāṃl lokān vicicchidvāṃ amanyata sa ete jarasi sāmanī apaśyat tayor aprayogād abibhet so 'bravīd ṛdhnavad yobhe sāmabhyāṃ stavatā iti
8.9.d: अष्टादंष्ट्रो वैरूपो ऽपुत्रो ऽप्रजा अजीर्यत् स इमांल् लोकान् विचिच्छिद्वां अमन्यत स एते जरसि सामनी अपश्यत् तयोर् अप्रयोगाद् अबिभेत् सो ऽब्रवीद् ऋध्नवद् योभे सामभ्यां स्तवता इति
8.9.m: Aṣṭādaṁṣṭra Vairūpa grew old without a son, without offspring. He thought these worlds were cut off from him. In old age he saw these two sāmans. He feared because they were not applied. He said, 'May he prosper who praises with both sāmans!'

8.9.s: ṛṣer vā etat prāśodbhūtaṃ yad aṣṭādaṃṣṭre bhavata ṛdhyā eva
8.9.d: ऋषेर् वा एतत् प्राशोद्भूतं यद् अष्टादंष्ट्रे भवत ऋध्या एव
8.9.m: That there are the two Āṣṭādaṁṣṭra [sāmans] is indeed the fruition of the seer's prayer, for prosperity.

8.10.s: gāyatrīṣu brahmavarcasakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur gāyatryāṃ brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣā gāyatrī saṃpadyate
8.10.d: गायत्रीषु ब्रह्मवर्चसकामायोक्थानि प्रणयेयुर् गायत्र्यां ब्रह्मसामानुष्टुभ्य् अच्छावाकसाम सैषा गायत्री संपद्यते
8.10.m: For one desirous of brahminical lustre they should lead forth the ukthas on gāyatrī verses; on a gāyatrī is the Brahma-sāman, on an anuṣṭubh the Acchāvāka-sāman: this amounts to a gāyatrī.

8.10.s: tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe
8.10.d: तेजो ब्रह्मवर्चसं गायत्री तेज एव ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अवरुन्धे
8.10.m: The gāyatrī is brilliance, brahminical lustre; he secures brilliance, brahminical lustre.

8.10.s: gāyatrīṣu paśukāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur uṣṇihi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣoṣṇik saṃpadyate
8.10.d: गायत्रीषु पशुकामायोक्थानि प्रणयेयुर् उष्णिहि ब्रह्मसामानुष्टुभ्य् अच्छावाकसाम सैषोष्णिक् संपद्यते
8.10.m: For one desirous of cattle they should lead forth the ukthas on gāyatrī verses; on an uṣṇih is the Brahma-sāman, on an anuṣṭubh the Acchāvāka-sāman: this amounts to an uṣṇih.
The uṣṇih is cattle; he secures cattle.

8.10.s: gāyatrīṣu puruṣakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyuḥ kakubhi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣā kakup saṃpadyate
8.10.d: गायत्रीषु पुरुषकामायोक्थानि प्रणयेयुः ककुभि ब्रह्मसामानुष्टुभ्य् अच्छावाकसाम सैषा ककुप् संपद्यते
8.10.m: For one desirous of men they should lead forth the ukthas on gāyatrī verses; on a kakubh is the Brahma-sāman, on an anuṣṭubh the Acchāvāka-sāman: this amounts to a kakubh.
The kakubh is man; he secures men.

8.10.s: virāṭsv annādyakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur uṣṇihi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣā virāṭ saṃpadyate
8.10.d: विराट्स्व् अन्नाद्यकामायोक्थानि प्रणयेयुर् उष्णिहि ब्रह्मसामानुष्टुभ्य् अच्छावाकसाम सैषा विराट् संपद्यते
8.10.m: For one desirous of food they should lead forth the ukthas on virāj verses; on an uṣṇih is the Brahma-sāman, on an anuṣṭubh the Acchāvāka-sāman: this amounts to a virāj.
The virāj is food; he secures food.

8.10.s: akṣarapaṅktiṣu jyaiṣṭhyakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur uṣṇihi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣānuṣṭup saṃpadyate
8.10.d: अक्षरपङ्क्तिषु ज्यैष्ठ्यकामायोक्थानि प्रणयेयुर् उष्णिहि ब्रह्मसामानुष्टुभ्य् अच्छावाकसाम सैषानुष्टुप् संपद्यते
8.10.m: For one desirous of seniority they should lead forth the ukthas on akṣarapaṅkti verses; on an uṣṇih is the Brahma-sāman, on an anuṣṭubh the Acchāvāka-sāman: this amounts to an anuṣṭubh.
The anuṣṭubh is seniority; he secures seniority.

9.1.s: devā vā ukthāny abhijitya rātriṃ nāśaknuvann abhijetuṃ te 'surān rātriṃ tamaḥ praviṣṭāṃ nānuvyapaśyaṃs ta etam anuṣṭupśirasaṃ pragāthm apaśyan virājaṃ jyotiḥ tān virājā jyotiṣānupaśyanto 'nuṣṭubhā vajreṇa rātrer nirāghnan
9.1.d: देवा वा उक्थान्य् अभिजित्य रात्रिं नाशक्नुवन्न् अभिजेतुं ते ऽसुरान् रात्रिं तमः प्रविष्टां नानुव्यपश्यंस् त एतम् अनुष्टुप्शिरसं प्रगाथ्म् अपश्यन् विराजं ज्योतिः तान् विराजा ज्योतिषानुपश्यन्तो ऽनुष्टुभा वज्रेण रात्रेर् निराघ्नन्
9.1.m: The gods, having conquered the ukthas, were not able to conquer the night. They could not discern the Asuras who had entered the darkness, the night. They saw this pragātha with an anuṣṭubh as its head, the virāj, a light. Discerning them by means of the virāj, the light, they smote them out of the night with the anuṣṭubh, the thunderbolt.

9.1.s: yad eṣo 'nuṣṭupśirāḥ pragātho bhavati virāḍ eva jyotiṣānupaśyann anuṣṭubhā vajreṇa rātrer bhrātṛvyaṃ nirhanti
9.1.d: यद् एषो ऽनुष्टुप्शिराः प्रगाथो भवति विराड् एव ज्योतिषानुपश्यन्न् अनुष्टुभा वज्रेण रात्रेर् भ्रातृव्यं निर्हन्ति
9.1.m: Since this pragātha has an anuṣṭubh as its head, [the sacrificer], discerning his rival by means of the virāj, the light, smites him out of the night with the anuṣṭubh, the thunderbolt.

9.1.s: tān samantaṃ paryāyaṃ prāṇudanta yat paryāyaṃ prāṇudanta tat paryāyāṇāṃ paryāyatvam
9.1.d: तान् समन्तं पर्यायं प्राणुदन्त यत् पर्यायं प्राणुदन्त तत् पर्यायाणां पर्यायत्वम्
9.1.m: They drove them away round about in a round (paryāya). In that they drove them away in a round, that is the roundness of the rounds.

9.1.s: prathamāni padāni punarādīni bhavanti prathamasya paryāyasya
9.1.d: प्रथमानि पदानि पुनरादीनि भवन्ति प्रथमस्य पर्यायस्य
9.1.m: The initial verse-quarters are repeated of the first round.

9.1.s: prathamair hi padaiḥ punar ādāya prathamarātrāt prāṇudanta
9.1.d: प्रथमैर् हि पदैः पुनर् आदाय प्रथमरात्रात् प्राणुदन्त
9.1.m: For, repeating the initial verse-quarters, they drove [them] away from the first part of the night.

9.1.s: pāntam ā vo andhasa iti prastauti
9.1.d: पान्तम् आ वो अन्धस इति प्रस्तौति
9.1.m: He chants the prastāva with: 'The draught of your juice'.

9.1.s: ahar vai pāntam andho rātrir ahnaiva tad rātrim ārabhante
9.1.d: अहर् वै पान्तम् अन्धो रात्रिर् अह्नैव तद् रात्रिम् आरभन्ते
9.1.m: The day is the draught, the juice is the night. Thereby they undertake the night by means of the day.

9.1.s: tāsu vaitahavyam
9.1.d: तासु वैतहव्यम्

9.1.s: vītahavyaḥ śrāyaso jyog niruddha etat sāmāpaśyat so 'vagacchat pratyatiṣṭhad avagacchati pratitiṣṭhaty etena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
9.1.d: वीतहव्यः श्रायसो ज्योग् निरुद्ध एतत् सामापश्यत् सो ऽवगच्छत् प्रत्यतिष्ठद् अवगच्छति प्रतितिष्ठत्य् एतेन तुष्टुवानः
9.1.m: Vītahavya Śrāyasa, having been excluded for a long time, saw this sāman. He attained [his wish] and became firmly established. He who praises with this attains [his wish] and becomes firmly established.

9.1.s: tam iva vā ete praviśantiye rātrim upayanti yad eko nidhanaṃ rātrer mukhe bhavati prajñātyai
9.1.d: तम् इव वा एते प्रविशन्तिये रात्रिम् उपयन्ति यद् एको निधनं रात्रेर् मुखे भवति प्रज्ञात्यै
9.1.m: They enter, as it were, into darkness who approach the night. That there is a single cadence at the beginning of the night is for discernment.

9.1.s: yadā vai puruṣaḥ svam oka āgacchati sarvaṃ tarhi prajānāti sarvam asmai divā bhavati
9.1.d: यदा वै पुरुषः स्वम् ओक आगच्छति सर्वं तर्हि प्रजानाति सर्वम् अस्मै दिवा भवति
9.1.m: When a man comes to his own home, then he knows everything; everything becomes day for him.

9.1.s: te madhyamaṃ paryāyam aśrayanta teṣām aurdhvasadmanena vācam avṛñjata
9.1.d: ते मध्यमं पर्यायम् अश्रयन्त तेषाम् और्ध्वसद्मनेन वाचम् अवृञ्जत
9.1.m: They resorted to the middle round. By means of the Aurdhvasadmana [sāman] they wrested away speech from them.

9.1.s: vācaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
9.1.d: वाचं भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते य एवंव् वेद
9.1.m: He who knows thus wrests away the speech of his rival.

9.1.s: triṇidhanaṃ bhavati
9.1.d: त्रिणिधनं भवति

9.1.s: yathā vā ahno mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ triṇidhanāyatanam evam eṣa rātrer madhyamaḥ paryāyas triṇidhanāyatanaḥ salokatvāya
9.1.d: यथा वा अह्नो माध्यन्दिनं सवनं त्रिणिधनायतनम् एवम् एष रात्रेर् मध्यमः पर्यायस् त्रिणिधनायतनः सलोकत्वाय
9.1.m: Just as the midday pressing of the day is the seat of three cadences, so this middle round of the night is the seat of three cadences, for [attaining] the same world.

9.1.s: madhyamāni padāni punarādīni bhavanti madhyamasya paryāyasya madhyamair hi padaiḥ punar ādāyaṃ madhyamarātrāt prāṇudanta
9.1.d: मध्यमानि पदानि पुनरादीनि भवन्ति मध्यमस्य पर्यायस्य मध्यमैर् हि पदैः पुनर् आदायं मध्यमरात्रात् प्राणुदन्त
9.1.m: The middle verse-quarters are repeated of the middle round. For, repeating the middle verse-quarters, they drove [them] away from the middle of the night.

9.1.s: ta uttamaṃ paryāyam aśrayanta teṣāṃ ghṛtaścyun nidhanena paśūn avṛñjata paśavo vai ghṛtaścyutaḥ
9.1.d: त उत्तमं पर्यायम् अश्रयन्त तेषां घृतश्च्युन् निधनेन पशून् अवृञ्जत पशवो वै घृतश्च्युतः
9.1.m: They resorted to the last round. By means of the cadence 'dripping with ghee' they wrested away cattle from them. Cattle indeed are dripping with ghee.

9.1.s: paśūn bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
9.1.d: पशून् भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते य एवंव् वेद
9.1.m: He who knows thus wrests away the cattle of his rival.

9.1.s: uttamāni padāni punarādīni bhavanty uttamasya paryāyasyottamair hi padaiḥpunar ādāyam uttamarātrāt prāṇudanta
9.1.d: उत्तमानि पदानि पुनरादीनि भवन्त्य् उत्तमस्य पर्यायस्योत्तमैर् हि पदैःपुनर् आदायम् उत्तमरात्रात् प्राणुदन्त
9.1.m: The final verses of the final round are repeated, for by taking [them] up again with the final verses, they drove [them] out from the end of the night.

9.1.s: tān sandhinābhipalāyanta
9.1.d: तान् सन्धिनाभिपलायन्त
9.1.m: They fled from them towards the twilight chant.

9.1.s: tān āśvinenāsaṃhāyyam agamayan
9.1.d: तान् आश्विनेनासंहाय्यम् अगमयन्

9.1.s: asaṃhāyyaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ gamayati ya evaṃv veda
9.1.d: असंहाय्यं भ्रातृव्यं गमयति य एवंव् वेद
9.1.m: He who knows this brings his rival to ruin.

9.1.s: eṣā vā agniṣṭomasya saṃmā yad rātriḥ
9.1.d: एषा वा अग्निष्टोमस्य संमा यद् रात्रिः
9.1.m: The night, indeed, is the measure of the Agniṣṭoma.

9.1.s: dvādaśa stotrāṇy agniṣṭomo dvādaśa strotrāṇi rātriḥ
9.1.d: द्वादश स्तोत्राण्य् अग्निष्टोमो द्वादश स्त्रोत्राणि रात्रिः
9.1.m: The Agniṣṭoma has twelve chants of praise; the night has twelve chants of praise.

9.1.s: eṣā vā ukthasya saṃmā yad rātriḥ
9.1.d: एषा वा उक्थस्य संमा यद् रात्रिः
9.1.m: The night, indeed, is the measure of the Uktha.

9.1.s: trīṇy ukthāni tridevatyaḥ sandhiḥ
9.1.d: त्रीण्य् उक्थानि त्रिदेवत्यः सन्धिः
9.1.m: The ukthas are three; the twilight chant has three deities.

9.1.s: yathā vā ahna ukthāny evam eṣa rātreḥ sandhir nānārūpāṇy ahna ukthāni nānārūpā ete tṛcā bhavanti
9.1.d: यथा वा अह्न उक्थान्य् एवम् एष रात्रेः सन्धिर् नानारूपाण्य् अह्न उक्थानि नानारूपा एते तृचा भवन्ति
9.1.m: As are the ukthas of the day, so is this twilight chant of the night: manifold are the ukthas of the day, [and] manifold are these triplets.

9.1.s: rathantaraṃ pratiṣṭhākāmāya sandhiṃ kuryāt
9.1.d: रथन्तरं प्रतिष्ठाकामाय सन्धिं कुर्यात्
9.1.m: For one desirous of a firm standing, he should make the Rathantara the twilight chant.

9.1.s: iyaṃ vai rathantaram asyām eva pratitiṣṭhati
9.1.d: इयं वै रथन्तरम् अस्याम् एव प्रतितिष्ठति
9.1.m: This [earth], indeed, is the Rathantara; he firmly stands on this very [earth].

9.1.s: bṛhat svargakāmāya sandhiṃ kuryāt
9.1.d: बृहत् स्वर्गकामाय सन्धिं कुर्यात्
9.1.m: For one desirous of heaven, he should make the Bṛhat the twilight chant.

9.1.s: svargo loko bṛhat svarga eva loke pratitiṣṭhati
9.1.d: स्वर्गो लोको बृहत् स्वर्ग एव लोके प्रतितिष्ठति
9.1.m: The Bṛhat is the heavenly world; he firmly stands in the heavenly world.

9.1.s: vāravantīyaṃ vā vāmadevyaṃ vā śruddhyaṃ vai teṣām ekaṃ paśukāmāya sandhiṃ kuryāt
9.1.d: वारवन्तीयं वा वामदेव्यं वा श्रुद्ध्यं वै तेषाम् एकं पशुकामाय सन्धिं कुर्यात्
9.1.m: For one desirous of cattle, he should make one of these—either the Vāravantīya, or the Vāmadevya, or the Śruddhīya—the twilight chant.

9.1.s: paśavo vā etāni sāmāni paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
9.1.d: पशवो वा एतानि सामानि पशुष्व् एव प्रतितिष्ठति
9.1.m: These s権利āmans are cattle; he firmly stands among cattle.

9.1.s: āśvinaṃ hotānuśaṃsati
9.1.d: आश्विनं होतानुशंसति

9.1.s: prajāpatir vā etat sahasram asṛjata tad devebhyaḥ prāyacchat tasmin na samarādhayaṃs te sūryaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ kṛtvājim adhāvan
9.1.d: प्रजापतिर् वा एतत् सहस्रम् असृजत तद् देवेभ्यः प्रायच्छत् तस्मिन् न समराधयंस् ते सूर्यं काष्ठां कृत्वाजिम् अधावन्
9.1.m: Prajāpati created this thousand [of verses]; he gave it to the gods. Over it they could not agree; having made the sun their goal, they ran a race.

9.1.s: teṣām aśvinau prathamāv adhāvatāṃ tāv anvavadan saha no 'stv iti tāv abrūtāṃ kiṃ tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayethe ity abruvaṃs tāv abrūtām asmaddevatyam idam uktham ucyātā iti tasmād āśvinam ucyate
9.1.d: तेषाम् अश्विनौ प्रथमाव् अधावतां ताव् अन्ववदन् सह नो ऽस्त्व् इति ताव् अब्रूतां किं ततः स्याद् इति यत् कामयेथे इत्य् अब्रुवंस् ताव् अब्रूताम् अस्मद्देवत्यम् इदम् उक्थम् उच्याता इति तस्माद् आश्विनम् उच्यते
9.1.m: Of them, the two Aśvins ran first. [The others] said after them: 'Let it be shared with us.' They two said: 'What would come of it then?' They said: 'Whatever you two desire.' They two said: 'Let this uktha be addressed to us as deities.' Therefore it is called the Āśvina.

9.1.s: sarvāḥ khalu devatāḥ śasyante
9.1.d: सर्वाः खलु देवताः शस्यन्ते
9.1.m: All the deities indeed are praised.

9.1.s: kṣipraṃ śasyam ājim iva hy ete dhāvanty ā sūryasyodetoḥ śaṃset sūryaṃ hi kāṣṭhām akurvata
9.1.d: क्षिप्रं शस्यम् आजिम् इव ह्य् एते धावन्त्य् आ सूर्यस्योदेतोः शंसेत् सूर्यं हि काष्ठाम् अकुर्वत
9.1.m: It is to be recited quickly, for like a race these run; he should recite it until the rising of the sun, for they made the sun their goal.

9.2.s: pāntam ā vo andhasa iti vaitahavyam anyakṣetraṃvā ete prayanti ye rātrim upayanti yad okonidhanaṃ rātrer mukhe bhavaty okaso 'pracyāvāya
9.2.d: पान्तम् आ वो अन्धस इति वैतहव्यम् अन्यक्षेत्रंवा एते प्रयन्ति ये रात्रिम् उपयन्ति यद् ओकोनिधनं रात्रेर् मुखे भवत्य् ओकसो ऽप्रच्यावाय
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'They drink from your juice' is the Vaitahavya. Those who undertake the night-rite go to a foreign field, as it were; in that there is a cadence on the word 'oka' (home) at the beginning of the night, it is for not falling away from home.

9.2.s: pra va indrāya mādanam iti gaurīvitam
9.2.d: प्र व इन्द्राय मादनम् इति गौरीवितम्
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'Forth to Indra [offer] the intoxicating [draught]' is the Gaurīvita.

9.2.s: brahma yad devā vyakurvata tato yad atyaricyata tad gaurīvitam abhavat
9.2.d: ब्रह्म यद् देवा व्यकुर्वत ततो यद् अत्यरिच्यत तद् गौरीवितम् अभवत्
9.2.m: When the gods distributed the sacred word, what was left over from it became the Gaurīvita.

9.2.s: atiriktaṃ gaurīvitam atiriktam etat stotraṃ yad rātrir atirikta evātiriktaṃ dadhāti
9.2.d: अतिरिक्तं गौरीवितम् अतिरिक्तम् एतत् स्तोत्रं यद् रात्रिर् अतिरिक्त एवातिरिक्तं दधाति
9.2.m: Surplus is the Gaurīvita; surplus is this chant of praise, which is the night; he places surplus into surplus.

9.2.s: vayam u tvā tad id arthā iti kāṇvam
9.2.d: वयम् उ त्वा तद् इद् अर्था इति काण्वम्
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'We [turn] to you for that very purpose' is the Kāṇva.

9.2.s: etena vai kaṇva indrasya sāṃvidyam agacchad indrasyaivaitena sāṃvidyaṃ gacchati
9.2.d: एतेन वै कण्व इन्द्रस्य सांविद्यम् अगच्छद् इन्द्रस्यैवैतेन सांविद्यं गच्छति
9.2.m: By this, Kaṇva attained agreement with Indra; by this, he attains agreement with Indra.

9.2.s: indrāya madvane sutam iti śrautakakṣaṃ kṣatrasāma pra kṣatram evaitena bhavati
9.2.d: इन्द्राय मद्वने सुतम् इति श्रौतकक्षं क्षत्रसाम प्र क्षत्रम् एवैतेन भवति
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'For the joyous Indra the pressed [juice]' is the Śrautakakṣa, a sāman of noble power; by this, noble power thrives.

9.2.s: ayaṃ ta indra soma iti daivodāsam
9.2.d: अयं त इन्द्र सोम इति दैवोदासम्
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'This Soma for you, O Indra' is the Daivodāsa.

9.2.s: agniṣṭomena vai devā imaṃl lokam abhyajayann antarikṣam ukthenātirātreṇāmuṃ ta imaṃl lokaṃ punar abhyakāmayanta ta ihety asmiṃl loke pratyatiṣṭhan yad etat sāma bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
9.2.d: अग्निष्टोमेन वै देवा इमंल् लोकम् अभ्यजयन्न् अन्तरिक्षम् उक्थेनातिरात्रेणामुं त इमंल् लोकं पुनर् अभ्यकामयन्त त इहेत्य् अस्मिंल् लोके प्रत्यतिष्ठन् यद् एतत् साम भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै
9.2.m: By the Agniṣṭoma the gods conquered this world; by the Uktha, the intermediate region; by the Atirātra, yonder [world]. They desired this world again; they firmly stood in this world, [thinking,] 'here [we are].' In that this sāman is used, it is for firm standing.

9.2.s: ūrdhvasadmanam api śarvarīṣu prohanti
9.2.d: ऊर्ध्वसद्मनम् अपि शर्वरीषु प्रोहन्ति
9.2.m: They also introduce the Ūrdhvasadman in the night [chants].

9.2.s: asurā vā eṣu lokeṣv āsaṃs tān devā ūrdhvasadmanenaibhyo lokebhyaḥ prāṇudanta
9.2.d: असुरा वा एषु लोकेष्व् आसंस् तान् देवा ऊर्ध्वसद्मनेनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यः प्राणुदन्त
9.2.m: The asuras were in these worlds; the gods drove them out from these worlds by means of the Ūrdhvasadman.

9.2.s: tad ya evaṃv vedaibhyo lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ praṇudya sva āyatane sattram āste
9.2.d: तद् य एवंव् वेदैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो भ्रातृव्यं प्रणुद्य स्व आयतने सत्त्रम् आस्ते
9.2.m: He who knows this, having driven his rival out from these worlds, celebrates the sacrificial session in his own abode.

9.2.s: ā tū na indra kṣumantam ity ākūpāram
9.2.d: आ तू न इन्द्र क्षुमन्तम् इत्य् आकूपारम्
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'Come to us, O Indra, rich in cattle' is the Ākūpāra.

9.2.s: akūpārāṅgirasasyāsīt tasyā yathā godhāyās tvag eva tvag āsīt tām etena triḥsāmnendraḥ pūtvā sūryatvacasam akarot tad vāva sā tarhy akāmayata yatkāmā etena sāmnā stuvate sa ebhyaḥ kāmaḥ samṛdhyate
9.2.d: अकूपाराङ्गिरसस्यासीत् तस्या यथा गोधायास् त्वग् एव त्वग् आसीत् ताम् एतेन त्रिःसाम्नेन्द्रः पूत्वा सूर्यत्वचसम् अकरोत् तद् वाव सा तर्ह्य् अकामयत यत्कामा एतेन साम्ना स्तुवते स एभ्यः कामः समृध्यते
9.2.m: Akūpārā was a daughter of Aṅgiras; her skin was like the skin of an iguana; Indra, having cleansed her three times with this sāman, made her sun-skinned. That was indeed what she desired then; whatever desire they have when chanting with this sāman, that desire is fulfilled for them.

9.2.s: abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sutaṃ ity ārṣabhaṃ kṣatrasāma kṣatram evaitena bhavati
9.2.d: अभि त्वा वृषभा सुतं इत्य् आर्षभं क्षत्रसाम क्षत्रम् एवैतेन भवति
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'Unto you, O bull, the pressed [juice]' is the Ārṣabha, a sāman of noble power; by this, noble power comes to be.

9.2.s: idaṃv vaso sutam andha iti gāram etena vai gara indram aprīṇāt prīta evāsyaitenendro bhavati
9.2.d: इदंव् वसो सुतम् अन्ध इति गारम् एतेन वै गर इन्द्रम् अप्रीणात् प्रीत एवास्यैतेनेन्द्रो भवति
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'This pressed draught, O Vasu' is the Gāra; by this, Gara pleased Indra; Indra is pleased with him by this.

9.2.s: idaṃ hy anv ojaseti mādhucchandasaṃ prajāpater vā eṣā tanūr ayātayāmnī prayujyate
9.2.d: इदं ह्य् अन्व् ओजसेति माधुच्छन्दसं प्रजापतेर् वा एषा तनूर् अयातयाम्नी प्रयुज्यते
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'For here, along with power' is the Mādhucchandasa; this, indeed, is the unexhausted body of Prajāpati [that] is employed.

9.2.s: ā tv etā niṣīdateti daivātitham
9.2.d: आ त्व् एता निषीदतेति दैवातिथम्
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'Come and sit down here' is the Daivātitha.

9.2.s: devātithiḥ saputro 'śanāyaṃś carann araṇya urvārūṇy avindat tāny etena sāmnopāsīdat tā asmai gāvaḥ pṛśnayo bhūtvodatiṣṭhan yad etat sām a bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai
9.2.d: देवातिथिः सपुत्रो ऽशनायंश् चरन्न् अरण्य उर्वारूण्य् अविन्दत् तान्य् एतेन साम्नोपासीदत् ता अस्मै गावः पृश्नयो भूत्वोदतिष्ठन् यद् एतत् साम् अ भवति पशूनां पुष्ट्यै
9.2.m: Devātithi, wandering hungry with his son in the wilderness, found some cucumbers; he sat by them with this sāman; they rose up for him having become speckled cows. In that this sāman is used, it is for the thriving of cattle.

9.2.s: yoge yoge tavastaram iti saumedhaṃ rātriṣāma rātrer eva samṛdhyai
9.2.d: योगे योगे तवस्तरम् इति सौमेधं रात्रिषाम रात्रेर् एव समृध्यै
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'In every team [we invoke] the stronger' is the Saumedha, a night-sāman, for the success of the night.

9.2.s: indra suteṣu someṣv iti kautsam
9.2.d: इन्द्र सुतेषु सोमेष्व् इति कौत्सम्
9.2.m: [The sāman on the verse] 'O Indra, when the Somas are pressed' is the Kautsa.

9.2.s: kutsaś ca luśaś cendraṃ vyahvayetāṃ sa indraḥ kutsam upāvartata taṃ śatena vārdhrībhir āṇḍayor abadhnāt taṃ luśo 'bhyavadat pramucyasva pari kutsād ihāgahi kim u tvāvān āṇḍayor baddha āsātā iti tās saṃcchidya prādravat sa etat kutsaḥ sāmāpaśyat tenainam anvavadat sa upāvartata
9.2.d: कुत्सश् च लुशश् चेन्द्रं व्यह्वयेतां स इन्द्रः कुत्सम् उपावर्तत तं शतेन वार्ध्रीभिर् आण्डयोर् अबध्नात् तं लुशो ऽभ्यवदत् प्रमुच्यस्व परि कुत्साद् इहागहि किम् उ त्वावान् आण्डयोर् बद्ध आसाता इति तास् संच्छिद्य प्राद्रवत् स एतत् कुत्सः सामापश्यत् तेनैनम् अन्ववदत् स उपावर्तत
9.2.m: Kutsa and Luśa challenged Indra; Indra turned toward Kutsa; he bound him by the testicles with a hundred leather thongs. Luśa spoke to him: 'Free yourself from Kutsa and come here! How can one like you sit bound by the testicles?' Having cut them, he ran off. Kutsa saw this sāman; with it he called after him; he turned back.

9.2.s: yad etat sāma bhavati sendratvāya
9.2.d: यद् एतत् साम भवति सेन्द्रत्वाय
9.2.m: In that this sāman is used, it is for possessing Indra.

9.3.s: yadi sattrāya dīkṣerann atha sāmy uttiṣṭhet somam apabhajya viśvajitātirātreṇa yajeta sarvavedasena sarvasmā eva dīkṣate sarvam āpnoti
9.3.d: यदि सत्त्राय दीक्षेरन्न् अथ साम्य् उत्तिष्ठेत् सोमम् अपभज्य विश्वजितातिरात्रेण यजेत सर्ववेदसेन सर्वस्मा एव दीक्षते सर्वम् आप्नोति
9.3.m: If they should be consecrated for a sacrificial session and then one leaves halfway through, having separated the Soma, he should sacrifice with the Viśvajit Atirātra with all his possessions given as dakṣiṇā; he is consecrated for everything, he obtains everything.

9.3.s: yā id dakṣiṇā dadāti tābhir iti prayuṅkte
9.3.d: या इद् दक्षिणा ददाति ताभिर् इति प्रयुङ्क्ते
9.3.m: He employs it with [the thought]: 'With these, [I give] whatever dakṣiṇās he gives.'

9.3.s: yadi paryāyair astutam abhivyucchet pancadaśabhir hotre stuyuḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhir itarebhyaḥ
9.3.d: यदि पर्यायैर् अस्तुतम् अभिव्युच्छेत् पन्चदशभिर् होत्रे स्तुयुः पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिर् इतरेभ्यः
9.3.m: If dawn should break upon them when the rounds are not yet chanted, they should chant fifteen [verses] for the hotṛ, and five each for the others.

9.3.s: agne vivasvad uṣasa iti sandhinā stuyuḥ prāṇā vai trivṛt stomānāṃ pratiṣṭhā rathantaraṃ sāmnāṃ prāṇāṃs caivopayanti pratiṣṭhāṃ ca
9.3.d: अग्ने विवस्वद् उषस इति सन्धिना स्तुयुः प्राणा वै त्रिवृत् स्तोमानां प्रतिष्ठा रथन्तरं साम्नां प्राणांस् चैवोपयन्ति प्रतिष्ठां च
9.3.m: They should chant the twilight chant with: 'O Agni, radiant at the dawns'; the ninefold stoma is the vital breaths, the Rathantara is the firm standing of the s権利āmans; they attain the vital breaths and firm standing.

9.3.s: ṣaṣṭiṃ ca trīṇi ca śatāni hotā śaṃsati
9.3.d: षष्टिं च त्रीणि च शतानि होता शंसति
9.3.m: The hotṛ recites three hundred and sixty [verses].

9.3.s: tāvatyaḥ saṃvatsarasya rātrayaḥ saṃvatsarasaṃmitābhir eva tad ṛgbhir āśīvinam āpnoti
9.3.d: तावत्यः संवत्सरस्य रात्रयः संवत्सरसंमिताभिर् एव तद् ऋग्भिर् आशीविनम् आप्नोति
9.3.m: So many are the nights of the year; with verses equal in number to the year, he thus obtains the Āśvina.

9.3.s: yad arvāk stuvanti tad astutaṃ yat samprati stuvanti tat stutaṃ yad atiṣṭuvanti tat suṣṭutam
9.3.d: यद् अर्वाक् स्तुवन्ति तद् अस्तुतं यत् सम्प्रति स्तुवन्ति तत् स्तुतं यद् अतिष्टुवन्ति तत् सुष्टुतम्
9.3.m: When they chant fewer, it is unchanted; when they chant the exact amount, it is chanted; when they chant more, it is well-chanted.

9.3.s: yady arvāk stuyur yāvatībhir na stuyus tāvatībhir vātiṣṭuyur bhūyo 'kṣarābhir vā
9.3.d: यद्य् अर्वाक् स्तुयुर् यावतीभिर् न स्तुयुस् तावतीभिर् वातिष्टुयुर् भूयो ऽक्षराभिर् वा
9.3.m: If they should chant fewer, they should chant with as many more verses, or with [verses of] more syllables, as they did not chant.

9.3.s: yady atiṣṭuyur yāvatībhir atiṣṭuyus tāvatībhir vā na stuyuḥ kanīyo 'kṣarābhir vā
9.3.d: यद्य् अतिष्टुयुर् यावतीभिर् अतिष्टुयुस् तावतीभिर् वा न स्तुयुः कनीयो ऽक्षराभिर् वा
9.3.m: If they should chant more, they should omit as many verses, or [use verses of] fewer syllables, as they chanted in excess.

9.3.s: yady arvāk stuyus trīḍam agniṣṭomasāma kāryaṃ nidhanam ekeḍayā ye dve tābhyām eva tat samaṃ kriyate
9.3.d: यद्य् अर्वाक् स्तुयुस् त्रीडम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कार्यं निधनम् एकेडया ये द्वे ताभ्याम् एव तत् समं क्रियते
9.3.m: If they should chant fewer, the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is to be made with three iḍās; with the one iḍā of the cadence, it is made equal to those which are two.

9.3.s: yady atiṣṭuyuḥ svāram agniṣṭomasāma kāryam ūnam iva vā etat sāmno yat svaras tenaiva tat samaṃ kriyate
9.3.d: यद्य् अतिष्टुयुः स्वारम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कार्यम् ऊनम् इव वा एतत् साम्नो यत् स्वरस् तेनैव तत् समं क्रियते
9.3.m: If they should chant more, the Agniṣṭoma-sāman is to be made with a svar-ending; what is tone is deficient, as it were, of the sāman; by that it is made equal.

9.4.s: yadi somau saṃsutau syātāṃ mahati rātreḥ prātaranuvākam upākuryāt
9.4.d: यदि सोमौ संसुतौ स्यातां महति रात्रेः प्रातरनुवाकम् उपाकुर्यात्
9.4.m: If two Somas should be pressed together, he should begin the morning recitation in the deep of the night.

9.4.s: pūrvo vācaṃ pūrvaś chandāṃsi pūrvo devatā vṛṅkte
9.4.d: पूर्वो वाचं पूर्वश् छन्दांसि पूर्वो देवता वृङ्क्ते
9.4.m: Being first, he appropriates speech; being first, the metres; being first, the deities.

9.4.s: vṛṣaṇvatīṃ pratipadaṃ kuryād indro vai vṛṣā prātaḥsavanād evaiṣām indraṃv vṛṅkte
9.4.d: वृषण्वतीं प्रतिपदं कुर्याद् इन्द्रो वै वृषा प्रातःसवनाद् एवैषाम् इन्द्रंव् वृङ्क्ते
9.4.m: He should make an introductory verse containing [the word] 'bull'; Indra is a bull; he appropriates Indra from their morning pressing.

9.4.s: atho khalv āhuḥ savanamukhe savanamukhe kāryā savanamukhāt savanamukhād evaiṣām indraṃv vṛṅkte
9.4.d: अथो खल्व् आहुः सवनमुखे सवनमुखे कार्या सवनमुखात् सवनमुखाद् एवैषाम् इन्द्रंव् वृङ्क्ते
9.4.m: Moreover they say: it is to be made at the beginning of each pressing; he appropriates Indra from the very beginning of each of their pressings.

9.4.s: susamiddhe hotavyam agnir vai sarvā devatāḥ sarvā eva devatāḥ paśyañ juhoti
9.4.d: सुसमिद्धे होतव्यम् अग्निर् वै सर्वा देवताः सर्वा एव देवताः पश्यञ् जुहोति
9.4.m: He should offer into a well-kindled [fire]; for Agni is all the deities. Beholding all the deities indeed he offers.

9.4.s: saṃveśāyopaveśāya gāyatryai cchandase 'bhibhūtaye svāhā saṃveśāyopaveśāya triṣṭubhe cchandase 'bhibhūtaye svāhā saṃveśāyopaveśāya jagatyai cchandase 'bhibhūtaye svāheti juhoti
9.4.d: संवेशायोपवेशाय गायत्र्यै च्छन्दसे ऽभिभूतये स्वाहा संवेशायोपवेशाय त्रिष्टुभे च्छन्दसे ऽभिभूतये स्वाहा संवेशायोपवेशाय जगत्यै च्छन्दसे ऽभिभूतये स्वाहेति जुहोति
9.4.m: "To lying down, to sitting down, to the gāyatrī metre, to overcoming, svāhā! To lying down, to sitting down, to the triṣṭubh metre, to overcoming, svāhā! To lying down, to sitting down, to the jagatī metre, to overcoming, svāhā!"—thus he offers.

9.4.s: cchandāṃsi vā abhibhūtayas tair evainān abhibhavaty ubhe bṛhadrathantare kārye
9.4.d: च्छन्दांसि वा अभिभूतयस् तैर् एवैनान् अभिभवत्य् उभे बृहद्रथन्तरे कार्ये
9.4.m: The metres are indeed the overcomings; by means of them he overcomes them. Both the Bṛhat and Rathantara should be used.

9.4.s: yatra vā indrasya harī tad indraḥ indrasya vai harī bṛhadrathantare yad ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavataḥ pūrva evendrasya harī ārabhante
9.4.d: यत्र वा इन्द्रस्य हरी तद् इन्द्रः इन्द्रस्य वै हरी बृहद्रथन्तरे यद् उभे बृहद्रथन्तरे भवतः पूर्व एवेन्द्रस्य हरी आरभन्ते
9.4.m: Where Indra's two bay steeds are, there is Indra. The Bṛhat and Rathantara are Indra's two bay steeds. When both the Bṛhat and Rathantara are [used], they take hold of Indra's two bay steeds first.

9.4.s: turaśravasaś ca vai pārāvatānāṃ ca somau saṃsutāv āstāṃ tata ete turaśravāḥ sāmanī apaśyat tābhyām asmā indraḥ śalmalināṃ yamunāyā havyaṃ nirāvahat yat tair aśravase bhavato havyam evaiṣāṃv vṛṅkte
9.4.d: तुरश्रवसश् च वै पारावतानां च सोमौ संसुताव् आस्तां तत एते तुरश्रवाः सामनी अपश्यत् ताभ्याम् अस्मा इन्द्रः शल्मलिनां यमुनाया हव्यं निरावहत् यत् तैर् अश्रवसे भवतो हव्यम् एवैषांव् वृङ्क्ते
9.4.m: The Soma [sacrifices] of Turaśravas and of the Pārāvatas were pressed simultaneously. Then Turaśravas saw these two sāmans. By means of them Indra brought out the oblation of the Śalmalins from the Yamunā for him. When the two Tauraśravasa [sāmans] are [used], he deprives them of their oblation.

9.4.s: yā vai pūrvāḥ prasnānti tāḥ pūrvās tīrthaṃ jayanti pūrva evendram ārabhante
9.4.d: या वै पूर्वाः प्रस्नान्ति ताः पूर्वास् तीर्थं जयन्ति पूर्व एवेन्द्रम् आरभन्ते
9.4.m: Those who bathe first win the ford first. They take hold of Indra first.

9.4.s: jamadagneś ca vā ṛṣīṇāṃ ca somau saṃsutāv āstāṃ tata etaj gamadagnir vihavyam apaśyat tam indra upāvartata yad vihavyaṃ hotā śaṃsatīndram evaiṣāṃv vṛṅkte
9.4.d: जमदग्नेश् च वा ऋषीणां च सोमौ संसुताव् आस्तां तत एतज् गमदग्निर् विहव्यम् अपश्यत् तम् इन्द्र उपावर्तत यद् विहव्यं होता शंसतीन्द्रम् एवैषांव् वृङ्क्ते
9.4.m: The Soma [sacrifices] of Jamadagni and of the ṛṣis were pressed simultaneously. Then Jamadagni saw this Vihavya [hymn]. To him Indra turned. When the Hotṛ recites the Vihavya, he deprives them of Indra.

9.4.s: yadītaro 'gniṣṭomaḥ syād ukthaḥ kāryo yady uktho 'tirātro yo vai bhūyān yajñakratuḥ sa indrasya priyo bhūyasaivaiṣāṃ yajnakratunendraṃv vṛṅkte
9.4.d: यदीतरो ऽग्निष्टोमः स्याद् उक्थः कार्यो यद्य् उक्थो ऽतिरात्रो यो वै भूयान् यज्ञक्रतुः स इन्द्रस्य प्रियो भूयसैवैषां यज्नक्रतुनेन्द्रंव् वृङ्क्ते
9.4.m: If the other [rite] should be an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya should be performed; if an Ukthya, an Atirātra. Whichever sacrificial rite is greater, that is dear to Indra; by means of a greater sacrificial rite he deprives them of Indra.

9.4.s: atho khalv āhur duṣprāpa iva vai paraḥ panthā yam evāgre yajñakratum ārabheta tasmān neyād iti
9.4.d: अथो खल्व् आहुर् दुष्प्राप इव वै परः पन्था यम् एवाग्रे यज्ञक्रतुम् आरभेत तस्मान् नेयाद् इति
9.4.m: And they also say: "Hard to reach, as it were, is the higher path; whichever sacrificial rite one undertakes in the beginning, from that he should not depart."
The Sajanīya [hymn] is to be recited; Agastya's Kayāśubhīya [hymn] is to be recited.

9.4.s: asyā amuṣyā adyaśvān mithunād ahorātrābhyām evainān nirbhajati
9.4.d: अस्या अमुष्या अद्यश्वान् मिथुनाद् अहोरात्राभ्याम् एवैनान् निर्भजति
9.4.m: From this [world], from yonder [world], from today and tomorrow, from the pair, by the day and night indeed he excludes them.

9.5.s: yadi somam akrītam apahareyur anyaḥ kretavyaḥ
9.5.d: यदि सोमम् अक्रीतम् अपहरेयुर् अन्यः क्रेतव्यः
9.5.m: If they should steal the unbought Soma, another [plant] should be bought.

9.5.s: yadi krītaṃ yo 'nyo 'bhyāśaṃ syāt sa āhṛtyaḥ somavikrayaṇe tu kiṃ cid dadyāt
9.5.d: यदि क्रीतं यो ऽन्यो ऽभ्याशं स्यात् स आहृत्यः सोमविक्रयणे तु किं चिद् दद्यात्
9.5.m: If [stolen when] bought, whatever other [Soma] might be at hand should be brought; but he should give something to the Soma-seller.

9.5.s: yadi somaṃ na vindeyuḥ pūtīkān abhiṣuṇuyur yadi na pūtīkān arjjunāni
9.5.d: यदि सोमं न विन्देयुः पूतीकान् अभिषुणुयुर् यदि न पूतीकान् अर्ज्जुनानि
9.5.m: If they should not find Soma, they should press pūtīka plants; if not pūtīka plants, brown [phālguna] plants.

9.5.s: gāyatrī somam āharat tasyā anu visṛjya somarakṣiḥ parṇam acchinat tasya yo 'ṃśuḥ parāpatat sa pūtīko 'bhavat tasmin devā ūtim avindann ūtīko vā eṣa yat pūtīkān abhiṣuṇvanty ūtim evāsmai vindanti
9.5.d: गायत्री सोमम् आहरत् तस्या अनु विसृज्य सोमरक्षिः पर्णम् अच्छिनत् तस्य यो ऽंशुः परापतत् स पूतीको ऽभवत् तस्मिन् देवा ऊतिम् अविन्दन्न् ऊतीको वा एष यत् पूतीकान् अभिषुण्वन्त्य् ऊतिम् एवास्मै विन्दन्ति
9.5.m: The Gāyatrī brought Soma. Having shot after her, the Soma-guardian cut off a feather of hers. Whichever shoot of it flew away, that became the pūtīka. In it the gods found help (ūti); this is indeed an "ūtīka" (help-plant). When they press pūtīka plants, they find help for him.

9.5.s: pratidhuk ca prātaḥ pūtīkāś ca śṛtaṃ ca madhyandine pūtīkāś ca dadhi cāparāhṇe pūtīkāś ca
9.5.d: प्रतिधुक् च प्रातः पूतीकाश् च शृतं च मध्यन्दिने पूतीकाश् च दधि चापराह्णे पूतीकाश् च
9.5.m: Freshly milked milk and pūtīka plants in the morning, boiled milk and pūtīka plants at midday, and curd and pūtīka plants in the afternoon.

9.5.s: somapītho vā etasmād apakrāmatīty āhur yasya somam apaharantīti sa oṣadhīś ca paśūṃś ca praviśati tam oṣadhibhyaś ca paśubhyaś cāvarundhe
9.5.d: सोमपीथो वा एतस्माद् अपक्रामतीत्य् आहुर् यस्य सोमम् अपहरन्तीति स ओषधीश् च पशूंश् च प्रविशति तम् ओषधिभ्यश् च पशुभ्यश् चावरुन्धे
9.5.m: "The draught of Soma departs from him whose Soma they steal," they say. It enters into the plants and cattle; he secures it from the plants and cattle.

9.5.s: indro vṛtram ahaṃs tasya yo nastaḥ somaḥ samadhāvat tāni babhrutūlāny arjunāni yo vapāyā utkhinnāyās tāni lohitatūlāni yāni babhrutūlāny arjunāni tāny abhiṣuṇuyād etad vai brahmaṇo rūpaṃ sākṣād eva somam abhiṣuṇoti
9.5.d: इन्द्रो वृत्रम् अहंस् तस्य यो नस्तः सोमः समधावत् तानि बभ्रुतूलान्य् अर्जुनानि यो वपाया उत्खिन्नायास् तानि लोहिततूलानि यानि बभ्रुतूलान्य् अर्जुनानि तान्य् अभिषुणुयाद् एतद् वै ब्रह्मणो रूपं साक्षाद् एव सोमम् अभिषुणोति
9.5.m: Indra slew Vṛtra. The Soma which flowed together from his nostrils became brown-tufted arjuna plants; that from his ruptured caul became red-tufted [plants]. Those which are brown-tufted arjuna plants he should press. That is the form of brahman; directly indeed he presses Soma.

9.5.s: śrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma kāryaṃ sad evainaṃ karoti
9.5.d: श्रायन्तीयं ब्रह्मसाम कार्यं सद् एवैनं करोति
9.5.m: The Śrāyantīya should be made the Brahmasāman; it makes him real.

9.5.s: yajñāyajñīyam anuṣṭubhi prohed vācaivainaṃ samardhayati vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kāryam indriyasya vīryasya parigṛhītyai
9.5.d: यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अनुष्टुभि प्रोहेद् वाचैवैनं समर्धयति वारवन्तीयम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कार्यम् इन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्य परिगृहीत्यै
9.5.m: He should weave the Yajñāyajñīya into the anuṣṭubh; he strengthens it with speech. The Vāravantīya should be made the Agniṣṭomasāman, for securing vital power and manly strength.

9.5.s: pāṅkto yajño yāvān yajñas tam evārabhate
9.5.d: पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यावान् यज्ञस् तम् एवारभते
9.5.m: Fivefold is the sacrifice; as great as the sacrifice is, of that he takes hold.
Having emerged from the purifying bath, he should be consecrated again.

9.5.s: tatra tad dadyād yad dāsyaṃ syāt
9.5.d: तत्र तद् दद्याद् यद् दास्यं स्यात्
9.5.m: Then he should give whatever was to be given.

9.6.s: yadi kalaśo dīryeta vaṣaṭkāraṇidhanaṃ brahmasāma kuryāt
9.6.d: यदि कलशो दीर्येत वषट्कारणिधनं ब्रह्मसाम कुर्यात्
9.6.m: If the jar should burst, he should make the Brahmasāman have the vaṣaṭ-call as cadence.

9.6.s: avaṣaṭkṛto vā etasya somaḥ parāsicyate yasya kalaśo dīryate yad vaṣaṭkāraṇīdhanaṃ brahmasāma bhavati vaṣaṭkṛta evāsya somo bhavati
9.6.d: अवषट्कृतो वा एतस्य सोमः परासिच्यते यस्य कलशो दीर्यते यद् वषट्कारणीधनं ब्रह्मसाम भवति वषट्कृत एवास्य सोमो भवति
9.6.m: Without the vaṣaṭ-call having been uttered, his Soma is poured away, whose jar bursts. When the Brahmasāman has the vaṣaṭ-call as cadence, his Soma is indeed provided with the vaṣaṭ-call.

9.6.s: vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ samane bahūnām ity etāsu kāryam
9.6.d: विधुं दद्राणं समने बहूनाम् इत्य् एतासु कार्यम्
9.6.m: It should be performed on these [verses]: "Running alone in the assembly of many..."

9.6.s: eṣa hi bahūnāṃ samane dīryate yat kalaśaḥ
9.6.d: एष हि बहूनां समने दीर्यते यत् कलशः
9.6.m: For it is in the assembly of many that this jar bursts.

9.6.s: tad āhur na vā ārtyārtir anūdyārtyā vā eṣa ārtim anuvadati yaḥ kalaśo dīrṇe dadrāṇavatīṣu karotīti
9.6.d: तद् आहुर् न वा आर्त्यार्तिर् अनूद्यार्त्या वा एष आर्तिम् अनुवदति यः कलशो दीर्णे दद्राणवतीषु करोतीति
9.6.m: Concerning this they say: "Distress is not to be repeated after distress; he speaks after distress with distress, who performs on [verses] containing 'running' when the jar has burst."
The Śrāyantīya alone should be performed.

9.6.s: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata sa dugdho riricāno 'manyata sa etac chrāyantīyam apaśyat tenātmānaṃ samaśrīṇāt prajayā paśubhir indriyeṇa
9.6.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत स दुग्धो रिरिचानो ऽमन्यत स एतच् छ्रायन्तीयम् अपश्यत् तेनात्मानं समश्रीणात् प्रजया पशुभिर् इन्द्रियेण
9.6.m: Prajāpati created creatures. Being milked out, he felt emptied. He saw this Śrāyantīya; by it he restored himself with offspring, cattle, and vital power.

9.6.s: dugdha iva eṣa riricāno yasya kalaśo dīryate yac chrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma bhavati punar evātmānaṃ saṃśrīṇāti prajayā paśubhir indriyeṇa
9.6.d: दुग्ध इव एष रिरिचानो यस्य कलशो दीर्यते यच् छ्रायन्तीयं ब्रह्मसाम भवति पुनर् एवात्मानं संश्रीणाति प्रजया पशुभिर् इन्द्रियेण
9.6.m: Milked out as it were, emptied is he whose jar bursts. When the Brahmasāman is the Śrāyantīya, he restores himself again with offspring, cattle, and vital power.

9.6.s: yadi śrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma syād vaiṣṇavīṣv anuṣṭupsu vaṣaṭkāraṇidhanaṃ kuryāt
9.6.d: यदि श्रायन्तीयं ब्रह्मसाम स्याद् वैष्णवीष्व् अनुष्टुप्सु वषट्कारणिधनं कुर्यात्
9.6.m: If the Brahmasāman should be the Śrāyantīya, he should make it have the vaṣaṭ-call as cadence on Vaiṣṇava anuṣṭubh verses.

9.6.s: yad vai yajñasya sravati vācaṃ pratisravati vāg anuṣṭup yajño viṣṇur vācaiva yajñasya cchidram apidadhāti
9.6.d: यद् वै यज्ञस्य स्रवति वाचं प्रतिस्रवति वाग् अनुष्टुप् यज्ञो विष्णुर् वाचैव यज्ञस्य च्छिद्रम् अपिदधाति
9.6.m: Whatever of the sacrifice leaks, leaks toward speech; speech is the anuṣṭubh, Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; with speech he covers the fissure of the sacrifice.

9.6.s: yad vai yajñasya sravaty antataḥ sravati vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kāryaṃ yajñasyaiva cchidraṃ vārayate
9.6.d: यद् वै यज्ञस्य स्रवत्य् अन्ततः स्रवति वारवन्तीयम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कार्यं यज्ञस्यैव च्छिद्रं वारयते
9.6.m: Whatever of the sacrifice leaks, leaks at the end. The Vāravantīya should be made the Agniṣṭomasāman; he wards off the fissure of the sacrifice.

9.7.s: yadi prātassavanāt somo 'tiricyeta asti somo ayaṃ suta iti marutvatīṣu gāyatreṣu stuyuḥ
9.7.d: यदि प्रातस्सवनात् सोमो ऽतिरिच्येत अस्ति सोमो अयं सुत इति मरुत्वतीषु गायत्रेषु स्तुयुः
9.7.m: If Soma should remain over from the morning pressing, they should chant on Marutvat verses in gāyatrī [metres]: "There is this pressed Soma..."

9.7.s: mādhyandinaṃ vā eṣa savanaṃ nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yaḥ prātassavanād atiricyate tasmān marutvatīṣu stuvanti marutvad dhi mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ tasmād u gāyatrīṣu gāyatraṃ hi prātassavanam
9.7.d: माध्यन्दिनं वा एष सवनं निकामयमानो ऽभ्यतिरिच्यते यः प्रातस्सवनाद् अतिरिच्यते तस्मान् मरुत्वतीषु स्तुवन्ति मरुत्वद् धि माध्यन्दिनं सवनं तस्माद् उ गायत्रीषु गायत्रं हि प्रातस्सवनम्
9.7.m: Desiring the midday pressing, this one is left over, which is left over from the morning pressing. Therefore they chant on Marutvat verses, for the midday pressing is accompanied by the Maruts; and therefore on gāyatrī [verses], for the morning pressing belongs to the gāyatrī.

9.7.s: yasmāt stomād atiricyate sa eva stomaḥ kāryaḥ salomatvāya
9.7.d: यस्मात् स्तोमाद् अतिरिच्यते स एव स्तोमः कार्यः सलोमत्वाय
9.7.m: Whatever stoma it is left over from, that same stoma should be used, for conformity.

9.7.s: vīryaṃ vā indro yajño viṣṇur vīrya eva yajñe pratitiṣṭhati
9.7.d: वीर्यं वा इन्द्रो यज्ञो विष्णुर् वीर्य एव यज्ञे प्रतितिष्ठति
9.7.m: Indra is manly strength, Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; in manly strength, in the sacrifice, he stands firm.

9.7.s: yadi mādhyandināt savanād atiricyeta baṇ mahāṃ asi sūryety ādityavatīṣu gaurīvitena stuyuḥ
9.7.d: यदि माध्यन्दिनात् सवनाद् अतिरिच्येत बण् महां असि सूर्येत्य् आदित्यवतीषु गौरीवितेन स्तुयुः
9.7.m: If it should remain over from the midday pressing, they should chant with the Gaurīvita on verses to the Ādityas: "Truly, great art thou, O Sūrya..."

9.7.s: tṛtīyasavanaṃ vā eṣa nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yo mādhyandināt savanād atiricyate tasmād ādityavatīṣu stuvanty ādityaṃ hi tṛtīyasavanaṃ tasmād u bṛhatīṣu bārhataṃ hi mādhyandinaṃ savanam
9.7.d: तृतीयसवनं वा एष निकामयमानो ऽभ्यतिरिच्यते यो माध्यन्दिनात् सवनाद् अतिरिच्यते तस्माद् आदित्यवतीषु स्तुवन्त्य् आदित्यं हि तृतीयसवनं तस्माद् उ बृहतीषु बार्हतं हि माध्यन्दिनं सवनम्
9.7.m: Desiring the third pressing, this one is left over, which is left over from the midday pressing. Therefore they chant on verses to the Ādityas, for the third pressing belongs to the Ādityas; and therefore on bṛhatī [verses], for the midday pressing belongs to the Bṛhat.

9.7.s: yasmāt stomād atiricyeta sa eva stomaḥ kāryaḥ salomatvāyaindrāvaiṣṇavaṃ hotānuśaṃsati vīryaṃ vā indro yajño viṣṇur vīrya eva yajñe pratitiṣṭhati
9.7.d: यस्मात् स्तोमाद् अतिरिच्येत स एव स्तोमः कार्यः सलोमत्वायैन्द्रावैष्णवं होतानुशंसति वीर्यं वा इन्द्रो यज्ञो विष्णुर् वीर्य एव यज्ञे प्रतितिष्ठति
9.7.m: Whatever stoma it should remain over from, that same stoma should be used, for conformity. The Hotṛ recites after it an Aindrāvaiṣṇava [hymn]. Indra is manly strength, Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; in manly strength, in the sacrifice, he stands firm.

9.7.s: yadi tṛtīyasavanād atiricyeta viṣṇoḥ śipiviṣṭavatīṣu gaurīvitena stuyuḥ
9.7.d: यदि तृतीयसवनाद् अतिरिच्येत विष्णोः शिपिविष्टवतीषु गौरीवितेन स्तुयुः
9.7.m: If it should remain over from the third pressing, they should chant with the Gaurīvita on verses to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.

9.7.s: yajño vai viṣṇuś śipiviṣṭo yajña eva viṣṇau pratitiṣṭhaty atiriktaṃ gaurīvitam atirikta evātiriktaṃ dadhāti
9.7.d: यज्ञो वै विष्णुश् शिपिविष्टो यज्ञ एव विष्णौ प्रतितिष्ठत्य् अतिरिक्तं गौरीवितम् अतिरिक्त एवातिरिक्तं दधाति
9.7.m: Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa is the sacrifice; in the sacrifice, in Viṣṇu, he stands firm. Redundant is the Gaurīvita; in the redundant he places the redundant.

9.7.s: etad anyat kuryur ukthāni praṇayeyur ukthāni vā eṣa nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yo 'gniṣṭomād atiricyate yady ukthyebhyo 'tiricyetātirātraḥ kāryo rātriṃ vā eṣa nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate ya ukthyebhyo 'tiricyate yadi rātrer atiricyeta viṣṇoḥ śipiviṣṭavatīṣu bṛhatā stuyur eṣu tu vā atiricyata ity āhur yo rātrer atiricyata iti
9.7.d: एतद् अन्यत् कुर्युर् उक्थानि प्रणयेयुर् उक्थानि वा एष निकामयमानो ऽभ्यतिरिच्यते यो ऽग्निष्टोमाद् अतिरिच्यते यद्य् उक्थ्येभ्यो ऽतिरिच्येतातिरात्रः कार्यो रात्रिं वा एष निकामयमानो ऽभ्यतिरिच्यते य उक्थ्येभ्यो ऽतिरिच्यते यदि रात्रेर् अतिरिच्येत विष्णोः शिपिविष्टवतीषु बृहता स्तुयुर् एषु तु वा अतिरिच्यत इत्य् आहुर् यो रात्रेर् अतिरिच्यत इति
9.7.m: They should do this otherwise: they should bring forward the uktha [lauds]. Desiring the uktha [lauds], indeed, does he become redundant who is left over from the agniṣṭoma. If he is left over from the ukthya [lauds], an atirātra should be performed; for desiring the night, indeed, does he become redundant who is left over from the ukthya [lauds]. If he is left over from the night [rite], they should chant with the Bṛhat on verses addressed to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa; for they say, 'In these [verses], indeed, he is left over,' who is left over from the night [rite].

9.7.s: amuṃ vā eṣa lokaṃ nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yo rātrer atiricyate bṛhatā stuvanti bṛhad amuṃ lokam āptum arhati tam evāpnoti
9.7.d: अमुं वा एष लोकं निकामयमानो ऽभ्यतिरिच्यते यो रात्रेर् अतिरिच्यते बृहता स्तुवन्ति बृहद् अमुं लोकम् आप्तुम् अर्हति तम् एवाप्नोति
9.7.m: Desiring that world, indeed, does he become redundant who is left over from the night [rite]. They chant with the Bṛhat; the Bṛhat is able to attain that world, and he attains that very [world].

9.8.s: yadi dīkṣitānāṃ pramīyate dagdhvāsthīny upanahya yo nediṣṭhī syāt taṃ dīkṣayitvā saha yajeran
9.8.d: यदि दीक्षितानां प्रमीयते दग्ध्वास्थीन्य् उपनह्य यो नेदिष्ठी स्यात् तं दीक्षयित्वा सह यजेरन्
9.8.m: If one of the consecrated dies, having burned [the body] and tied up the bones, having consecrated him who is nearest [of kin], they should sacrifice together.

9.8.s: etad anyat kuryur abhiṣutyānyat somam agṛhītvā grahān yāsau dakṣiṇā sraktis tad vā stuyur mārjālīye vā
9.8.d: एतद् अन्यत् कुर्युर् अभिषुत्यान्यत् सोमम् अगृहीत्वा ग्रहान् यासौ दक्षिणा स्रक्तिस् तद् वा स्तुयुर् मार्जालीये वा
9.8.m: They should do this otherwise: having pressed other Soma without taking the libation-cups, they should chant either at that southern corner or at the Mārjālīya [hearth].

9.8.s: api vā etasya yajñe yo dīkṣitaḥ pramīyate tam etena niravadayante
9.8.d: अपि वा एतस्य यज्ञे यो दीक्षितः प्रमीयते तम् एतेन निरवदयन्ते
9.8.m: Indeed, him who, being consecrated, dies during his sacrifice, they appease by this.
They chant with the Yāma [sāman]; they make him go to the world of Yama.

9.8.s: tisṛbhiḥ stuvanti tṛtīye hi loke pitaraḥ
9.8.d: तिसृभिः स्तुवन्ति तृतीये हि लोके पितरः
9.8.m: They chant with three [verses], for the Fathers are in the third world.

9.8.d: पराचीभिः स्तुवन्ति पराङ् हीतो ऽसौ लोकः
9.8.m: They chant with non-returning [verses], for that world is turned away from here.
They chant with the verses of the Serpent Queen.

9.8.s: arbudaḥ sarpa etābhir mṛtāṃ tvacam apāhata mṛtām evaitābhis tvacam apaghnate
9.8.d: अर्बुदः सर्प एताभिर् मृतां त्वचम् अपाहत मृताम् एवैताभिस् त्वचम् अपघ्नते
9.8.m: Arbuda the serpent sloughed off his dead skin by means of these [verses]; by means of these they slough off the dead skin.

9.8.s: tā ṛco 'nubruvantas trir mārjālīyaṃ pariyanti savyān ūrūn āghnānāḥ
9.8.d: ता ऋचो ऽनुब्रुवन्तस् त्रिर् मार्जालीयं परियन्ति सव्यान् ऊरून् आघ्नानाः
9.8.m: Reciting these verses, beating their left thighs, they go thrice around the Mārjālīya [hearth].

9.8.s: stutam anuśaṃsaty amuṣminn evainaṃ loke nidhnuvanti
9.8.d: स्तुतम् अनुशंसत्य् अमुष्मिन्न् एवैनं लोके निध्नुवन्ति
9.8.m: He recites after the chant of praise; in that world they lay him down.

9.8.s: yanti vā ete patha ity āhur ye mṛtāya kurvantīty aindravāyavāgrān grahān gṛhṇate punaḥ panthānam apiyanti
9.8.d: यन्ति वा एते पथ इत्य् आहुर् ये मृताय कुर्वन्तीत्य् ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रान् ग्रहान् गृह्णते पुनः पन्थानम् अपियन्ति
9.8.m: They say, 'Departing from the path are those who perform [rites] for the dead.' They take the libation-cups beginning with that for Indra and Vāyu; they return to the path.

9.8.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti pratipatkāryā ya eva jīvanti teṣv āyur dadhāti
9.8.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवस इति प्रतिपत्कार्या य एव जीवन्ति तेष्व् आयुर् दधाति
9.8.m: 'O Agni, you purify life-spans' is to be made the introductory verse; in those who are alive he bestows life.

9.8.s: saṃvatsare 'sthīni yājayeyuḥ saṃvvatsaro vai sarvasya śāntir yat purā saṃvvatsarād yājayeyur vācam aruṣkṛtāṃ krūrām ṛccheyuḥ
9.8.d: संवत्सरे ऽस्थीनि याजयेयुः संव्वत्सरो वै सर्वस्य शान्तिर् यत् पुरा संव्वत्सराद् याजयेयुर् वाचम् अरुष्कृतां क्रूराम् ऋच्छेयुः
9.8.m: After a year they should cause the bones to sacrifice; the year is indeed the pacification of everything. If they were to cause [them] to sacrifice before a year, they would meet with wounded, cruel speech.

9.8.s: vṛtaḥ pavamānāḥ syuḥ saptadaśam itarat sarvam
9.8.d: वृतः पवमानाः स्युः सप्तदशम् इतरत् सर्वम्
9.8.m: The Pavamāna [stotras] should be ninefold; all the rest seventeenfold.

9.8.s: yat trivṛtaḥ pavamānā bhavanti prāṇā vai trivṛt prāṇān evopayanti yat saptadaśam itarat sarvaṃ prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajatim evopayanti
9.8.d: यत् त्रिवृतः पवमाना भवन्ति प्राणा वै त्रिवृत् प्राणान् एवोपयन्ति यत् सप्तदशम् इतरत् सर्वं प्रजापतिर् वै सप्तदशः प्रजतिम् एवोपयन्ति
9.8.m: In that the Pavamāna [stotras] are ninefold, the vital breaths are indeed ninefold; they obtain the vital breaths. In that all the rest is seventeenfold, Prajāpati is seventeenfold; they obtain procreation.

9.8.s: prāṇāpānair vā ete vyṛdhyanta ity āhur ye mṛtāya kurvantīti maitrāvaruṇāgrān grahān gṛhṇate prāṇāpānau mitrāvaruṇau prāṇāpānair eva samṛdhyante
9.8.d: प्राणापानैर् वा एते व्यृध्यन्त इत्य् आहुर् ये मृताय कुर्वन्तीति मैत्रावरुणाग्रान् ग्रहान् गृह्णते प्राणापानौ मित्रावरुणौ प्राणापानैर् एव समृध्यन्ते
9.8.m: They say, 'Deprived of in-breath and out-breath are those who perform [rites] for the dead.' They draw the libation-cups beginning with that for Mitra and Varuṇa; Mitra and Varuṇa are in-breath and out-breath; they prosper with in-breath and out-breath.

9.9.s: yasya kalaśa upadasyati kalaśam evāsyopadasyantaṃ prāṇo 'nūpadasyati prāṇo hi somaḥ
